types.name: packet.ActorEvent
types.doc:
ActorEvent is sent by the server when a particular event happens that has to do with an entity. Some of
these events are entity-specific, for example a wolf shaking itself dry, but others are used for each
entity, such as dying.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: EventType
fields.doc: EventType is the ID of the event to be called. It is one of the constants that can be found above.

fields.name: EventData
fields.doc:
EventData is optional data associated with a particular event. The data has a different function for
different events, however most events don't use this field at all.

fields.name: FireAtPosition
fields.doc:
FireAtPosition is the position in the same world at which the event should fire. If this is not present,
the position entity will be used instead.

types.name: packet.ActorPickRequest
types.doc:
ActorPickRequest is sent by the client when it tries to pick an entity, so that it gets a spawn egg which
can spawn that entity.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity that was attempted to be picked. The server must find the
type of that entity and provide the correct spawn egg to the player.

fields.name: HotBarSlot
fields.doc:
HotBarSlot is the held hot bar slot of the player at the time of trying to pick the entity. If empty,
the resulting spawn egg should be put into this slot.

fields.name: WithData
fields.doc: WithData is true if the pick request requests the entity metadata.

types.name: packet.AddActor
types.doc:
AddActor is sent by the server to the client to spawn an entity to the player. It is used for every entity
except other players, for which the AddPlayer packet is used.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: EntityType
fields.doc:
EntityType is the string entity type of the entity, for example 'minecraft:skeleton'. A list of these
entities may be found online.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position to spawn the entity on. If the entity is on a distance that the player cannot
see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

fields.name: Velocity
fields.doc:
Velocity is the initial velocity the entity spawns with. This velocity will initiate client side
movement of the entity.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc:
Pitch is the vertical rotation of the entity. Facing straight forward yields a pitch of 0. Pitch is
measured in degrees.

fields.name: Yaw
fields.doc: Yaw is the horizontal rotation of the entity. Yaw is also measured in degrees.

fields.name: HeadYaw
fields.doc:
HeadYaw is the same as Yaw, except that it applies specifically to the head of the entity. A different value for
HeadYaw than Yaw means that the entity will have its head turned.

fields.name: BodyYaw
fields.doc:
BodyYaw is the same as Yaw, except that it applies specifically to the body of the entity. A different value for
BodyYaw than HeadYaw means that the entity will have its body turned, although it is unclear what the difference
between BodyYaw and Yaw is.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes is a slice of attributes that the entity has. It includes attributes such as its health,
movement speed, etc.

fields.name: EntityMetadata
fields.doc:
EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in
particular the way the entity looks. Flags include ones such as 'on fire' and 'sprinting'.
The metadata values are indexed by their property key.

fields.name: EntityProperties
fields.doc:
EntityProperties is a list of properties that the entity inhibits. These properties define and alter specific
attributes of the entity.

fields.name: EntityLinks
fields.doc:
EntityLinks is a list of entity links that are currently active on the entity. These links alter the
way the entity shows up when first spawned in terms of it shown as riding an entity. Setting these
links is important for new viewers to see the entity is riding another entity.

types.name: packet.AddBehaviourTree
types.doc:
AddBehaviourTree is sent by the server to the client. The packet is currently unused by both client and
server.

fields.name: BehaviourTree
fields.doc: BehaviourTree is an unused string.

types.name: packet.AddItemActor
types.doc:
AddItemActor is sent by the server to the client to make an item entity show up. It is one of the few
entities that cannot be sent using the AddActor packet

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Item
fields.doc:
Item is the item that is spawned. It must have a valid ID for it to show up client-side. If it is not
a valid item, the client will crash when coming near.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position to spawn the entity on. If the entity is on a distance that the player cannot
see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

fields.name: Velocity
fields.doc:
Velocity is the initial velocity the entity spawns with. This velocity will initiate client side
movement of the entity.

fields.name: EntityMetadata
fields.doc:
EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in
particular the way the entity looks. Flags include ones such as 'on fire' and 'sprinting'.
The metadata values are indexed by their property key.

fields.name: FromFishing
fields.doc:
FromFishing specifies if the item was obtained by fishing it up using a fishing rod. It is not clear
why the client needs to know this.

types.name: packet.AddPainting
types.doc:
AddPainting is sent by the server to the client to make a painting entity show up. It is one of the few
entities that cannot be sent using the AddActor packet.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position to spawn the entity on. If the entity is on a distance that the player cannot
see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

fields.name: Direction
fields.doc: Direction is the facing direction of the painting.

fields.name: Title
fields.doc:
Title is the title of the painting. It specifies the motive of the painting. The title of the painting
must be valid.

types.name: packet.AddPlayer
types.doc:
AddPlayer is sent by the server to the client to make a player entity show up client-side. It is one of the
few entities that cannot be sent using the AddActor packet.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc:
UUID is the UUID of the player. It is the same UUID that the client sent in the Login packet at the
start of the session. A player with this UUID must exist in the player list (built up using the
PlayerList packet), for it to show up in-game.

fields.name: Username
fields.doc:
Username is the name of the player. This username is the username that will be set as the initial
name tag of the player.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: PlatformChatID
fields.doc:
PlatformChatID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when chatting (presumably only for
Nintendo Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to
chat with each other.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position to spawn the player on. If the player is on a distance that the viewer cannot
see it, the player will still show up if the viewer moves closer.

fields.name: Velocity
fields.doc:
Velocity is the initial velocity the player spawns with. This velocity will initiate client side
movement of the player.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc:
Pitch is the vertical rotation of the player. Facing straight forward yields a pitch of 0. Pitch is
measured in degrees.

fields.name: Yaw
fields.doc: Yaw is the horizontal rotation of the player. Yaw is also measured in degrees.

fields.name: HeadYaw
fields.doc:
HeadYaw is the same as Yaw, except that it applies specifically to the head of the player. A different
value for HeadYaw than Yaw means that the player will have its head turned.

fields.name: HeldItem
fields.doc:
HeldItem is the item that the player is holding. The item is shown to the viewer as soon as the player
itself shows up. Needless to say that this field is rather pointless, as additional packets still must
be sent for armour to show up.

fields.name: GameType
fields.doc: GameType is the game type of the player. If set to GameTypeSpectator, the player will not be shown to viewers.

fields.name: EntityMetadata
fields.doc:
EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in
particular the way the player looks. Flags include ones such as 'on fire' and 'sprinting'.
The metadata values are indexed by their property key.

fields.name: EntityProperties
fields.doc:
EntityProperties is a list of properties that the entity inhibits. These properties define and alter specific
attributes of the entity.

fields.name: AbilityData
fields.doc: AbilityData represents various data about the abilities of a player, such as ability layers or permissions.

fields.name: EntityLinks
fields.doc:
EntityLinks is a list of entity links that are currently active on the player. These links alter the
way the player shows up when first spawned in terms of it shown as riding an entity. Setting these
links is important for new viewers to see the player is riding another entity.

fields.name: DeviceID
fields.doc:
DeviceID is the device ID set in one of the files found in the storage of the device of the player. It
may be changed freely, so it should not be relied on for anything.

fields.name: BuildPlatform
fields.doc:
BuildPlatform is the build platform/device OS of the player that is about to be added, as it sent in
the Login packet when joining.

types.name: packet.AddVolumeEntity
types.doc: AddVolumeEntity sends a volume entity's definition and metadata from server to client.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the volume. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: EntityMetadata
fields.doc:
EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in
particular the way the volume functions or looks.

fields.name: EncodingIdentifier
fields.doc:
EncodingIdentifier is the unique identifier for the volume. It must be of the form 'namespace:name', where
namespace cannot be 'minecraft'.

fields.name: InstanceIdentifier
fields.doc: InstanceIdentifier is the identifier of a fog definition.

fields.name: Bounds
fields.doc:
Bounds represent the volume's bounds. The first value is the minimum bounds, and the second value is the
maximum bounds.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc: Dimension is the dimension in which the volume exists.

fields.name: EngineVersion
fields.doc: EngineVersion is the engine version the entity is using, for example, '1.17.0'.

types.name: packet.AdventureSettings
types.doc:
AdventureSettings is sent by the server to update game-play related features, in particular permissions to
access these features for the client. It includes allowing the player to fly, build and mine, and attack
entities. Most of these flags should be checked server-side instead of using this packet only.
The client may also send this packet to the server when it updates one of these settings through the
in-game settings interface. The server should verify if the player actually has permission to update those
settings.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
Flags is a set of flags that specify certain properties of the player, such as whether or not it can
fly and/or move through blocks. It is one of the AdventureFlag constants above.

fields.name: CommandPermissionLevel
fields.doc:
CommandPermissionLevel is a permission level that specifies the kind of commands that the player is
allowed to use. It is one of the CommandPermissionLevel constants above.

fields.name: ActionPermissions
fields.doc:
ActionPermissions is, much like Flags, a set of flags that specify actions that the player is allowed
to undertake, such as whether it is allowed to edit blocks, open doors etc. It is a combination of the
ActionPermission constants above.

fields.name: PermissionLevel
fields.doc:
PermissionLevel is the permission level of the player as it shows up in the player list built up using
the PlayerList packet. It is one of the PermissionLevel constants above.

fields.name: CustomStoredPermissions
fields.doc: CustomStoredPermissions ...

fields.name: PlayerUniqueID
fields.doc:
PlayerUniqueID is a unique identifier of the player. This must be filled out with the entity unique ID of the
player.

types.name: packet.AgentAction
types.doc:
AgentAction is an Education Edition packet sent from the server to the client to return a response to a
previously requested action.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.doc: Identifier is a JSON identifier referenced in the initial action.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action represents the action type that was requested. It is one of the constants defined above.

fields.name: Response
fields.doc: Response is a JSON string containing the response to the action.

types.name: packet.AgentAnimation
types.doc: AgentAnimation is an Education Edition packet sent from the server to the client to make an agent perform an animation.

fields.name: Animation
fields.doc:
Animation is the ID of the animation that the agent should perform. As of its implementation, there are no IDs
that can be used in the regular client.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

types.name: packet.Animate
types.doc:
Animate is sent by the server to send a player animation from one player to all viewers of that player. It
is used for a couple of actions, such as arm swimming and critical hits.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the ID of the animation action to execute. It is one of the action type constants that
may be found above.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player that the animation should be played upon. The runtime
ID is unique for each world session, and entities are generally identified in packets using this
runtime ID.

fields.name: Data
fields.doc: Data ...

fields.name: SwingSource
fields.doc:
SwingSource is the source for swing actions. It is one of the action type constants that
may be found above.

types.name: packet.AnimateEntity
types.doc:
AnimateEntity is sent by the server to animate an entity client-side. It may be used to play a single
animation, or to activate a controller which can start a sequence of animations based on different
conditions specified in an animation controller.
Much of the documentation of this packet can be found at
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/minecraft/creator/reference/content/animationsreference

fields.name: Animation
fields.doc: Animation is the name of a single animation to start playing.

fields.name: NextState
fields.doc:
NextState is the first state to start with. These states are declared in animation controllers (which,
in themselves, are animations too). These states in turn may have animations and transitions to move to
a next state.

fields.name: StopCondition
fields.doc: StopCondition is a MoLang expression that specifies when the animation should be stopped.

fields.name: StopConditionVersion
fields.doc: StopConditionVersion is the MoLang stop condition version.

fields.name: Controller
fields.doc:
Controller is the animation controller that is used to manage animations. These controllers decide when
to play which animation.

fields.name: BlendOutTime
fields.doc: BlendOutTime does not currently seem to be used.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeIDs
fields.doc: EntityRuntimeIDs is list of runtime IDs of entities that the animation should be applied to.

types.name: packet.AnvilDamage
types.doc:
AnvilDamage is sent by the client to request the dealing damage to an anvil. This packet is completely
pointless and the server should never listen to it.

fields.name: AnvilPosition
fields.doc: AnvilPosition is the position in the world that the anvil can be found at.

types.name: packet.AutomationClientConnect
types.doc:
AutomationClientConnect is used to make the client connect to a websocket server. This websocket server has
the ability to execute commands on the behalf of the client and it can listen for certain events fired by
the client.

fields.name: ServerURI
fields.doc:
ServerURI is the URI to make the client connect to. It can be, for example, 'localhost:8000/ws' to
connect to a websocket server on the localhost at port 8000.

types.name: packet.AvailableActorIdentifiers
types.doc:
AvailableActorIdentifiers is sent by the server at the start of the game to let the client know all
entities that are available on the server.

fields.name: SerialisedEntityIdentifiers
fields.doc:
SerialisedEntityIdentifiers is a network NBT serialised compound of all entity identifiers that are
available in the server.

types.name: packet.AvailableCommands
types.doc:
AvailableCommands is sent by the server to send a list of all commands that
the player is able to use on the server. This packet holds all the arguments
of each commands as well, making it possible for the client to provide
auto-completion and command usages. AvailableCommands packets can be resent,
but the packet is often very big, so doing this very often should be avoided.

fields.name: EnumValues
fields.doc:
EnumValues is a slice of all enum values of any enum in the
AvailableCommands packet. EnumValues generally should contain each
possible value only once. Enums are built by pointing to entries in this
slice.

fields.name: ChainedSubcommandValues
fields.doc:
ChainedSubcommandValues is a slice of all chained subcommand names. ChainedSubcommandValues generally should
contain each possible value only once. ChainedSubcommands are built by pointing to entries in this slice.

fields.name: Suffixes
fields.doc:
Suffixes, like EnumValues, is a slice of all suffix values of any command
parameter in the AvailableCommands packet.

fields.name: Enums
fields.doc:
Enums is a slice of all (fixed) command enums present in any of the
commands.

fields.name: ChainedSubcommands
fields.doc:
ChainedSubcommands is a slice of all subcommands that are followed by a chained command. An example usage of this
is /execute which allows you to run another command as another entity or at a different position etc.

fields.name: Commands
fields.doc:
Commands is a list of all commands that the client should show
client-side. The AvailableCommands packet replaces any commands sent
before. It does not only add the commands that are sent in it.

fields.name: DynamicEnums
fields.doc:
DynamicEnums is a slice of dynamic command enums. These command enums can
be changed during runtime without having to resend an AvailableCommands
packet.

fields.name: Constraints
fields.doc:
Constraints is a list of constraints that should be applied to certain
options of enums in the commands above.

types.name: packet.AwardAchievement
types.doc: AwardAchievement is sent by the server to award an achievement to a player.

fields.name: AchievementID
fields.doc:
AchievementID is the ID of the achievement that should be awarded to the player. The values for these
IDs are currently unknown.

types.name: packet.BiomeDefinitionList
types.doc:
BiomeDefinitionList is sent by the server to let the client know all biomes that are available and
implemented on the server side. When enabled, it also includes information for the client to
accurately recreate the server-side generation in vanilla worlds/servers for increased performance.

fields.name: BiomeDefinitions
fields.doc: BiomeDefinitions is a list of biomes that are available on the server.

fields.name: StringList
fields.doc:
StringList is a makeshift dictionary implementation Mojang created to try and reduce the size of the
overall packet. It is a list of common strings that are used in the biome definitions, such as
biome names, float values or query expressions.

types.name: packet.BlockActorData
types.doc:
BlockActorData is sent by the server to update data of a block entity client-side, for example the data of
a chest.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the block that holds the block entity. If no block entity is at this
position, the packet is ignored by the client.

fields.name: NBTData
fields.doc:
NBTData is the new data of the block that will be encoded to NBT and applied client-side, so that the
client can see the block update. The NBTData should contain all properties of the block, not just
properties that were changed.

types.name: packet.BlockEvent
types.doc:
BlockEvent is sent by the server to initiate a certain event that has something to do with blocks in
specific, for example opening a chest.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position of the block that an event occurred at.

fields.name: EventType
fields.doc:
EventType is the type of the block event. The event type decides the way the event data that follows
is used. It is one of the constants found above.

fields.name: EventData
fields.doc:
EventData holds event type specific data. For chests for example, opening the chest means the data must
hold 1, whereas closing it should hold 0.

types.name: packet.BlockPickRequest
types.doc:
BlockPickRequest is sent by the client when it requests to pick a block in the world and place its item in
their inventory.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position at which the client requested to pick the block. The block at that position
should have its item put in HotBarSlot if it is empty.

fields.name: AddBlockNBT
fields.doc:
AddBlockNBT specifies if the item should get all NBT tags from the block, meaning the item places a
block practically always equal to the one picked.

fields.name: HotBarSlot
fields.doc: HotBarSlot is the slot that was held at the time of picking a block.

types.name: packet.BookEdit
types.doc:
BookEdit is sent by the client when it edits a book. It is sent each time a modification was made and the
player stops its typing 'session', rather than simply after closing the book.

fields.name: InventorySlot
fields.doc:
InventorySlot is the slot in which the book that was edited may be found. Typically, the server should
check if this slot matches the held item slot of the player.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the book edit action. The data obtained depends on what type this is. The
action type is one of the constants above.

fields.name: PageNumber
fields.doc:
PageNumber is the number of the page that the book edit action concerns. It applies for all actions
but the BookActionSign. In BookActionSwapPages, it is one of the pages that was swapped.

fields.name: SecondaryPageNumber
fields.doc:
SecondaryPageNumber is the page number of the second page that the action concerned. It is only set for
the BookActionSwapPages action, in which case it is the other page that is swapped.

fields.name: Text
fields.doc:
Text is the text that was written in a particular page of the book. It applies for the
BookActionAddPage and BookActionReplacePage only.

fields.name: PhotoName
fields.doc:
PhotoName is the name of the photo on the page in the book. It applies for the BookActionAddPage and
BookActionReplacePage only.
Unfortunately, the functionality of this field was removed from the default Minecraft Bedrock Edition.
It is still available on Education Edition.

fields.name: Title
fields.doc: Title is the title that the player has given the book. It applies only for the BookActionSign action.

fields.name: Author
fields.doc:
Author is the author that the player has given the book. It applies only for the BookActionSign action.
Note that the author may be freely changed, so no assumptions can be made on if the author is actually
the name of a player.

fields.name: XUID
fields.doc:
XUID is the XBOX Live User ID of the player that edited the book. The field is rather pointless, as the
server is already aware of the XUID of the player anyway.

types.name: packet.BossEvent
types.doc:
BossEvent is sent by the server to make a specific 'boss event' occur in the
world. It includes features such as showing a boss bar to the player and
turning the sky dark.

fields.name: BossEntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
BossEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the boss entity that the boss
event sent involves. By default, the health percentage and title of the
boss bar depend on the health and name tag of this entity. If
BossEntityUniqueID is the same as the client's entity unique ID, its
HealthPercentage and BossBarTitle can be freely altered.

fields.name: EventType
fields.doc: EventType is the type of the event. It is one of the BossEvent constants above.

fields.name: BossBarTitle
fields.doc:
BossBarTitle is the title shown above the boss bar. It may be set to set
a different title if the BossEntityUniqueID matches the client's entity
unique ID.

fields.name: FilteredBossBarTitle
fields.doc:
FilteredBossBarTitle is a filtered version of BossBarTitle with all the
profanity removed. The client will use this over BossBarTitle if this
field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

fields.name: HealthPercentage
fields.doc:
HealthPercentage is the percentage of health that is shown in the boss
bar (0.0-1.0). The HealthPercentage may be set to a specific value if the
BossEntityUniqueID matches the client's entity unique ID.

fields.name: Colour
fields.doc:
Colour is the colour of the boss bar that is shown when a player is
subscribed. It is one of the BossEventColour constants listed above.

fields.name: Overlay
fields.doc:
Overlay is the overlay of the boss bar that is shown on top of the boss
bar when a player is subscribed. It is one of the BossEventOverlay
constants listed above.

types.name: packet.Camera
types.doc:
Camera is sent by the server to use an Education Edition camera on a player. It produces an image
client-side.

fields.name: CameraEntityUniqueID
fields.doc: CameraEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the camera entity from which the picture was taken.

fields.name: TargetPlayerUniqueID
fields.doc:
TargetPlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the target player. The unique ID is a value that remains
consistent across different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of
the player out for this field.

types.name: packet.CameraAimAssist
types.doc: CameraAimAssist is sent by the server to the client to set up aim assist for the client's camera.

fields.name: Preset
fields.doc: Preset is the ID of the preset that has previously been defined in the CameraAimAssistPresets packet.

fields.name: Angle
fields.doc:
Angle is the maximum angle around the playes's cursor that the aim assist should check for a target,
if TargetMode is set to protocol.AimAssistTargetModeAngle.

fields.name: Distance
fields.doc:
Distance is the maximum distance from the player's cursor should check for a target, if TargetMode is
set to protocol.AimAssistTargetModeDistance.

fields.name: TargetMode
fields.doc:
TargetMode is the mode that the camera should use for detecting targets. This is currently one of
protocol.AimAssistTargetModeAngle or protocol.AimAssistTargetModeDistance.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is the action that should be performed with the aim assist. This is one of the constants above.

fields.name: ShowDebugRender
fields.doc: ShowDebugRender specifies if debug render should be shown.

types.name: packet.CameraAimAssistActorPriority
types.doc: CameraAimAssistActorPriority is sent by the server to define actor-specific aim assist priorities.

fields.name: PriorityData
fields.doc: PriorityData is a list of aim assist actor priority entries.

types.name: packet.CameraAimAssistPresets
types.doc:
CameraAimAssistPresets is sent by the server to the client to provide a list of categories and presets
that can be used when sending a CameraAimAssist packet or a CameraInstruction including aim assist.

fields.name: Categories
fields.doc: Categories is a list of categories which can be referenced by one of the Presets.

fields.name: Presets
fields.doc: Presets is a list of presets which define a base for how aim assist should behave

fields.name: Operation
fields.doc: Operation is the operation to perform with the presets. It is one of the constants above.

types.name: packet.CameraInstruction
types.doc: CameraInstruction gives a custom camera specific instructions to operate.

fields.name: Set
fields.doc: Set is a camera instruction that sets the camera to a specified preset.

fields.name: Clear
fields.doc: Clear can be set to true to clear all the current camera instructions.

fields.name: Fade
fields.doc: Fade is a camera instruction that fades the screen to a specified colour.

fields.name: Target
fields.doc: Target is a camera instruction that targets a specific entity.

fields.name: RemoveTarget
fields.doc: RemoveTarget can be set to true to remove the current aim assist target.

fields.name: FieldOfView
fields.doc: FieldOfView is a camera instruction that updates the field of view for the camera.

fields.name: Spline
fields.doc: Spline is a camera instruction that creates a spline path for the camera to follow.

fields.name: AttachToEntity
fields.doc: AttachToEntity is the entity ID to attach the camera to.

fields.name: DetachFromEntity
fields.doc: DetachFromEntity can be set to true to detach the camera from the current entity.

types.name: packet.CameraPresets
types.doc: CameraPresets gives the client a list of custom camera presets.

fields.name: Presets
fields.doc:
Presets is a list of camera presets that can be used by other cameras. The order of this list is important because
the index of presets is used as a pointer in the CameraInstruction packet.

types.name: packet.CameraShake
types.doc:
CameraShake is sent by the server to make the camera shake client-side. This feature was added for map-
making partners.

fields.name: Intensity
fields.doc:
Intensity is the intensity of the shaking. The client limits this value to 4, so anything higher may
not work.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Duration is the number of seconds the camera will shake for.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc:
Type is the type of shake, and is one of the constants listed above. The different type affects how
the shake looks in game.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc:
Action is the action to be performed, and is one of the constants listed above. Currently the
different actions will either add or stop shaking the client.

types.name: packet.CameraSpline
types.doc: CameraSpline is sent by the server to define camera spline paths.

fields.name: Splines
fields.doc: Splines is a list of camera spline definitions.

types.name: packet.ChangeDimension
types.doc:
ChangeDimension is sent by the server to the client to send a dimension change screen client-side. Once the
screen is cleared client-side, the client will send a PlayerAction packet with
PlayerActionDimensionChangeDone.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc:
Dimension is the dimension that the client should be changed to. The fog colour will change depending
on the type of dimension, which is one of the constants above.
Note that Dimension MUST be a different dimension than the one that the player is currently in. Sending
a ChangeDimension packet with a Dimension that the player is currently in will result in a never-ending
dimension change screen.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position in the new dimension that the player is spawned in.

fields.name: Respawn
fields.doc:
Respawn specifies if the dimension change was respawn based, meaning that the player died in one
dimension and got respawned into another. The client will send a PlayerAction packet with
PlayerActionDimensionChangeRequest if it dies in another dimension, indicating that it needs a
DimensionChange packet with Respawn set to true.

fields.name: LoadingScreenID
fields.doc:
LoadingScreenID is a unique ID for the loading screen that the player is currently in. The client will
update the server on its state through the ServerBoundLoadingScreen packet, and it can be used to not
send specific packets to the client if it is changing dimensions. This field should be unique for every
ChangeDimension packet sent.

types.name: packet.ChangeMobProperty
types.doc: ChangeMobProperty is a packet sent from the server to the client to change one of the properties of a mob client-side.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc: EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity whose property is being changed.

fields.name: Property
fields.doc: Property is the name of the property being updated.

fields.name: BoolValue
fields.doc: BoolValue is set if the property value is a bool type. If the type is not a bool, this field is ignored.

fields.name: StringValue
fields.doc: StringValue is set if the property value is a string type. If the type is not a string, this field is ignored.

fields.name: IntValue
fields.doc: IntValue is set if the property value is an int type. If the type is not an int, this field is ignored.

fields.name: FloatValue
fields.doc: FloatValue is set if the property value is a float type. If the type is not a float, this field is ignored.

types.name: packet.ChunkRadiusUpdated
types.doc:
ChunkRadiusUpdated is sent by the server in response to a RequestChunkRadius packet. It defines the chunk
radius that the server allows the client to have. This may be lower than the chunk radius requested by the
client in the RequestChunkRadius packet.

fields.name: ChunkRadius
fields.doc:
ChunkRadius is the final chunk radius that the client will adapt when it receives the packet. It does
not have to be the same as the requested chunk radius.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundAttributeLayerSync
types.doc: ClientBoundAttributeLayerSync is sent by the server to synchronise attribute layers with the client.

fields.name: PayloadType
fields.doc: PayloadType is the type of attribute layer payload. It is one of the protocol.AttributeLayerPayloadType constants.

fields.name: Layers
fields.doc: Layers is set if PayloadType is AttributeLayerPayloadTypeUpdateLayers.

fields.name: LayerName
fields.doc: LayerName is the attribute layer name, used for UpdateSettings, UpdateEnvironment and RemoveEnvironment.

fields.name: DimensionID
fields.doc: DimensionID is the dimension ID, used for UpdateSettings, UpdateEnvironment and RemoveEnvironment.

fields.name: Settings
fields.doc: Settings is set if PayloadType is AttributeLayerPayloadTypeUpdateSettings.

fields.name: EnvironmentAttributes
fields.doc: EnvironmentAttributes is set if PayloadType is AttributeLayerPayloadTypeUpdateEnvironment.

fields.name: RemoveAttributeNames
fields.doc: RemoveAttributeNames is set if PayloadType is AttributeLayerPayloadTypeRemoveEnvironment.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundCloseForm
types.doc:
ClientBoundCloseForm is sent by the server to clear the entire form stack of the client. This means that all
forms that are currently open will be closed. This does not affect inventories and other containers.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundControlSchemeSet
types.doc:
ClientBoundControlSchemeSet is sent by the server upon the client's request or the usage of the vanilla
/controlscheme command. It is used to set the control scheme of the client, often used in combination with
custom cameras.

fields.name: ControlScheme
fields.doc:
ControlScheme is the control scheme that the client should use. It is one of the following:
 - ControlSchemeLockedPlayerRelativeStrafe is the default behaviour, this cannot be set when the client
   is in a custom camera.
 - ControlSchemeCameraRelative makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's
   rotation being relative to the client's movement.
 - ControlSchemeCameraRelativeStrafe makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the
   client's rotation being locked.
 - ControlSchemePlayerRelative makes movement relative to the player's transform, meaning holding
   left/right will make the player turn in a circle.
 - ControlSchemePlayerRelativeStrafe makes movement the same as the default behaviour, but can be
   used in a custom camera.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundDataDrivenUICloseScreen
types.doc:
ClientBoundDataDrivenUICloseScreen is sent by the server to close a data-driven UI screen on the client.
If FormID is not set, all data-driven UI screens are closed.

fields.name: FormID
fields.doc: FormID is the optional unique instance ID of the form to close. If not set, all forms are closed.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundDataDrivenUIReload
types.doc: ClientBoundDataDrivenUIReload is sent by the server to reload the data-driven UI on the client.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundDataDrivenUIShowScreen
types.doc: ClientBoundDataDrivenUIShowScreen is sent by the server to show a data-driven UI screen on the client.

fields.name: ScreenID
fields.doc: ScreenID is the identifier of the screen to show.

fields.name: FormID
fields.doc: FormID is a unique instance ID for the form, used for scripting to identify specific screen instances.

fields.name: DataInstanceID
fields.doc: DataInstanceID is an optional data ID associated with the screen.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundDataStore
types.doc: ClientBoundDataStore is sent by the server to update, change or remove data store entries on the client.

fields.name: Updates
fields.doc: Updates is an array of data store changes. Each entry has its own change type discriminator.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundDebugRenderer
types.doc: ClientBoundDebugRenderer is sent by the server to spawn an outlined cube on client-side.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the type of action. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: Data
fields.doc:
Data holds the marker data. It is only present when Type is
ClientBoundDebugRendererAddCube.

types.name: packet.ClientBoundMapItemData
types.doc:
ClientBoundMapItemData is sent by the server to the client to update the data of a map shown to the client.
It is sent with a combination of flags that specify what data is updated.
The ClientBoundMapItemData packet may be used to update specific parts of the map only. It is not required
to send the entire map each time when updating one part.

fields.name: MapID
fields.doc:
MapID is the unique identifier that represents the map that is updated over network. It remains
consistent across sessions.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc:
Dimension is the dimension of the map that should be updated, for example the overworld (0), the nether
(1) or the end (2).

fields.name: LockedMap
fields.doc:
LockedMap specifies if the map that was updated was a locked map, which may be done using a cartography
table.

fields.name: Origin
fields.doc: Origin is the center position of the map being updated.

fields.name: Scale
fields.doc: Scale is the scale of the map as it is shown in-game.

fields.name: MapsIncludedIn
fields.doc:
MapsIncludedIn holds an array of map IDs that the map updated is included in. This has to do with the
scale of the map: Each map holds its own map ID and all map IDs of maps that include this map and have
a bigger scale. This means that a scale 0 map will have 5 map IDs in this slice, whereas a scale 4 map
will have only 1 (its own).
The actual use of this field remains unknown.

fields.name: TrackedObjects
fields.doc:
TrackedObjects is a list of tracked objects on the map, which may either be entities or blocks. The
client makes sure these tracked objects are actually tracked. (position updated etc.)

fields.name: Decorations
fields.doc:
Decorations is a list of fixed decorations located on the map. The decorations will not change
client-side, unless the server updates them.

fields.name: Height
fields.doc:
Height is the height of the texture area that was updated. The height may be a subset of the total
height of the map.

fields.name: Width
fields.doc:
Width is the width of the texture area that was updated. The width may be a subset of the total width
of the map.

fields.name: XOffset
fields.doc:
XOffset is the X offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this X, the updated
texture will extend exactly Width pixels to the right.

fields.name: YOffset
fields.doc:
YOffset is the Y offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this Y, the updated
texture will extend exactly Height pixels up.

fields.name: Pixels
fields.doc: Pixels is a list of pixel colours for the new texture of the map. It is indexed as Pixels[y*height + x].

types.name: packet.ClientBoundTextureShift
types.doc: ClientBoundTextureShift is sent by the server to control texture shift animations on the client.

fields.name: ActionID
fields.doc: ActionID is the texture shift action to perform. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: CollectionName
fields.doc: CollectionName is the name of the texture shift collection.

fields.name: FromStep
fields.doc: FromStep is the step to shift from.

fields.name: ToStep
fields.doc: ToStep is the step to shift to.

fields.name: AllSteps
fields.doc: AllSteps is a list of all steps in the texture shift.

fields.name: CurrentLengthTicks
fields.doc: CurrentLengthTicks is the current length of the shift in ticks.

fields.name: TotalLengthTicks
fields.doc: TotalLengthTicks is the total length of the shift in ticks.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.doc: Enabled specifies if the texture shift is enabled.

types.name: packet.ClientCacheBlobStatus
types.doc:
ClientCacheBlobStatus is part of the blob cache protocol. It is sent by the client to let the server know
what blobs it needs and which blobs it already has, in an ACK type system.

fields.name: MissHashes
fields.doc:
MissHashes is a list of blob hashes that the client does not have a blob available for. The server
should send the blobs matching these hashes as soon as possible.

fields.name: HitHashes
fields.doc:
HitHashes is a list of blob hashes that the client has a blob available for. The blobs hashes here mean
that the client already has them: The server does not need to send the blobs anymore.

types.name: packet.ClientCacheMissResponse
types.doc:
ClientCacheMissResponse is part of the blob cache protocol. It is sent by the server in response to a
ClientCacheBlobStatus packet and contains the blob data of all blobs that the client acknowledged not to
have yet.

fields.name: Blobs
fields.doc:
Blobs is a list of all blobs that the client sent misses for in the ClientCacheBlobStatus. These blobs
hold the data of the blobs with the hashes they are matched with.

types.name: packet.ClientCacheStatus
types.doc:
ClientCacheStatus is sent by the client to the server at the start of the game. It is sent to let the
server know if it supports the client-side blob cache. Clients such as Nintendo Switch do not support the
cache, and attempting to use it anyway will fail.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.doc:
Enabled specifies if the blob cache is enabled. If false, the server should not attempt to use the
blob cache. If true, it may do so, but it may also choose not to use it.

types.name: packet.ClientCameraAimAssist
types.doc:
ClientCameraAimAssist is sent by the server to send a player animation from one player to all viewers of that player. It
is used for a couple of actions, such as arm swimming and critical hits.

fields.name: PresetID
fields.doc:
PresetID is the identifier of the preset to use which was previously defined in the CameraAimAssistPresets
packet.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is the action to perform with the aim assist. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: AllowAimAssist
fields.doc: AllowAimAssist specifies the client can use aim assist or not.

types.name: packet.ClientCheatAbility
types.doc:
ClientCheatAbility functions the same as UpdateAbilities. It is unclear why these two were separated.

Deprecated: ClientCheatAbility is deprecated as of 1.20.10.

fields.name: AbilityData
fields.doc: AbilityData represents various data about the abilities of a player, such as ability layers or permissions.

types.name: packet.ClientMovementPredictionSync
types.doc:
ClientMovementPredictionSync is sent by the client to the server periodically if the client has received
movement corrections from the server, containing information about client-predictions that are relevant
to movement.

fields.name: ActorFlags
fields.doc: ActorFlags is a bitset of all the flags that are currently set for the client.

fields.name: BoundingBoxScale
fields.doc: BoundingBoxScale is the scale of the client's bounding box.

fields.name: BoundingBoxWidth
fields.doc: BoundingBoxWidth is the width of the client's bounding box.

fields.name: BoundingBoxHeight
fields.doc: BoundingBoxHeight is the height of the client's bounding box.

fields.name: MovementSpeed
fields.doc: MovementSpeed is the movement speed attribute or 0 if not set.

fields.name: UnderwaterMovementSpeed
fields.doc: UnderwaterMovementSpeed is the underwater movement speed attribute or 0 if not set.

fields.name: LavaMovementSpeed
fields.doc: LavaMovementSpeed is the lava movement speed attribute or 0 if not set.

fields.name: JumpStrength
fields.doc: JumpStrength is the jump strength attribute or 0 if not set.

fields.name: Health
fields.doc: Health is the health attribute or 0 if not set.

fields.name: Hunger
fields.doc: Hunger is the hunger attribute or 0 if not set.

fields.name: FrictionModifier
fields.doc: FrictionModifier is the friction modifier movement attribute.

fields.name: Bounciness
fields.doc: Bounciness is the bounciness movement attribute.

fields.name: AirDragModifier
fields.doc: AirDragModifier is the air drag modifier movement attribute.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc: EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity that the prediction data applies to.

fields.name: Flying
fields.doc: Flying specifies if the client is currently flying.

types.name: packet.ClientStartItemCooldown
types.doc: ClientStartItemCooldown is sent by the server to the client to initiate a cooldown on an item.

fields.name: Category
fields.doc: Category is the category of the item to start the cooldown on.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Duration is the duration of ticks the cooldown should last.

types.name: packet.ClientToServerHandshake
types.doc:
ClientToServerHandshake is sent by the client in response to a ServerToClientHandshake packet sent by the
server. It is the first encrypted packet in the login handshake and serves as a confirmation that
encryption is correctly initialised client side.

types.name: packet.ClientboundUpdateSoundData
types.doc:
ClientboundUpdateSoundData is sent by the server to update a sound that is currently playing, identified by
the handle that the server sent in the PlaySound packet that started it. Currently, the data field is
repeated 7 times, but only the last Resume field is actually used by the client for the actual value.

fields.name: ServerSoundHandle
fields.doc: ServerSoundHandle is the server-side handle of the sound to update.

types.name: packet.CodeBuilder
types.doc:
CodeBuilder is an Education Edition packet sent by the server to the client to open the URL to a Code
Builder (websocket) server.

fields.name: URL
fields.doc: URL is the url to the Code Builder (websocket) server.

fields.name: ShouldOpenCodeBuilder
fields.doc:
ShouldOpenCodeBuilder specifies if the client should automatically open the Code Builder app. If set to
true, the client will attempt to use the Code Builder app to connect to and interface with the server
running at the URL above.

types.name: packet.CodeBuilderSource
types.doc:
CodeBuilderSource is an Education Edition packet sent by the client to the server to run an operation with a
code builder.

fields.name: Operation
fields.doc: Operation is used to distinguish the operation performed. It is always one of the constants listed above.

fields.name: Category
fields.doc:
Category is used to distinguish the category of the operation performed. It is always one of the constants
listed above.

fields.name: CodeStatus
fields.doc: CodeStatus is the status of the code builder. It is always one of the constants listed above.

types.name: packet.CommandBlockUpdate
types.doc:
CommandBlockUpdate is sent by the client to update a command block at a specific position. The command
block may be either a physical block or an entity.

fields.name: Block
fields.doc:
Block specifies if the command block updated was an actual physical block. If false, the command block
is in a minecart and has an entity runtime ID instead.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the command block updated. It is only set if Block is set to true. Nothing
happens if no command block is set at this position.

fields.name: Mode
fields.doc:
Mode is the mode of the command block. It is either CommandBlockImpulse, CommandBlockChain or
CommandBlockRepeat. It is only set if Block is set to true.

fields.name: NeedsRedstone
fields.doc:
NeedsRedstone specifies if the command block needs to be powered by redstone to be activated. If false,
the command block is always active. The field is only set if Block is set to true.

fields.name: Conditional
fields.doc:
Conditional specifies the behaviour of the command block if the command block before it (the opposite
side of the direction the arrow if facing) fails to execute. If set to false, it will activate at all
times, whereas if set to true, it will activate only if the previous command block executed
successfully. The field is only set if Block is set to true.

fields.name: MinecartEntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
MinecartEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the minecart entity carrying the command block that is
updated. It is set only if Block is set to false.

fields.name: Command
fields.doc:
Command is the command currently entered in the command block. This is the command that is executed
when the command block is activated.

fields.name: LastOutput
fields.doc:
LastOutput is the output of the last command executed by the command block. It may be left empty to
show simply no output at all, in combination with setting ShouldTrackOutput to false.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc:
Name is the name of the command block updated. If not empty, it will show this name hovering above the
command block when hovering over the block with the cursor.

fields.name: FilteredName
fields.doc:
FilteredName is a filtered version of Name with all the profanity removed. The client will use this
over Name if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

fields.name: ShouldTrackOutput
fields.doc:
ShouldTrackOutput specifies if the command block tracks output. If set to false, the output box won't
be shown within the command block.

fields.name: TickDelay
fields.doc:
TickDelay is the delay in ticks between executions of a command block, if it is a repeating command
block.

fields.name: ExecuteOnFirstTick
fields.doc:
ExecuteOnFirstTick specifies if the command block should execute on the first tick, AKA as soon as the
command block is enabled.

types.name: packet.CommandOutput
types.doc:
CommandOutput is sent by the server to the client to send text as output of a command. Most servers do not
use this packet and instead simply send Text packets, but there is reason to send it.
If the origin of a CommandRequest packet is not the player itself, but, for example, a websocket server,
sending a Text packet will not do what is expected: The message should go to the websocket server, not to
the client's chat. The CommandOutput packet will make sure the messages are relayed to the correct origin
of the command request.

fields.name: CommandOrigin
fields.doc:
CommandOrigin is the data specifying the origin of the command. In other words, the source that the
command request was from, such as the player itself or a websocket server. The client forwards the
messages in this packet to the right origin, depending on what is sent here.

fields.name: OutputType
fields.doc:
OutputType specifies the type of output that is sent. The OutputType sent by vanilla games appears to
be CommandOutputTypeAllOutput, which seems to work.

fields.name: SuccessCount
fields.doc:
SuccessCount is the amount of times that a command was executed successfully as a result of the command
that was requested. For servers, this is usually a rather meaningless fields, but for vanilla, this is
applicable for commands created with Functions.

fields.name: OutputMessages
fields.doc:
OutputMessages is a list of all output messages that should be sent to the player. Whether they are
shown or not, depends on the type of the messages.

fields.name: DataSet
fields.doc: DataSet ... TODO: Find out what this is for.

types.name: packet.CommandRequest
types.doc:
CommandRequest is sent by the client to request the execution of a server-side command. Although some
servers support sending commands using the Text packet, this packet is guaranteed to have the correct
result.

fields.name: CommandLine
fields.doc:
CommandLine is the raw entered command line. The client does no parsing of the command line by itself
(unlike it did in the early stages), but lets the server do that.

fields.name: CommandOrigin
fields.doc:
CommandOrigin is the data specifying the origin of the command. In other words, the source that the
command was from, such as the player itself or a websocket server.

fields.name: Internal
fields.doc:
Internal specifies if the command request internal. Setting it to false seems to work and the usage of
this field is not known.

fields.name: Version
fields.doc: Version is the version of the command that is being executed. This field currently has no purpose or functionality.

types.name: packet.CompletedUsingItem
types.doc:
CompletedUsingItem is sent by the server to tell the client that it should be done using the item it is
currently using.

fields.name: UsedItemID
fields.doc:
UsedItemID is the item ID of the item that the client completed using. This should typically be the
ID of the item held in the hand.

fields.name: UseMethod
fields.doc:
UseMethod is the method of the using of the item that was completed. It is one of the constants that
may be found above.

types.name: packet.ContainerClose
types.doc:
ContainerClose is sent by the server to close a container the player currently has opened, which was opened
using the ContainerOpen packet, or by the client to tell the server it closed a particular container, such
as the crafting grid.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc:
WindowID is the ID representing the window of the container that should be closed. It must be equal to
the one sent in the ContainerOpen packet to close the designated window.

fields.name: ContainerType
fields.doc:
ContainerType is the type of container that the server is trying to close. This is used to validate on
the client side whether or not the server's close request is valid.

fields.name: ServerSide
fields.doc:
ServerSide determines whether or not the container was force-closed by the server. If this value is
not set correctly, the client may ignore the packet and respond with a PacketViolationWarning.

types.name: packet.ContainerOpen
types.doc:
ContainerOpen is sent by the server to open a container client-side. This container must be physically
present in the world, for the packet to have any effect. Unlike Java Edition, Bedrock Edition requires that
chests for example must be present and in range to open its inventory.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc:
WindowID is the ID representing the window that is being opened. It may be used later to close the
container using a ContainerClose packet.

fields.name: ContainerType
fields.doc:
ContainerType is the type ID of the container that is being opened when opening the container at the
position of the packet. It depends on the block/entity, and could, for example, be the window type of
a chest or a hopper, but also a horse inventory.

fields.name: ContainerPosition
fields.doc:
ContainerPosition is the position of the container opened. The position must point to a block entity
that actually has a container. If that is not the case, the window will not be opened and the packet
will be ignored, if a valid ContainerEntityUniqueID has not also been provided.

fields.name: ContainerEntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
ContainerEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity container that was opened. It is only used if
the ContainerType is one that points to an entity, for example a horse.

types.name: packet.ContainerRegistryCleanup
types.doc:
ContainerRegistryCleanup is sent by the server to trigger a client-side cleanup of the dynamic container
registry.

fields.name: RemovedContainers
fields.doc:
RemovedContainers is a list of protocol.FullContainerName's that should be removed from the client-side
container registry.

types.name: packet.ContainerSetData
types.doc:
ContainerSetData is sent by the server to update specific data of a single container, meaning a block such
as a furnace or a brewing stand. This data is usually used by the client to display certain features
client-side.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc:
WindowID is the ID of the window that should have its data set. The player must have a window open with
the window ID passed, or nothing will happen.

fields.name: Key
fields.doc:
Key is the key of the property. It is one of the constants that can be found above. Multiple properties
share the same key, but the functionality depends on the type of the container that the data is set to.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc: Value is the value of the property. Its use differs per property.

types.name: packet.CorrectPlayerMovePrediction
types.doc:
CorrectPlayerMovePrediction is sent by the server if and only if StartGame.ServerAuthoritativeMovementMode
is set to AuthoritativeMovementModeServerWithRewind. The packet is used to correct movement at a specific
point in time.

fields.name: PredictionType
fields.doc: PredictionType is the type of prediction that was corrected. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position that the player is supposed to be at the tick written in the field below.
The client will change its current position based on movement after that tick starting from the
Position.

fields.name: Delta
fields.doc: Delta is the change in position compared to what the client sent as its position at that specific tick.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.doc: Rotation is the rotation of the player at the tick written in the field below.

fields.name: VehicleAngularVelocity
fields.doc: VehicleAngularVelocity is the angular velocity of the vehicle that the rider is riding.

fields.name: OnGround
fields.doc: OnGround specifies if the player was on the ground at the time of the tick below.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the tick of the movement which was corrected by this packet.

types.name: packet.CraftingData
types.doc:
CraftingData is sent by the server to let the client know all crafting data that the server maintains. This
includes shapeless crafting, crafting table recipes, furnace recipes etc. Each crafting station's recipes
are included in it.

fields.name: ShapedRecipes
fields.doc: ShapedRecipes through SmithingTrimRecipes are the typed recipe vectors used by 1.26.40.

fields.name: PotionRecipes
fields.doc: PotionRecipes is a list of all potion mixing recipes which may be used in the brewing stand.

fields.name: PotionContainerChangeRecipes
fields.doc:
PotionContainerChangeRecipes is a list of all recipes to convert a potion from one type to another,
such as from a drinkable potion to a splash potion, or from a splash potion to a lingering potion.

fields.name: MaterialReducers
fields.doc: MaterialReducers is a list of all material reducers which is used in education edition chemistry.

fields.name: ClearRecipes
fields.doc:
ClearRecipes indicates if all recipes currently active on the client should be cleaned. Doing this
means that the client will have no recipes active by itself: Any CraftingData packets previously sent
will also be discarded, and only the recipes in this CraftingData packet will be used.

types.name: packet.CreatePhoto
types.doc:
CreatePhoto is a packet that allows players to export photos from their portfolios into items in their inventory.
This packet only works on the Education Edition version of Minecraft.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc: EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity.

fields.name: PhotoName
fields.doc: PhotoName is the name of the photo.

fields.name: ItemName
fields.doc: ItemName is the name of the photo as an item.

types.name: packet.CreativeContent
types.doc:
CreativeContent is a packet sent by the server to set the creative inventory's content for a player.
Introduced in 1.16, this packet replaces the previous method - sending an InventoryContent packet with
creative inventory window ID.
As of v1.21.60, this packet is no longer required to be sent as part of the login sequence however the
client will crash if they try to open their creative inventory before receiving this packet. Every item
must be part of a group, any items that are not part of a group will need to reference an "anonymous group"
which has an empty name OR no icon. The order of Groups and Items is how the client will render items
in the creative inventory compared to the previous, hard coded order.

Below is an example of defining 2 ungrouped items, 2 grouped items and then another 2 ungrouped items, all
in the nature category.

	CreativeContent{
		Groups: []protocol.CreativeGroup{
			{Category: 1}, // No name or icon, this is the "anonymous group"
			{Category: 1, Name: "itemGroup.name.planks", Icon: protocol.ItemStack{...}}, // A "planks" group
			{Category: 1}, // Another "anonymous group"
		},
		Items: []protocol.CreativeItem{
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 0, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 0}, // Ungrouped before "planks"
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 1, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 0}, // Ungrouped before "planks"
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 2, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 1}, // Grouped under the "planks" group
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 3, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 1}, // Grouped under the "planks" group
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 4, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 2}, // Ungrouped after "planks"
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 5, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 2}, // Ungrouped after "planks"
		}
	}

fields.name: Groups
fields.doc: Groups is a list of the groups that should be added to the creative inventory.

fields.name: Items
fields.doc: Items is a list of the items that should be added to the creative inventory.

types.name: packet.CurrentStructureFeature
types.doc:
CurrentStructureFeature is sent by the server to let the client know the name of the structure feature
that the player is currently occupying.

fields.name: CurrentFeature
fields.doc:
CurrentFeature is the identifier of the structure feature that the player is currently occupying.
If the player is not occupying any structure feature, this field is empty.

types.name: packet.DeathInfo
types.doc:
DeathInfo is a packet sent from the server to the client expected to be sent when a player dies. It contains messages
related to the player's death, which are shown on the death screen as of v1.19.10.

fields.name: Cause
fields.doc: Cause is the cause of the player's death, such as "suffocation" or "suicide".

fields.name: Messages
fields.doc: Messages is a list of death messages to be shown on the death screen.

types.name: packet.DebugInfo
types.doc:
DebugInfo is a packet sent by the server to the client. It does not seem to do anything when sent to the
normal client in 1.16.

fields.name: PlayerUniqueID
fields.doc: PlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the player that the packet is sent to.

fields.name: Data
fields.doc: Data is the debug data.

types.name: packet.DebugMarkerData
types.doc:
DebugMarkerData holds the data of a debug marker cube spawned through a
ClientBoundDebugRenderer packet.

fields.name: Text
fields.doc: Text is the text that is displayed above the debug.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position to spawn the debug on.

fields.name: Colour
fields.doc:
Colour is the RGBA colour rendered on the debug, packed as an ARGB uint32
on the wire.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Duration is how long the debug will last in the world for. It is measured in milliseconds.

types.name: packet.DimensionData
types.doc:
DimensionData is a packet sent from the server to the client containing information about data-driven dimensions
that the server may have registered. This packet does not seem to be sent by default, rather only being sent when
any data-driven dimensions are registered.

fields.name: Definitions
fields.doc: Definitions contain a list of data-driven dimension definitions registered on the server.

types.name: packet.Disconnect
types.doc:
Disconnect may be sent by the server to disconnect the client using an optional message to send as the
disconnect screen.

fields.name: Reason
fields.doc:
Reason is the reason for the disconnection. This affects the error code displayed on the Ore UI
disconnection screen and is one of the constants above.

fields.name: HideDisconnectionScreen
fields.doc:
HideDisconnectionScreen specifies if the disconnection screen should be hidden when the client is
disconnected, meaning it will be sent directly to the main menu.

fields.name: Message
fields.doc:
Message is an optional message to show when disconnected. This message is only written if the
HideDisconnectionScreen field is set to false.

fields.name: FilteredMessage
fields.doc:
FilteredMessage is a filtered version of Message with all the profanity removed. The client will use
this over Message if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

types.name: packet.EditorNetwork
types.doc:
EditorNetwork is a packet sent from the server to the client and vise-versa to communicate editor-mode related
information. It carries a single compound tag containing the relevant information.

fields.name: RouteToManager
fields.doc: RouteToManager ...

fields.name: Payload
fields.doc: Payload is a network little endian compound tag holding data relevant to the editor.

types.name: packet.EducationResourceURI
types.doc: EducationResourceURI is a packet that transmits education resource settings to all clients.

fields.name: Resource
fields.doc: Resource is the resource that is being referenced.

types.name: packet.EducationSettings
types.doc:
EducationSettings is a packet sent by the server to update Minecraft: Education Edition related settings.
It is unused by the normal base game.

fields.name: CodeBuilderDefaultURI
fields.doc:
CodeBuilderDefaultURI is the default URI that the code builder is ran on. Using this, a Code Builder program can
make code directly affect the server.

fields.name: CodeBuilderTitle
fields.doc: CodeBuilderTitle is the title of the code builder shown when connected to the CodeBuilderDefaultURI.

fields.name: CanResizeCodeBuilder
fields.doc:
CanResizeCodeBuilder specifies if clients connected to the world should be able to resize the code
builder when it is opened.

fields.name: DisableLegacyTitleBar
fields.doc: DisableLegacyTitleBar ...

fields.name: PostProcessFilter
fields.doc: PostProcessFilter ...

fields.name: ScreenshotBorderPath
fields.doc: ScreenshotBorderPath ...

fields.name: CanModifyBlocks
fields.doc: CanModifyBlocks ...

fields.name: OverrideURI
fields.doc: OverrideURI ...

fields.name: HasQuiz
fields.doc: HasQuiz specifies if the world has a quiz connected to it.

fields.name: ExternalLinkSettings
fields.doc: ExternalLinkSettings ...

types.name: packet.Emote
types.doc:
Emote is sent by both the server and the client. When the client sends an emote, it sends this packet to
the server, after which the server will broadcast the packet to other players online.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the entity that sent the emote. When a player sends this packet, it has this field
set as its own entity runtime ID.

fields.name: EmoteLength
fields.doc: EmoteLength is the number of ticks that the emote lasts for.

fields.name: EmoteID
fields.doc: EmoteID is the ID of the emote to send.

fields.name: XUID
fields.doc:
XUID is the Xbox User ID of the player that sent the emote. It is only set when the emote is used by a player that
is authenticated with Xbox Live.

fields.name: PlatformID
fields.doc:
PlatformID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when using an emote (presumably only for Nintendo
Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to emote with each other.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
Flags is a combination of flags that change the way the Emote packet operates. When the server sends
this packet to other players, EmoteFlagServerSide must be present.

types.name: packet.EmoteList
types.doc:
EmoteList is sent by the client every time it joins the server and when it equips new emotes. It may be
used by the server to find out which emotes the client has available. If the player has no emotes equipped,
this packet is not sent.
Under certain circumstances, this packet is also sent from the server to the client, but I was unable to
find when this is done.

fields.name: PlayerRuntimeID
fields.doc:
PlayerRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player that owns the emote pieces below. If sent by the
client, this player runtime ID is always that of the player itself.

fields.name: EmotePieces
fields.doc: EmotePieces is a list of emote pieces that the player with the runtime ID above has.

types.name: packet.Event
types.doc:
Event is sent by the server to send an event with additional data. It is typically sent to the client for
telemetry reasons, much like the SimpleEvent packet.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: UsePlayerID
fields.doc:
UsePlayerID ...
TODO: Figure out what UsePlayerID is for.

fields.name: Event
fields.doc: Event is the event that is transmitted.

types.name: packet.FeatureRegistry
types.doc:
FeatureRegistry is a packet used to notify the client about the world generation features the server is currently
using. This is used in combination with the client-side world generation system introduced in v1.19.20, allowing the
client to completely generate the chunks of the world without having to rely on the server.

fields.name: Features
fields.doc: Features is a slice of all registered world generation features.

types.name: packet.FilterText
types.doc:
FilterText is sent by the both the client and the server. The client sends the packet to the server to
allow the server to filter the text server-side. The server then responds with the same packet and the
safer version of the text.

Deprecated: This packet was deprecated in unknown.

fields.name: Text
fields.doc: Text is either the text from the client or the safer version of the text sent by the server.

fields.name: FromServer
fields.doc: FromServer indicates if the packet was sent by the server or not.

types.name: packet.GUIDataPickItem
types.doc:
GUIDataPickItem is sent by the server to make the client 'select' a hot bar slot. It currently appears to
be broken however, and does not actually set the selected slot to the hot bar slot set in the packet.

fields.name: ItemName
fields.doc:
ItemName is the name of the item that shows up in the top part of the popup that shows up when
selecting an item. It is shown as if an item was selected by the player itself.

fields.name: ItemEffects
fields.doc: ItemEffects is the line under the ItemName, where the effects of the item are usually situated.

fields.name: HotBarSlot
fields.doc:
HotBarSlot is the hot bar slot to be selected/picked. This does not currently work, so it does not
matter what number this is.

types.name: packet.GameRulesChanged
types.doc:
GameRulesChanged is sent by the server to the client to update client-side game rules, such as game rules
like the 'showCoordinates' game rule.

fields.name: GameRules
fields.doc:
GameRules defines game rules changed with their respective values. The value of these game rules may be
either 'bool', 'int32' or 'float32'.
Note that some game rules are server side only, and don't necessarily need to be sent to the client.
Only changed game rules need to be sent in this packet. Game rules that were not changed do not need to
be sent if the client is already updated on them.

types.name: packet.GameTestRequest
types.doc: GameTestRequest ...

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name represents the name of the test.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.doc: Rotation represents the rotation of the test. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: Repetitions
fields.doc: Repetitions represents the amount of times the test will be run.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position at which the test will be performed.

fields.name: StopOnError
fields.doc: StopOnError indicates whether the test should immediately stop when an error is encountered.

fields.name: TestsPerRow
fields.doc: TestsPerRow ...

fields.name: MaxTestsPerBatch
fields.doc: MaxTestsPerBatch ...

types.name: packet.GameTestResults
types.doc:
GameTestResults is a packet sent in response to the GameTestRequest packet, with a boolean indicating whether the
test was successful or not, and an error string if the test failed.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name represents the name of the test.

fields.name: Succeeded
fields.doc: Succeeded indicates whether the test succeeded or not.

fields.name: Error
fields.doc: Error is the error that occurred. If Succeeded is true, this field is empty.

types.name: packet.GraphicsOverrideParameter
types.doc: GraphicsOverrideParameter is sent by the server to override graphics parameters.

fields.name: Values
fields.doc: Values is a list of parameter keyframe values.

fields.name: FloatValue
fields.doc: FloatValue is an optional single float graphics parameter to be overridden.

fields.name: Vec3Value
fields.doc: Vec3Value is an optional single Vec3 graphics parameter to be overridden.

fields.name: BiomeIdentifier
fields.doc: BiomeIdentifier is the identifier of the biome for which the parameters apply.

fields.name: PlayerIdentifier
fields.doc: PlayerIdentifier is the optional identifier of the player for which the override parameter applies.

fields.name: ParameterType
fields.doc: ParameterType is the type of parameter being overridden.

fields.name: Reset
fields.doc: Reset indicates whether to reset the parameters.

types.name: packet.HurtArmour
types.doc:
HurtArmour is sent by the server to damage the player's armour after being hit. The packet should never be
used by servers as it hands the responsibility over to the player completely, while the server can easily
reliably update the armour damage of players itself.

fields.name: Cause
fields.doc: Cause is the cause of the damage dealt to the armour.

fields.name: Damage
fields.doc:
Damage is the amount of damage points that was dealt to the player. The damage to the armour will be
calculated by the client based upon this damage, and will also be based upon any enchantments like
thorns that the armour may have.

fields.name: ArmourSlots
fields.doc: ArmourSlots is a bitset of all armour slots affected.

types.name: packet.Interact
types.doc:
Interact is sent by the client when it interacts with another entity in some way. It used to be used for
normal entity and block interaction, but this is no longer the case now.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
Action type is the ID of the action that was executed by the player. It is one of the constants that
may be found above.

fields.name: TargetEntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
TargetEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity that the player interacted with. This is empty
for the InteractActionOpenInventory action type.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position associated with the ActionType above. For the InteractActionMouseOverEntity, this is the
position relative to the entity moused over over which the player hovered with its mouse/touch. For the
InteractActionLeaveVehicle, this is the position that the player spawns at after leaving the vehicle.

types.name: packet.InventoryContent
types.doc:
InventoryContent is sent by the server to update the full content of a particular inventory. It is usually
sent for the main inventory of the player, but also works for other inventories that are currently opened
by the player.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc:
WindowID is the ID that identifies one of the windows that the client currently has opened, or one of
the consistent windows such as the main inventory.

fields.name: Content
fields.doc:
Content is the new content of the inventory. The length of this slice must be equal to the full size of
the inventory window updated.

fields.name: Container
fields.doc: Container is the protocol.FullContainerName that describes the container that the content is for.

fields.name: StorageItem
fields.doc:
StorageItem is the item that is acting as the storage container for the inventory. If the inventory is
not a dynamic container then this field should be left empty. When set, only the item type is used by
the client and none of the other stack info.

types.name: packet.InventorySlot
types.doc:
InventorySlot is sent by the server to update a single slot in one of the inventory windows that the client
currently has opened. Usually this is the main inventory, but it may also be the off hand or, for example,
a chest inventory.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc:
WindowID is the ID of the window that the packet modifies. It must point to one of the windows that the
client currently has opened.

fields.name: Slot
fields.doc:
Slot is the index of the slot that the packet modifies. The new item will be set to the slot at this
index.

fields.name: Container
fields.doc: Container is the protocol.FullContainerName that describes the container that the content is for.
