fields.name: StorageItem
fields.doc:
StorageItem is the item that is acting as the storage container for the inventory. If the inventory is
not a dynamic container then this field should be left empty. When set, only the item type is used by
the client and none of the other stack info.

fields.name: NewItem
fields.doc:
NewItem is the item to be put in the slot at Slot. It will overwrite any item that may currently
be present in that slot.

types.name: packet.InventoryTransaction
types.doc:
InventoryTransaction is a packet sent by the client. It essentially exists out of multiple sub-packets,
each of which have something to do with the inventory in one way or another. Some of these sub-packets
directly relate to the inventory, others relate to interaction with the world, that could potentially
result in a change in the inventory.

fields.name: LegacyRequestID
fields.doc:
LegacyRequestID is an ID that is only non-zero at times when sent by the client. The server should
always send 0 for this. When this field is not 0, the LegacySetItemSlots slice below will have values
in it.
LegacyRequestID ties in with the ItemStackResponse packet. If this field is non-0, the server should
respond with an ItemStackResponse packet. Some inventory actions such as dropping an item out of the
hotbar are still one using this packet, and the ItemStackResponse packet needs to tie in with it.

fields.name: LegacySetItemSlots
fields.doc:
LegacySetItemSlots are only present if the LegacyRequestID is non-zero. These item slots inform the
server of the slots that were changed during the inventory transaction, and the server should send
back an ItemStackResponse packet with these slots present in it. (Or false with no slots, if rejected.)

fields.name: Actions
fields.doc:
Actions is a list of actions that took place, that form the inventory transaction together. Each of
these actions hold one slot in which one item was changed to another. In general, the combination of
all of these actions results in a balanced inventory transaction. This should be checked to ensure that
no items are cheated into the inventory.

fields.name: TransactionData
fields.doc:
TransactionData is a data object that holds data specific to the type of transaction that the
TransactionPacket held. Its concrete type must be one of NormalTransactionData, MismatchTransactionData
UseItemTransactionData, UseItemOnEntityTransactionData or ReleaseItemTransactionData. If nil is set,
the transaction will be assumed to of type InventoryTransactionTypeNormal.

types.name: packet.ItemRegistry
types.doc:
ItemRegistry is sent by the server to send the client a list of available items and attach client-side
components to a custom item. This packet was formerly known as the ItemComponent packet before 1.21.60,
which did not include item definitions but only the components.

fields.name: Items
fields.doc:
Items is a list of all items with their legacy IDs which are available in the game. Failing to send any
of the items that are in the game will crash mobile clients. Any custom components are also attached to
the items in this list.

types.name: packet.ItemStackRequest
types.doc:
ItemStackRequest is sent by the client to change item stacks in an inventory. It is essentially a
replacement of the InventoryTransaction packet added in 1.16 for inventory specific actions, such as moving
items around or crafting. The InventoryTransaction packet is still used for actions such as placing blocks
and interacting with entities.

fields.name: Requests
fields.doc:
Requests holds a list of item stack requests. These requests are all separate, but the client buffers
the requests, so you might find multiple unrelated requests in this packet.

types.name: packet.ItemStackResponse
types.doc:
ItemStackResponse is sent by the server in response to an ItemStackRequest packet from the client. This
packet is used to either approve or reject ItemStackRequests from the client. If a request is approved, the
client will simply continue as normal. If rejected, the client will undo the actions so that the inventory
should be in sync with the server again.

fields.name: Responses
fields.doc:
Responses is a list of responses to ItemStackRequests sent by the client before. Responses either
approve or reject a request from the client.
Vanilla limits the size of this slice to 4096.

types.name: packet.JigsawStructureData
types.doc: JigsawStructureData is sent by the server to let the client know all the rules for jigsaw structures.

fields.name: StructureData
fields.doc:
StructureData is a network NBT serialised compound of all the jigsaw structure rules defined
on the server.

types.name: packet.LabTable
types.doc:
LabTable is sent by the client to let the server know it started a chemical reaction in Education Edition,
and is sent by the server to other clients to show the effects.
The packet is only functional if Education features are enabled.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the action that was executed. It is one of the constants above. Typically,
only LabTableActionCombine is sent by the client, whereas LabTableActionReact is sent by the server.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position at which the lab table used was located.

fields.name: ReactionType
fields.doc:
ReactionType is the type of the reaction that took place as a result of the items put into the lab
table. The reaction type can be either that of an item or a particle, depending on whatever the result
was of the reaction.

types.name: packet.LecternUpdate
types.doc:
LecternUpdate is sent by the client to update the server on which page was opened in a book on a lectern,
or if the book should be removed from it.

fields.name: Page
fields.doc: Page is the page number in the book that was opened by the player on the lectern.

fields.name: PageCount
fields.doc: PageCount is the number of pages that the book opened in the lectern has.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the lectern that was updated. If no lectern is at the block position,
the packet should be ignored.

types.name: packet.LessonProgress
types.doc:
LessonProgress is a packet sent by the server to the client to inform the client of updated progress on a lesson.
This packet only functions on the Minecraft: Education Edition version of the game.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.doc: Identifier is the identifier of the lesson that is being progressed.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is the action the client should perform to show progress. This is one of the constants defined above.

fields.name: Score
fields.doc: Score is the score the client should use when displaying the progress.

types.name: packet.LevelChunk
types.doc:
LevelChunk is sent by the server to provide the client with a chunk of a world data (16xYx16 blocks).
Typically, a certain amount of chunks is sent to the client before sending it the spawn PlayStatus packet,
so that the client spawns in a loaded world.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position contains the X and Z coordinates of the chunk sent. You can convert a block coordinate to a chunk
coordinate by right-shifting it four bits.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc:
Dimension is the ID of the dimension that the chunk belongs to. This must always be set otherwise the
client will always assume the chunk is part of the overworld dimension.

fields.name: SubChunkLimit
fields.doc:
SubChunkLimit is the maximum amount of sub-chunks a client will request when in request mode. A value of -1
means there is no limit.

fields.name: CacheEnabled
fields.doc:
CacheEnabled specifies if the client blob cache should be enabled. This system is based on hashes of
blobs which are consistent and saved by the client in combination with that blob, so that the server
does not have the same chunk multiple times. If the client does not yet have a blob with the hash sent,
it will send a ClientCacheBlobStatus packet containing the hashes is does not have the data of.

fields.name: BlobHashes
fields.doc:
BlobHashes is a list of all blob hashes used in the chunk. It is composed of SubChunkCount + 1 hashes,
with the first SubChunkCount hashes being those of the sub-chunks and the last one that of the biome
of the chunk.
If CacheEnabled is set to false, BlobHashes can be left empty.

fields.name: RawPayload
fields.doc:
RawPayload is a serialised string of chunk data. The data held depends on if CacheEnabled is set to
true. If set to false, the payload is composed of multiple sub-chunks, each of which carry a version
which indicates the way they are serialised, followed by biomes, border blocks and tile entities. If
CacheEnabled is true, the payload consists out of the border blocks and tile entities only.

types.name: packet.LevelEvent
types.doc:
LevelEvent is sent by the server to make a certain event in the level occur. It ranges from particles, to
sounds, and other events such as starting rain and block breaking.

fields.name: EventType
fields.doc:
EventType is the ID of the event that is being 'called'. It is one of the events found in the constants
above.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the level event. Practically every event requires this Vec3 set for it, as
particles, sounds and block editing relies on it.

fields.name: EventData
fields.doc:
EventData is an integer holding additional data of the event. The type of data held depends on the
EventType.

types.name: packet.LevelEventGeneric
types.doc:
LevelEventGeneric is sent by the server to send a 'generic' level event to the client. This packet sends an
NBT serialised object and may for that reason be used for any event holding additional data.

fields.name: EventID
fields.doc:
EventID is a unique identifier that identifies the event called. The data that follows has fields in
the NBT depending on what event it is.

fields.name: SerialisedEventData
fields.doc:
SerialisedEventData is a network little endian serialised object of event data, with fields that vary
depending on EventID.
Unlike many other NBT structures, this data is not actually in a compound but just loosely floating
NBT tags. To decode using the nbt package, you would need to append 0x0a00 at the start (compound id
and name length) and add 0x00 at the end, to manually wrap it in a compound. Likewise, you would have
to remove these bytes when encoding.
Example of the resulting data with an EventID of 2026:
TAG_Compound({
   'pos15x': TAG_Float(198),
   'pos11x': TAG_Float(201),
   'pos6y': TAG_Float(65),
   'pos13y': TAG_Float(64),
   'pos17z': TAG_Float(36),
   'pos8y': TAG_Float(65),
   'originY': TAG_Float(65.06125),
   'pos10z': TAG_Float(37),
   'pos13x': TAG_Float(201),
   'pos7y': TAG_Float(65),
   'pos9x': TAG_Float(203),
   'pos11y': TAG_Float(64),
   'pos15y': TAG_Float(65),
   'pos15z': TAG_Float(40),
   'pos7z': TAG_Float(41),
   'pos8x': TAG_Float(198),
   'pos13z': TAG_Float(40),
   'pos1z': TAG_Float(37),
   'pos6z': TAG_Float(42),
   'size': TAG_Int(18),
   'pos0x': TAG_Float(204),
   'pos12x': TAG_Float(200),
   'pos2x': TAG_Float(204),
   'pos9z': TAG_Float(37),
   'pos16y': TAG_Float(64),
   'pos5x': TAG_Float(204),
   'pos5y': TAG_Float(64),
   'pos17x': TAG_Float(202),
   'pos3y': TAG_Float(64),
   'pos3z': TAG_Float(36),
   'radius': TAG_Float(4),
   'pos0z': TAG_Float(38),
   'pos4z': TAG_Float(36),
   'pos8z': TAG_Float(38),
   'pos1x': TAG_Float(204),
   'pos0y': TAG_Float(64),
   'pos14z': TAG_Float(39),

types.name: packet.LevelSoundEvent
types.doc:
LevelSoundEvent is sent by the server to make any kind of built-in sound heard to a player. It is sent to,
for example, play a stepping sound or a shear sound. The packet is also sent by the client, in which case
it could be forwarded by the server to the other players online. If possible, the packets from the client
should be ignored however, and the server should play them on its own accord.

fields.name: SoundType
fields.doc:
SoundType is the type of the sound to play. It is one of the constants above. Some of the sound types
require additional data, which is set in the ExtraData field.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the sound event. The player will be able to hear the direction of the sound
based on what position is sent here.

fields.name: ExtraData
fields.doc:
ExtraData is a packed integer that some sound types use to provide extra data. An example of this is
the note sound, which is composed of a pitch and an instrument type.

fields.name: EntityType
fields.doc:
EntityType is the string entity type of the entity that emitted the sound, for example
'minecraft:skeleton'. Some sound types use this entity type for additional data.

fields.name: BabyMob
fields.doc:
BabyMob specifies if the sound should be that of a baby mob. It is most notably used for parrot
imitations, which will change based on if this field is set to true or not.

fields.name: DisableRelativeVolume
fields.doc:
DisableRelativeVolume specifies if the sound should be played relatively or not. If set to true, the
sound will have full volume, regardless of where the Position is, whereas if set to false, the sound's
volume will be based on the distance to Position.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of a source entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

fields.name: FireAtPosition
fields.doc:
FireAtPosition is the position in the same world at which the event should fire. If this is not present,
the position entity will be used instead.

types.name: packet.LocatorBar
types.doc: LocatorBar is sent by the server to add, remove or update waypoints on the client's locator bar.

fields.name: Waypoints
fields.doc: Waypoints is a slice of waypoints to add, remove or update.

types.name: packet.Login
types.doc:
Login is sent when the client initially tries to join the server. It is the first packet sent and contains
information specific to the player.

fields.name: ClientProtocol
fields.doc:
ClientProtocol is the protocol version of the player. The player is disconnected if the protocol is incompatible
with the protocol of the server. It has been superseded by the protocol version sent in the
RequestNetworkSettings packet, so this should no longer be used by the server.

fields.name: ConnectionRequest
fields.doc:
ConnectionRequest is a string containing information about the player and JWTs that may be used to
verify if the player is connected to XBOX Live. The connection request also contains the necessary
client public key to initiate encryption.

types.name: packet.MapCreateLockedCopy
types.doc:
MapCreateLockedCopy is sent by the client to create a locked copy of one map into another map. In vanilla,
it is used in the cartography table to create a map that is locked and cannot be modified.

fields.name: OriginalMapID
fields.doc:
OriginalMapID is the ID of the map that is being copied. The locked copy will obtain all content that
is visible on this map, except the content will not change.

fields.name: NewMapID
fields.doc:
NewMapID is the ID of the map that holds the locked copy of the map that OriginalMapID points to. Its
contents will be impossible to change.

types.name: packet.MapInfoRequest
types.doc:
MapInfoRequest is sent by the client to request the server to deliver information of a certain map in the
inventory of the player. The server should respond with a ClientBoundMapItemData packet.

fields.name: MapID
fields.doc:
MapID is the unique identifier that represents the map that is requested over network. It remains
consistent across sessions.

fields.name: ClientPixels
fields.doc:
ClientPixels is a slice of pixels sent from the client to notify the server about the pixels that it isn't aware
of.

types.name: packet.MobArmourEquipment
types.doc:
MobArmourEquipment is sent by the server to the client to update the armour an entity is wearing. It is
sent for both players and other entities, such as zombies.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Helmet
fields.doc:
Helmet is the equipped helmet of the entity. Items that are not wearable on the head will not be
rendered by the client. Unlike in Java Edition, blocks cannot be worn.

fields.name: Chestplate
fields.doc:
Chestplate is the chestplate of the entity. Items that are not wearable as chestplate will not be
rendered.

fields.name: Leggings
fields.doc:
Leggings is the item worn as leggings by the entity. Items not wearable as leggings will not be
rendered client-side.

fields.name: Boots
fields.doc: Boots is the item worn as boots by the entity. Items not wearable as boots will not be rendered.

fields.name: Body
fields.doc: Body is the item worn on the body of the entity. Items not wearable on the body will not be rendered.

types.name: packet.MobEffect
types.doc:
MobEffect is sent by the server to apply an effect to the player, for example an effect like poison. It may
also be used to modify existing effects, or removing them completely.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Operation
fields.doc:
Operation is the operation of the packet. It is either MobEffectAdd, MobEffectModify or MobEffectRemove
and specifies the result of the packet client-side.

fields.name: EffectType
fields.doc:
EffectType is the ID of the effect to be added, removed or modified. It is one of the constants that
may be found above.

fields.name: Amplifier
fields.doc:
Amplifier is the amplifier of the effect. Take note that the amplifier is not the same as the effect's
level. The level is usually one higher than the amplifier, and the amplifier can actually be negative
to reverse the behaviour effect.

fields.name: Particles
fields.doc:
Particles specifies if viewers of the entity that gets the effect shows particles around it. If set to
false, no particles are emitted around the entity.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc:
Duration is the duration of the effect in ticks (20 per second). After the duration has elapsed, the
effect will be removed automatically client-side. A negative duration means the effect never expires.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

fields.name: Ambient
fields.doc: Ambient specifies if the effect is ambient. If set to false, it will not get treated as an ambient effect.

types.name: packet.MobEquipment
types.doc:
MobEquipment is sent by the client to the server and the server to the client to make the other side
aware of the new item that an entity is holding. It is used to show the item in the hand of entities such
as zombies too.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: NewItem
fields.doc:
NewItem is the new item held after sending the MobEquipment packet. The entity will be shown holding
that item to the player it was sent to.

fields.name: InventorySlot
fields.doc:
InventorySlot is the slot in the inventory that was held. This is the same as HotBarSlot, and only
remains for backwards compatibility.

fields.name: HotBarSlot
fields.doc:
HotBarSlot is the slot in the hot bar that was held. It is the same as InventorySlot, which is only
there for backwards compatibility purposes.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc:
WindowID is the window ID of the window that had its equipped item changed. This is usually the window
ID of the normal inventory, but may also be something else, for example with the off hand.

types.name: packet.ModalFormRequest
types.doc:
ModalFormRequest is sent by the server to make the client open a form. This form may be either a modal form
which has two options, a menu form for a selection of options and a custom form for properties.

fields.name: FormID
fields.doc:
FormID is an ID used to identify the form. The ID is saved by the client and sent back when the player
submits the form, so that the server can identify which form was submitted.

fields.name: FormData
fields.doc:
FormData is a JSON encoded object of form data. The content of the object differs, depending on the
type of the form sent, which is also set in the JSON.

types.name: packet.ModalFormResponse
types.doc:
ModalFormResponse is sent by the client in response to a ModalFormRequest, after the player has submitted
the form sent. It contains the options/properties selected by the player, or a JSON encoded 'null' if
the form was closed by clicking the X at the top right corner of the form.

fields.name: FormID
fields.doc:
FormID is the form ID of the form the client has responded to. It is the same as the ID sent in the
ModalFormRequest, and may be used to identify which form was submitted.

fields.name: ResponseData
fields.doc:
ResponseData is a JSON encoded value representing the response of the player. For a modal form, the response is
either true or false, for a menu form, the response is an integer specifying the index of the button clicked, and
for a custom form, the response is an array containing a value for each element.

fields.name: CancelReason
fields.doc: CancelReason represents the reason why the form was cancelled. It is one of the constants above.

types.name: packet.MotionPredictionHints
types.doc:
MotionPredictionHints is sent by the server to the client. There is a predictive movement component for
entities. This packet fills the "history" of that component and entity movement is computed based on the
points. Vanilla sends this packet instead of the SetActorMotion packet when 'spatial optimisations' are
enabled.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc: EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity whose velocity is sent to the client.

fields.name: Velocity
fields.doc: Velocity is the server-calculated velocity of the entity at the point of sending the packet.

fields.name: OnGround
fields.doc: OnGround specifies if the server currently thinks the entity is on the ground.

types.name: packet.MoveActorAbsolute
types.doc:
MoveActorAbsolute is sent by the server to move an entity to an absolute position. It is typically used
for movements where high accuracy isn't needed, such as for long range teleporting.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
Flags is a combination of flags that specify details of the movement. It is a combination of the flags
above.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position to spawn the entity on. If the entity is on a distance that the player cannot
see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.doc:
Rotation is a Vec3 holding the X, Y and Z rotation of the entity after the movement. This is a Vec3 for
the reason that projectiles like arrows don't have yaw/pitch, but do have roll.

types.name: packet.MoveActorDelta
types.doc:
MoveActorDelta is sent by the server to move an entity. The packet is specifically optimised to save as
much space as possible, by only writing non-zero fields.
As of 1.16.100, this packet no longer actually contains any deltas.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity that is being moved. The packet works provided a
non-player entity with this runtime ID is present.

fields.name: PositionX
fields.doc: Position is the new position that the entity was moved to.

fields.name: RotationX
fields.doc:
Rotation is the new absolute rotation. Unlike the position, it is not actually a delta. If any of the
values of this rotation are not sent, these values are 0 and no flag for them is present.

fields.name: OnGround
fields.doc: OnGround specifies whether the entity is on the ground after applying the update.

fields.name: ForceMove
fields.doc: ForceMove specifies whether the client should snap the entity to its new position without interpolation.

fields.name: ForceMoveLocalEntity
fields.doc: ForceMoveLocalEntity specifies whether the client should also snap an entity it owns locally.

fields.name: ForceCompletion
fields.doc:
ForceCompletion specifies whether the client should complete any in-progress local movement before applying the
update.

fields.name: Ticks
fields.doc: Ticks is the number of ticks over which the movement should be interpolated by the client.

types.name: packet.MovePlayer
types.doc:
MovePlayer is sent by players to send their movement to the server, and by the server to update the
movement of player entities to other players.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position to spawn the player on. If the player is on a distance that the viewer cannot
see it, the player will still show up if the viewer moves closer.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc:
Pitch is the vertical rotation of the player. Facing straight forward yields a pitch of 0. Pitch is
measured in degrees.

fields.name: Yaw
fields.doc: Yaw is the horizontal rotation of the player. Yaw is also measured in degrees.

fields.name: HeadYaw
fields.doc:
HeadYaw is the same as Yaw, except that it applies specifically to the head of the player. A different
value for HeadYaw than Yaw means that the player will have its head turned.

fields.name: Mode
fields.doc:
Mode is the mode of the movement. It specifies the way the player's movement should be shown to other
players. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: OnGround
fields.doc:
OnGround specifies if the player is considered on the ground. Note that proxies or hacked clients could
fake this to always be true, so it should not be taken for granted.

fields.name: RiddenEntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
RiddenEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity that the player might currently be riding. If not
riding, this should be left 0.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

types.name: packet.MovementEffect
types.doc:
MovementEffect is sent by the server to the client to update specific movement effects to allow the client
to predict its movement. For example, fireworks used during gliding will send this packet to tell the
client the exact duration of the boost.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the type of movement effect being updated. It is one of the constants found above.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Duration is the duration of the effect, measured in ticks.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

types.name: packet.MultiPlayerSettings
types.doc:
MultiPlayerSettings is sent by the client to update multi-player related settings server-side and sent back
to online players by the server.
The MultiPlayerSettings packet is a Minecraft: Education Edition packet. It has no functionality for the
base game.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the action that should be done when this packet is sent. It is one of the constants that
may be found above.

types.name: packet.NPCDialogue
types.doc: NPCDialogue is a packet that allows the client to display dialog boxes for interacting with NPCs.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc: EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the NPC being requested.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc: ActionType is the type of action for the packet.

fields.name: Dialogue
fields.doc: Dialogue is the text that the client should see.

fields.name: SceneName
fields.doc:
SceneName is the identifier of the scene. If this is left empty, the client will use the last scene sent to it.
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/minecraft/creator/documents/npcdialogue.

fields.name: NPCName
fields.doc: NPCName is the name of the NPC to be displayed to the client.

fields.name: ActionJSON
fields.doc: ActionJSON is the JSON string of the buttons/actions the server can perform.

types.name: packet.NPCRequest
types.doc:
NPCRequest is sent by the client when it interacts with an NPC.
The packet is specifically made for Education Edition, where NPCs are available to use.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the NPC entity that the player interacted with. It is the same
as sent by the server when spawning the entity.

fields.name: RequestType
fields.doc:
RequestType is the type of the request, which depends on the permission that the player has. It will
be either a type that indicates that the NPC should show its dialog, or that it should open the
editing window.

fields.name: CommandString
fields.doc:
CommandString is the command string set in the NPC. It may consist of multiple commands, depending on
what the player set in it.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc: ActionType is the type of the action to execute.

fields.name: SceneName
fields.doc:
SceneName is the name of the scene. This can be left empty to specify the last scene that the player
was sent.

types.name: packet.NetworkChunkPublisherUpdate
types.doc:
NetworkChunkPublisherUpdate is sent by the server to change the point around which chunks are and remain
loaded. This is useful for mini-game servers, where only one area is ever loaded, in which case the
NetworkChunkPublisherUpdate packet can be sent in the middle of it, so that no chunks ever need to be
additionally sent during the course of the game.
In reality, the packet is not extraordinarily useful, and most servers just send it constantly at the
position of the player.
If the packet is not sent at all, no chunks will be shown to the player, regardless of where they are sent.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the block position around which chunks loaded will remain shown to the client. Most servers
set this position to the position of the player itself.

fields.name: Radius
fields.doc:
Radius is the radius in blocks around Position that chunks sent show up in and will remain loaded in.
Unlike the RequestChunkRadius and ChunkRadiusUpdated packets, this radius is in blocks rather than
chunks, so the chunk radius needs to be multiplied by 16. (Or shifted to the left by 4.)

fields.name: SavedChunks
fields.doc:
SavedChunks ...
TODO: Figure out what this field is used for.

reason.value: saved chunks exceeds maximum length of 9216 chunk positions

types.name: packet.NetworkSettings
types.doc:
NetworkSettings is sent by the server to update a variety of network settings. These settings modify the
way packets are sent over the network stack.

fields.name: CompressionThreshold
fields.doc:
CompressionThreshold is the minimum size of a packet that is compressed when sent. If the size of a
packet is under this value, it is not compressed.
When set to 0, all packets will be left uncompressed.

fields.name: CompressionAlgorithm
fields.doc: CompressionAlgorithm is the algorithm that is used to compress packets.

fields.name: ClientThrottle
fields.doc:
ClientThrottle regulates whether the client should throttle players when exceeding of the threshold. Players
outside threshold will not be ticked, improving performance on low-end devices.

fields.name: ClientThrottleThreshold
fields.doc:
ClientThrottleThreshold is the threshold for client throttling. If the number of players exceeds this value, the
client will throttle players.

fields.name: ClientThrottleScalar
fields.doc:
ClientThrottleScalar is the scalar for client throttling. The scalar is the amount of players that are ticked
when throttling is enabled.

types.name: packet.NetworkStackLatency
types.doc:
NetworkStackLatency is sent by the server (and the client, on development builds) to measure the latency
over the entire Minecraft stack, rather than the RakNet latency. It has other usages too, such as the
ability to be used as some kind of acknowledgement packet, to know when the client has received a certain
other packet.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.doc:
Timestamp is the timestamp of the network stack latency packet. The client will, if NeedsResponse is
set to true, send a NetworkStackLatency packet with this same timestamp packet in response.

fields.name: NeedsResponse
fields.doc:
NeedsResponse specifies if the sending side of this packet wants a response to the packet, meaning that
the other side should send a NetworkStackLatency packet back.

types.name: packet.OnScreenTextureAnimation
types.doc:
OnScreenTextureAnimation is sent by the server to show a certain animation on the screen of the player.
The packet is used, as an example, for when a raid is triggered and when a raid is defeated.

fields.name: AnimationType
fields.doc:
AnimationType is the type of the animation to show. The packet provides no further extra data to allow
modifying the duration or other properties of the animation.

types.name: packet.OpenSign
types.doc:
OpenSign is sent by the server to open a sign for editing. As of 1.19.80, the player can interact with a sign to edit
the text on both sides instead of just the front.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the sign to edit. The client uses this position to get the data of the sign, including
the existing text and formatting etc.

fields.name: FrontSide
fields.doc:
FrontSide dictates whether the front side of the sign should be opened for editing. If false, the back side is
assumed to be edited.

types.name: packet.PacketViolationWarning
types.doc:
PacketViolationWarning is sent by the client when it receives an invalid packet from the server. It holds
some information on the error that occurred.
noinspection GoNameStartsWithPackageName

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the type of violation. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: Severity
fields.doc:
Severity specifies the severity of the packet violation. The action the client takes after this
violation depends on the severity sent.

fields.name: PacketID
fields.doc: PacketID is the ID of the invalid packet that was received.

fields.name: ViolationContext
fields.doc: ViolationContext holds a description on the violation of the packet.

types.name: packet.PartyChanged
types.doc: PartyChanged is sent by the client to the server to indicate that the player's party ID has changed.

types.name: packet.PartyDestinationCookieResponse
types.doc:
PartyDestinationCookieResponse is sent by the client to the server in response to a
SendPartyDestinationCookie packet.

fields.name: Cookie
fields.doc: Cookie is the opaque party destination cookie echoed back from the SendPartyDestinationCookie packet.

fields.name: Accepted
fields.doc: Accepted is true if the client accepted the party destination.

types.name: packet.PartyInfo
types.doc: PartyInfo represents the information of the client's role in a party.

fields.name: PartyID
fields.doc: PartyID is the party identifier.

fields.name: PartyLeader
fields.doc: PartyLeader is if the client is the new party leader or not.

types.name: packet.PhotoInfoRequest
types.doc:
PhotoInfoRequest is sent by the client to request photo information from the server.

Deprecated: This packet was deprecated in 1.19.80.

fields.name: PhotoID
fields.doc: PhotoID is the ID of the photo.

types.name: packet.PhotoTransfer
types.doc:
PhotoTransfer is sent by the server to transfer a photo (image) file to the client. It is typically used
to transfer photos so that the client can display it in a portfolio in Education Edition.
While previously usable in the default Bedrock Edition, the displaying of photos in books was disabled and
the packet now has little use anymore.

fields.name: PhotoName
fields.doc:
PhotoName is the name of the photo to transfer. It is the exact file name that the client will download
the photo as, including the extension of the file.

fields.name: PhotoData
fields.doc:
PhotoData is the raw data of the photo image. The format of this data may vary: Formats such as JPEG or
PNG work, as long as PhotoName has the correct extension.

fields.name: BookID
fields.doc:
BookID is the ID of the book that the photo is associated with. If the PhotoName in a book with this ID
is set to PhotoName, it will display the photo (provided Education Edition is used).
The photo image is downloaded to a sub-folder with this book ID.

fields.name: PhotoType
fields.doc: PhotoType is one of the three photo types above.

fields.name: SourceType
fields.doc: SourceType is the source photo type. It is one of the three photo types above.

fields.name: OwnerEntityUniqueID
fields.doc: OwnerEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the photo's owner.

fields.name: NewPhotoName
fields.doc: NewPhotoName is the new name of the photo.

types.name: packet.PlaySound
types.doc:
PlaySound is sent by the server to play a sound to the client. Some of the sounds may only be started using
this packet and must be stopped using the StopSound packet.

fields.name: SoundName
fields.doc: SoundName is the name of the sound to play.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position at which the sound was played. Some sounds do not depend on a position,
which will then ignore it, but most of them will play with the direction based on the position compared
to the player's position.

fields.name: Volume
fields.doc:
Volume is the relative volume of the sound to play. It will be less loud for the player if it is
farther away from the position of the sound.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc:
Pitch is the pitch of the sound to play. Some sounds completely ignore this field, whereas others use
it to specify the pitch as the field is intended.

fields.name: LoopCount
fields.doc: LoopCount is the number of times to loop the sound before stopping. -1 means no looping at all.

fields.name: BypassListenerRangeCheck
fields.doc:
BypassListenerRangeCheck specifies if the sound should be played regardless of how far away the player
is from the position of the sound.

fields.name: Handle
fields.doc:
Handle is an optional sound handle ID. It is currently unknown what this is for, and is not required
to be set by servers.

fields.name: PlaybackPositionSeconds
fields.doc:
PlaybackPositionSeconds is an optional offset, in seconds, into the sound at which playback should
start. If not set, the sound is played from the start.

types.name: packet.PlayStatus
types.doc:
PlayStatus is sent by the server to update a player on the play status. This includes failed statuses due
to a mismatched version, but also success statuses.

fields.name: Status
fields.doc: Status is the status of the packet. It is one of the constants found above.

types.name: packet.PlayerAction
types.doc:
PlayerAction is sent by the client when it executes any action, for example starting to sprint, swim,
starting the breaking of a block, dropping an item, etc.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the ID of the action that was executed by the player. It is one of the constants that may
be found in protocol/player.go.

fields.name: BlockPosition
fields.doc:
BlockPosition is the position of the target block, if the action with the ActionType set concerned a
block. If that is not the case, the block position will be zero.

fields.name: ResultPosition
fields.doc:
ResultPosition is the position of the action's result. When a UseItemOn action is sent, this is the position of
the block clicked, but when a block is placed, this is the position at which the block will be placed.

fields.name: BlockFace
fields.doc:
BlockFace is the face of the target block that was touched. If the action with the ActionType set
concerned a block. If not, the face is always 0.

types.name: packet.PlayerArmourDamage
types.doc:
PlayerArmourDamage is sent by the server to damage the armour of a player. It is a very efficient packet,
but generally it's much easier to just send a slot update for the damaged armour.

fields.name: List
fields.doc: List is a list of armour entries indicating which pieces of armour should receive damage.

types.name: packet.PlayerAuthInput
types.doc:
PlayerAuthInput is sent by the client to allow for server authoritative movement. It is used to synchronise
the player input with the position server-side.
The client sends this packet when the ServerAuthoritativeMovementMode field in the StartGame packet is set
to true, instead of the MovePlayer packet. The client will send this packet once every tick.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc: Pitch and Yaw hold the rotation that the player reports it has.

fields.name: Yaw
fields.doc: Pitch and Yaw hold the rotation that the player reports it has.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position holds the position that the player reports it has.

fields.name: MoveVector
fields.doc:
MoveVector is a Vec2 that specifies the direction in which the player moved, as a combination of X/Z
values which are created using the WASD/controller stick state.

fields.name: HeadYaw
fields.doc: HeadYaw is the horizontal rotation of the head that the player reports it has.

fields.name: InputData
fields.doc:
InputData is the set of input flags that together specify the way the player moved last tick. It holds
the flags above.

fields.name: InputMode
fields.doc:
InputMode specifies the way that the client inputs data to the screen. It is one of the constants that
may be found above.

fields.name: PlayMode
fields.doc:
PlayMode specifies the way that the player is playing. The values it holds, which are rather random,
may be found above.

fields.name: InteractionModel
fields.doc:
InteractionModel is a constant representing the interaction model the player is using. It is one of the
constants that may be found above.

fields.name: InteractPitch
fields.doc:
InteractPitch and interactYaw is the rotation the player is looking that they intend to use for
interactions. This is only different to Pitch and Yaw in cases such as VR or when custom cameras
being used.

fields.name: InteractYaw
fields.doc:
InteractPitch and interactYaw is the rotation the player is looking that they intend to use for
interactions. This is only different to Pitch and Yaw in cases such as VR or when custom cameras
being used.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc:
Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to
CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

fields.name: Delta
fields.doc:
Delta was the delta between the old and the new position. There isn't any practical use for this field
as it can be calculated by the server itself.

fields.name: ItemInteractionData
fields.doc: ItemInteractionData is the transaction data if the InputData includes an item interaction.

fields.name: ItemStackRequest
fields.doc: ItemStackRequest is sent by the client to change an item in their inventory.

fields.name: BlockActions
fields.doc: BlockActions is a slice of block actions that the client has interacted with.

fields.name: VehicleRotation
fields.doc: VehicleRotation is the rotation of the vehicle that the player is in, if any.

fields.name: ClientPredictedVehicle
fields.doc: ClientPredictedVehicle is the unique ID of the vehicle that the client predicts the player to be in.

fields.name: AnalogueMoveVector
fields.doc:
AnalogueMoveVector is a Vec2 that specifies the direction in which the player moved, as a combination
of X/Z values which are created using an analogue input.

fields.name: CameraOrientation
fields.doc:
CameraOrientation is the vector that represents the camera's forward direction which can be used to
transform movement to be camera relative.

fields.name: RawMoveVector
fields.doc:
RawMoveVector is the value of MoveVector before it is affected by input permissions, sneaking/fly
speeds and isn't normalised for analogue inputs.

types.name: packet.PlayerEnchantOptions
types.doc:
PlayerEnchantOptions is sent by the server to update the enchantment options displayed when the user opens
the enchantment table and puts an item in. This packet was added in 1.16 and allows the server to decide on
the enchantments that can be selected by the player.
The PlayerEnchantOptions packet should be sent once for every slot update of the enchantment table. The
vanilla server sends an empty PlayerEnchantOptions packet when the player opens the enchantment table
(air is present in the enchantment table slot) and sends the packet with actual enchantments in it when
items are put in that can have enchantments.

fields.name: Options
fields.doc: Options is a list of possible enchantment options for the item that was put into the enchantment table.

types.name: packet.PlayerFog
types.doc:
PlayerFog is sent by the server to render the different fogs in the Stack. The types of fog are controlled
by resource packs to change how they are rendered, and the ability to create custom fog.

fields.name: Stack
fields.doc:
Stack is a list of fog identifiers to be sent to the client. Examples of fog identifiers are
"minecraft:fog_ocean" and "minecraft:fog_hell".

types.name: packet.PlayerHotBar
types.doc:
PlayerHotBar is sent by the server to the client. It used to be used to link hot bar slots of the player to
actual slots in the inventory, but as of 1.2, this was changed and hot bar slots are no longer a free
floating part of the inventory.
Since 1.2, the packet has been re-purposed, but its new functionality is not clear.

fields.name: SelectedHotBarSlot
fields.doc: SelectedHotBarSlot ...

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc: WindowID ...

fields.name: SelectHotBarSlot
fields.doc: SelectHotBarSlot ...

types.name: packet.PlayerList
types.doc:
PlayerList is sent by the server to update the client-side player list in the in-game menu screen. It shows
the icon of each player if the correct XUID is written in the packet.
Sending the PlayerList packet is obligatory when sending an AddPlayer packet. The added player will not
show up to a client if it has not been added to the player list, because several properties of the player
are obtained from the player list, such as the skin.

fields.name: Entries
fields.doc:
Entries is a list of all player list entries that should be added/removed from the player list,
depending on the ActionType set.

types.name: packet.PlayerLocation
types.doc:
PlayerLocation is sent by the server to the client to either update a player's position on the locator bar,
or remove them completely. The client will determine how to render the player on the locator bar based on
their own distance to Position.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the action that is being performed. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the player to be used on the locator bar. This is only set when the Type is
PlayerLocationTypeCoordinates.

types.name: packet.PlayerSkin
types.doc:
PlayerSkin is sent by the client to the server when it updates its own skin using the in-game skin picker.
It is relayed by the server, or sent if the server changes the skin of a player on its own accord. Note
that the packet can only be sent for players that are in the player list at the time of sending.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc:
UUID is the UUID of the player as sent in the Login packet when the client joined the server. It must
match this UUID exactly for the skin to show up on the player.

fields.name: Skin
fields.doc:
Skin is the new skin to be applied on the player with the UUID in the field above. The skin, including
its animations, will be shown after sending it.

fields.name: NewSkinName
fields.doc: NewSkinName no longer has a function: The field can be left empty at all times.

fields.name: OldSkinName
fields.doc: OldSkinName no longer has a function: The field can be left empty at all times.

types.name: packet.PlayerToggleCrafterSlotRequest
types.doc: PlayerToggleCrafterSlotRequest is sent by the client when it tries to toggle the state of a slot within a Crafter.

fields.name: PosX
fields.doc: PosX is the X position of the Crafter that is being modified.

fields.name: PosY
fields.doc: PosY is the Y position of the Crafter that is being modified.

fields.name: PosZ
fields.doc: PosZ is the Z position of the Crafter that is being modified.

fields.name: Slot
fields.doc: Slot is the index of the slot that was toggled. This should be a value between 0 and 8.

fields.name: Disabled
fields.doc: Disabled is the new state of the slot. If true, the slot is disabled, if false, the slot is enabled.

types.name: packet.PlayerUpdateEntityOverrides
types.doc: PlayerUpdateEntityOverrides is sent by the server to modify an entity's properties individually.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

fields.name: PropertyIndex
fields.doc: PropertyIndex is the index of the property to modify. The index is unique for each property of an entity.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the type of action to perform with the property. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: IntValue
fields.doc:
IntValue is the new integer value of the property. It is only used when Type is set to
PlayerUpdateEntityOverridesTypeInt.

fields.name: FloatValue
fields.doc:
FloatValue is the new float value of the property. It is only used when Type is set to
PlayerUpdateEntityOverridesTypeFloat.

types.name: packet.PlayerVideoCapture
types.doc:
PlayerVideoCapture packet is sent by the server to start or stop video recording for a player. This packet
only works on development builds and has no effect on retail builds. When recording, the client will save
individual frames to '/LocalCache/minecraftpe' in the format specified below.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is the action to perform with the video capture. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: FrameRate
fields.doc:
FrameRate is the frame rate at which the video should be recorded. It is only used when Action is
PlayerVideoCaptureActionStart. A higher frame rate will cause more frames to be recorded, but also
a noticeable increase in lag.

fields.name: FilePrefix
fields.doc:
FilePrefix is the prefix of the file name that will be used to save the frames. The frames will be saved
in the format 'FilePrefix%d.png' where %d is the frame index.

types.name: packet.PositionTrackingDBClientRequest
types.doc:
PositionTrackingDBClientRequest is a packet sent by the client to request the position and dimension of a
'tracking ID'. These IDs are tracked in a database by the server. In 1.16, this is used for lodestones.
The client will send this request to find the position a lodestone compass needs to point to. If found, it
will point to the lodestone. If not, it will start spinning around.
A PositionTrackingDBServerBroadcast packet should be sent in response to this packet.

fields.name: RequestAction
fields.doc:
RequestAction is the action that should be performed upon the receiving of the packet. It is one of the
constants found above.

fields.name: TrackingID
fields.doc:
TrackingID is a unique ID used to identify the request. The server responds with a
PositionTrackingDBServerBroadcast packet holding the same ID, so that the client can find out what that
packet was in response to.

types.name: packet.PositionTrackingDBServerBroadcast
types.doc:
PositionTrackingDBServerBroadcast is sent by the server in response to the
PositionTrackingDBClientRequest packet. This packet is, as of 1.16, currently only used for lodestones. The
server maintains a database with tracking IDs and their position and dimension. The client will request
these tracking IDs, (NBT tag set on the lodestone compass with the tracking ID?) and the server will
respond with the status of those tracking IDs.
What is actually done with the data sent depends on what the client chooses to do with it. For the
lodestone compass, it is used to make the compass point towards lodestones and to make it spin if the
lodestone at a position is no longer there.

fields.name: BroadcastAction
fields.doc:
BroadcastAction specifies the status of the position tracking DB response. It is one of the constants
above, specifying the result of the request with the ID below.
The Update action is sent for setting the position of a lodestone compass, the Destroy and NotFound to
indicate that there is not (no longer) a lodestone at that position.

fields.name: TrackingID
fields.doc:
TrackingID is the ID of the PositionTrackingDBClientRequest packet that this packet was in response to.
The tracking ID is also present as the 'id' field in the SerialisedData field.

fields.name: Payload

types.name: packet.PrimitiveShapes
types.doc:
PrimitiveShapes is a packet sent by the server to instruct the client to render one or more shapes in the world.
Shapes can be added, removed or updated based on the data provided individually.

fields.name: Shapes
fields.doc: Shapes is a list of shapes to draw on the client-side.

types.name: packet.PurchaseReceipt
types.doc:
PurchaseReceipt is sent by the client to the server to notify the server it purchased an item from the
Marketplace store that was offered by the server. The packet is only used for partnered servers.

fields.name: Receipts
fields.doc:
Receipts is a list of receipts, or proofs of purchases, for the offers that have been purchased by the
player.

types.name: packet.RecordStarted
types.doc:
RecordStarted is sent by the server to notify the client that a record started playing at a specific block
position, such as when a music disc is inserted into a jukebox.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position of the block that the record started playing at.

fields.name: Handle
fields.doc:
Handle is the server-side handle of the sound that the record is played through. It may be used in the
ClientboundUpdateSoundData packet to update the sound afterwards.

types.name: packet.RefreshEntitlements
types.doc: RefreshEntitlements is sent by the client to the server to refresh the entitlements of the player.

types.name: packet.RemoveActor
types.doc:
RemoveActor is sent by the server to remove an entity that currently exists in the world from the client-
side. Sending this packet if the client cannot already see this entity will have no effect.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity to be removed. The unique ID is a value that remains
consistent across different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID
of the entity out for this field.

types.name: packet.RemoveObjective
types.doc:
RemoveObjective is sent by the server to remove a scoreboard objective. It is used to stop showing a
scoreboard to a player.

fields.name: ObjectiveName
fields.doc:
ObjectiveName is the name of the objective that the scoreboard currently active has. This name must
be identical to the one sent in the SetDisplayObjective packet.

types.name: packet.RemoveVolumeEntity
types.doc: RemoveVolumeEntity indicates a volume entity to be removed from server to client.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc: EntityRuntimeID ...

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc: Dimension ...

types.name: packet.RequestAbility
types.doc:
RequestAbility is a packet sent by the client to the server to request permission for a specific ability from the
server. These abilities are defined above.

fields.name: Ability
fields.doc:
Ability is the ability that the client is requesting. This is one of the constants defined in the
protocol/ability.go file.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc:
Value represents the value of the ability. This can either be a boolean or a float32, otherwise the writer/reader
will panic.

types.name: packet.RequestChunkRadius
types.doc:
RequestChunkRadius is sent by the client to the server to update the server on the chunk view radius that
it has set in the settings. The server may respond with a ChunkRadiusUpdated packet with either the chunk
radius requested, or a different chunk radius if the server chooses so.

fields.name: ChunkRadius
fields.doc:
ChunkRadius is the requested chunk radius. This value is always the value set in the settings of the
player.

fields.name: MaxChunkRadius
fields.doc:
MaxChunkRadius is the maximum chunk radius that the player wants to receive. The reason for the client sending this
is currently unknown.

types.name: packet.RequestNetworkSettings
types.doc: RequestNetworkSettings is sent by the client to request network settings, such as compression, from the server.

fields.name: ClientProtocol
fields.doc:
ClientProtocol is the protocol version of the player. The player is disconnected if the protocol is
incompatible with the protocol of the server.

types.name: packet.RequestPermissions
types.doc:
RequestPermissions is a packet sent from the client to the server to request permissions that the client does not
currently have. It can only be sent by operators and host in vanilla Minecraft.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the player. The unique ID is unique for the entire world and is
often used in packets. Most servers send an EntityUniqueID equal to the EntityRuntimeID.

fields.name: PermissionLevel
fields.doc:
PermissionLevel is the current permission level of the player. This is one of the constants that may be found
in the AdventureSettings packet.

fields.name: RequestedPermissions
fields.doc: RequestedPermissions contains the requested permission flags.

types.name: packet.ResourcePackChunkData
types.doc:
ResourcePackChunkData is sent to the client so that the client can download the resource pack. Each packet
holds a chunk of the compressed resource pack, of which the size is defined in the ResourcePackDataInfo
packet sent before.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc: UUID is the unique ID of the resource pack that the chunk of data is taken out of.

fields.name: ChunkIndex
fields.doc:
ChunkIndex is the current chunk index of the chunk. It is a number that starts at 0 and is incremented
for each resource pack data chunk sent to the client.

fields.name: DataOffset
fields.doc:
DataOffset is the current progress in bytes or offset in the data that the resource pack data chunk is
taken from.

fields.name: Data
fields.doc:
RawPayload is a byte slice containing a chunk of data from the resource pack. It must be of the same size or
less than the DataChunkSize set in the ResourcePackDataInfo packet.

types.name: packet.ResourcePackChunkRequest
types.doc:
ResourcePackChunkRequest is sent by the client to request a chunk of data from a particular resource pack,
that it has obtained information about in a ResourcePackDataInfo packet.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc: UUID is the unique ID of the resource pack that the chunk of data is requested from.

fields.name: ChunkIndex
fields.doc:
ChunkIndex is the requested chunk index of the chunk. It is a number that starts at 0 and is
incremented for each resource pack data chunk requested.

types.name: packet.ResourcePackClientResponse
types.doc:
ResourcePackClientResponse is sent by the client in response to resource packets sent by the server. It is
used to let the server know what action needs to be taken for the client to have all resource packs ready
and set.

fields.name: Response
fields.doc: Response is the response type of the response. It is one of the constants found above.

fields.name: PacksToDownload
fields.doc:
PacksToDownload is a list of resource pack UUIDs combined with their version that need to be downloaded
(for example SomePack_1.0.0), if the Response field is PackResponseSendPacks.

types.name: packet.ResourcePackDataInfo
types.doc:
ResourcePackDataInfo is sent by the server to the client to inform the client about the data contained in
one of the resource packs that are about to be sent.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc: UUID is the unique ID of the resource pack that the info concerns.

fields.name: DataChunkSize
fields.doc:
DataChunkSize is the maximum size in bytes of the chunks in which the total size of the resource pack
to be sent will be divided. A size of 1MB (1024*1024) means that a resource pack of 15.5MB will be
split into 16 data chunks.

fields.name: ChunkCount
fields.doc:
ChunkCount is the total amount of data chunks that the sent resource pack will exist out of. It is the
total size of the resource pack divided by the DataChunkSize field.
The client doesn't actually seem to use this field. Rather, it divides the size by the chunk size to
calculate it itself.

fields.name: Size
fields.doc:
Size is the total size in bytes that the resource pack occupies. This is the size of the compressed
archive (zip) of the resource pack.

fields.name: Hash
fields.doc: Hash is a SHA256 hash of the content of the resource pack.

fields.name: Premium
fields.doc:
Premium specifies if the resource pack was a premium resource pack, meaning it was bought from the
Minecraft store.

fields.name: PackType
fields.doc:
PackType is the type of the resource pack. It is one of the resource pack types that may be found in
the constants above.

types.name: packet.ResourcePackStack
types.doc:
ResourcePackStack is sent by the server to send the order in which resource packs and behaviour packs
should be applied (and downloaded) by the client.

fields.name: TexturePackRequired
fields.doc:
TexturePackRequired specifies if the client must accept the texture packs the server has in order to
join the server. If set to true, the client gets the option to either download the resource packs and
join, or quit entirely. Behaviour packs never have to be downloaded.

fields.name: TexturePacks
fields.doc:
TexturePacks is a list of texture packs that the client needs to download before joining the server.
The order of these texture packs specifies the order that they are applied in on the client side. The
first in the list will be applied first.

fields.name: BaseGameVersion
fields.doc: BaseGameVersion is the vanilla version that the client should set its resource pack stack to.

fields.name: Experiments
fields.doc:
Experiments holds a list of experiments that are either enabled or disabled in the world that the
player spawns in.
It is not clear why experiments are sent both here and in the StartGame packet.

fields.name: ExperimentsPreviouslyToggled
fields.doc:
ExperimentsPreviouslyToggled specifies if any experiments were previously toggled in this world. It is
probably used for some kind of metrics.

fields.name: IncludeEditorPacks
fields.doc:
IncludeEditorPacks specifies if vanilla editor packs should be included in the resource pack stack when
connecting to an editor world.

types.name: packet.ResourcePacksInfo
types.doc:
ResourcePacksInfo is sent by the server to inform the client on what resource packs the server has. It
sends a list of the resource packs it has and basic information on them like the version and description.

fields.name: TexturePackRequired
fields.doc:
TexturePackRequired specifies if the client must accept the texture packs the server has in order to
join the server. If set to true, the client gets the option to either download the resource packs and
join, or quit entirely. Behaviour packs never have to be downloaded.

fields.name: HasAddons
fields.doc:
HasAddons specifies if any of the resource packs contain addons in them. If set to true, only clients
that support addons will be able to download them.

fields.name: HasScripts
fields.doc:
HasScripts specifies if any of the resource packs contain scripts in them. If set to true, only clients
that support scripts will be able to download them.

fields.name: ForceDisableVibrantVisuals
fields.doc:
ForceDisableVibrantVisuals specifies if the vibrant visuals feature should be forcibly disabled on the server.
If set to true, the server will ensure that vibrant visuals are not enabled, regardless of the client's settings.

fields.name: WorldTemplateUUID
fields.doc:
WorldTemplateUUID is the UUID of the template that has been used to generate the world. Templates can
be downloaded from the marketplace or installed via '.mctemplate' files. If the world was not generated
from a template, this field is empty.

fields.name: WorldTemplateVersion
fields.doc:
WorldTemplateVersion is the version of the world template that has been used to generate the world. If
the world was not generated from a template, this field is empty.

fields.name: TexturePacks
fields.doc:
TexturePacks is a list of texture packs that the client needs to download before joining the server.
The order of these texture packs is not relevant in this packet. It is however important in the
ResourcePackStack packet.

types.name: packet.ResourcePacksReadyForValidation
types.doc:
ResourcePacksReadyForValidation is sent by the client to inform the server that the client has finished
loading resource packs and is ready for validation.

types.name: packet.Respawn
types.doc:
Respawn is sent by the server to make a player respawn client-side. It is sent in response to a
PlayerAction packet with ActionType PlayerActionRespawn.
As of 1.13, the server sends two of these packets with different states, and the client sends one of these
back in order to complete the respawn.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position on which the player should be respawned. The position might be in a different
dimension, in which case the client should first be sent a ChangeDimension packet.

fields.name: State
fields.doc:
State is the 'state' of the respawn. It is one of the constants that may be found above, and the value
the packet contains depends on whether the server or client sends it.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID of the player that the respawn packet concerns. This is
apparently for the server to recognise which player sends this packet.

types.name: packet.ScriptCustomEvent
types.doc:
ScriptCustomEvent is sent by both the client and the server. It is a way to let scripts communicate with
the server, so that the client can let the server know it triggered an event, or the other way around.
ScriptCustomEvent is deprecated as of 1.20.10.

fields.name: EventName
fields.doc:
EventName is the name of the event. The script and the server will use this event name to identify the
data that is sent.

fields.name: EventData
fields.doc:
EventData is the data of the event. This data is typically a JSON encoded string, that the script is
able to encode and decode too.

types.name: packet.ScriptMessage
types.doc:
ScriptMessage is used to communicate custom messages from the client to the server, or from the server to the client.
While the name may suggest this packet is used for the discontinued scripting API, it is likely instead for the
GameTest framework.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.doc: Identifier is the identifier of the message, used by either party to identify the message data sent.

fields.name: Data
fields.doc: Data contains the data of the message.

types.name: packet.SendPartyDestinationCookie
types.doc: SendPartyDestinationCookie is sent by the server to a client with a party destination cookie.

fields.name: Cookie
fields.doc: Cookie is the opaque party destination cookie.

fields.name: Intent
fields.doc: Intent is the intent of the cookie. It is one of the PartyDestinationCookieIntent constants.

fields.name: DestinationName
fields.doc: DestinationName is the name of the destination the cookie refers to.

types.name: packet.ServerBoundDataDrivenScreenClosed
types.doc: ServerBoundDataDrivenScreenClosed is sent by the client when a data-driven UI screen is closed.

fields.name: FormID
fields.doc: FormID is the unique instance ID of the form that was closed.

fields.name: CloseReason
fields.doc: CloseReason is the reason the screen was closed. It is one of the DataDrivenScreenCloseReason constants.

types.name: packet.ServerBoundDataStore
types.doc: ServerBoundDataStore is sent by the client to update a data store property on the server.

fields.name: Update
fields.doc: Update contains the data store update.

types.name: packet.ServerBoundDiagnostics
types.doc:
ServerBoundDiagnostics is sent by the client to tell the server about the performance diagnostics
of the client. It is sent by the client roughly every 500ms or 10 in-game ticks when the
"Creator > Enable Client Diagnostics" setting is enabled.

fields.name: AverageFramesPerSecond
fields.doc:
AverageFramesPerSecond is the average amount of frames per second that the client has been
running at.

fields.name: AverageServerSimTickTime
fields.doc:
AverageServerSimTickTime is the average time that the server spends simulating a single tick
in milliseconds.

fields.name: AverageClientSimTickTime
fields.doc:
AverageClientSimTickTime is the average time that the client spends simulating a single tick
in milliseconds.

fields.name: AverageBeginFrameTime
fields.doc:
AverageBeginFrameTime is the average time that the client spends beginning a frame in
milliseconds.

fields.name: AverageInputTime
fields.doc: AverageInputTime is the average time that the client spends processing input in milliseconds.

fields.name: AverageRenderTime
fields.doc: AverageRenderTime is the average time that the client spends rendering in milliseconds.

fields.name: AverageEndFrameTime
fields.doc: AverageEndFrameTime is the average time that the client spends ending a frame in milliseconds.

fields.name: AverageRemainderTimePercent
fields.doc:
AverageRemainderTimePercent is the average percentage of time that the client spends on
tasks that are not accounted for.

fields.name: AverageUnaccountedTimePercent
fields.doc:
AverageUnaccountedTimePercent is the average percentage of time that the client spends on
unaccounted tasks.

fields.name: MemoryCategoryValues
fields.doc: MemoryCategoryValues is a list of memory category counters sent by the client.

fields.name: EntityDiagnostics
fields.doc: EntityDiagnostics is a list of entity timing entries sent by the client.

fields.name: SystemDiagnostics
fields.doc: SystemDiagnostics is a list of system timing entries sent by the client.

fields.name: SystemCategories
fields.doc: SystemCategories maps diagnostics category names to system indices.

fields.name: WhiskerScopes
fields.doc: WhiskerScopes is a list of whisker profiler scope diagnostic summaries sent by the client.

types.name: packet.ServerBoundLoadingScreen
types.doc:
ServerBoundLoadingScreen is sent by the client to tell the server about the state of the loading
screen that the client is currently displaying.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the type of the loading screen event. It is one of the constants that may be found above.

fields.name: LoadingScreenID
fields.doc:
LoadingScreenID is the ID of the screen that was previously sent by the server in the ChangeDimension
packet. The server should validate that the ID matches the last one it sent.

types.name: packet.ServerBoundPackSettingChange
types.doc:
ServerBoundPackSettingChange is sent by the client to the server when it changes a setting
for a specific pack in the pack settings UI.

fields.name: PackID
fields.doc: PackID is the UUID of the pack.

fields.name: PackSetting
fields.doc: PackSetting is the new setting value applied to the pack.

types.name: packet.ServerPlayerPostMovePosition
types.doc: ServerPlayerPostMovePosition is sent by the server with the player's position after movement processing.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the player's position after the server has processed movement.

types.name: packet.ServerPresenceInfo
types.doc: ServerPresenceInfo is sent by the server to provide the client with presence info.

fields.name: PresenceInfo
fields.doc: PresenceInfo is the presence info to set, or nothing to fall back to the default.

types.name: packet.ServerSettingsRequest
types.doc:
ServerSettingsRequest is sent by the client to request the settings specific to the server. These settings
are shown in a separate tab client-side, and have the same structure as a custom form.

types.name: packet.ServerSettingsResponse
types.doc:
ServerSettingsResponse is optionally sent by the server in response to a ServerSettingsRequest from the
client. It is structured the same as a ModalFormRequest packet, and if filled out correctly, will show
a specific tab for the server in the settings of the client. A ModalFormResponse packet is sent by the
client in response to a ServerSettingsResponse, when the client fills out the settings and closes the
settings again.

fields.name: FormID
fields.doc:
FormID is an ID used to identify the form. The ID is saved by the client and sent back when the player
submits the form, so that the server can identify which form was submitted.

fields.name: FormData
fields.doc:
FormData is a JSON encoded object of form data. The content of the object differs, depending on the
type of the form sent, which is also set in the JSON.

types.name: packet.ServerStats
types.doc:
ServerStats is a packet sent from the server to the client to update the client on server statistics. It is purely
used for telemetry.

fields.name: ServerTime
fields.doc: ServerTime ...

fields.name: NetworkTime
fields.doc: NetworkTime ...

types.name: packet.ServerStoreInfo
types.doc:
ServerStoreInfo is sent by the server to provide the client with a store entry point. Like the ShowStoreOffer packet,
this only has an effect on partnered servers.

fields.name: StoreInfo
fields.doc: StoreInfo is the store info to set, or nothing to fall back to the default.

types.name: packet.ServerToClientHandshake
types.doc:
ServerToClientHandshake is sent by the server to the client to complete the key exchange in order to
initialise encryption on client and server side. It is followed up by a ClientToServerHandshake packet
from the client.

fields.name: JWT
fields.doc:
JWT is a raw JWT token containing data such as the public key from the server, the algorithm used and
the server's token. It is used for the client to produce a shared secret.

types.name: packet.SetActorData
types.doc:
SetActorData is sent by the server to update the entity metadata of an entity. It includes flags such as
if the entity is on fire, but also properties such as the air it has left until it starts drowning.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: EntityMetadata
fields.doc:
EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in
particular the way the entity looks. Flags include ones such as 'on fire' and 'sprinting'.
The metadata values are indexed by their property key.

fields.name: EntityProperties
fields.doc:
EntityProperties is a list of properties that the entity inhibits. These properties define and alter specific
attributes of the entity.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

types.name: packet.SetActorLink
types.doc:
SetActorLink is sent by the server to initiate an entity link client-side, meaning one entity will start
riding another.

fields.name: EntityLink
fields.doc:
EntityLink is the link to be set client-side. It links two entities together, so that one entity rides
another. Note that players that see those entities later will not see the link, unless it is also sent
in the AddActor and AddPlayer packets.

types.name: packet.SetActorMotion
types.doc:
SetActorMotion is sent by the server to change the client-side velocity of an entity. It is usually used
in combination with server-side movement calculation.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Velocity
fields.doc:
Velocity is the new velocity the entity gets. This velocity will initiate the client-side movement of
the entity.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

types.name: packet.SetCommandsEnabled
types.doc:
SetCommandsEnabled is sent by the server to enable or disable the ability to execute commands for the
client. If disabled, the client itself will stop the execution of commands.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.doc: Enabled defines if the commands should be enabled, or if false, disabled.

types.name: packet.SetDefaultGameType
types.doc:
SetDefaultGameType is sent by the client when it toggles the default game type in the settings UI, and is
sent by the server when it actually changes the default game type, resulting in the toggle being changed
in the settings UI.

fields.name: GameType
fields.doc:
GameType is the new game type that is set. When sent by the client, this is the requested new default
game type.

types.name: packet.SetDifficulty
types.doc:
SetDifficulty is sent by the server to update the client-side difficulty of the client. The actual effect
of this packet on the client isn't very significant, as the difficulty is handled server-side.

fields.name: Difficulty
fields.doc: Difficulty is the new difficulty that the world has.

types.name: packet.SetDisplayObjective
types.doc:
SetDisplayObjective is sent by the server to display an object as a scoreboard to the player. Once sent,
it should be followed up by a SetScore packet to set the lines of the packet.

fields.name: DisplaySlot
fields.doc:
DisplaySlot is the slot in which the scoreboard should be displayed. Available options can be found in
the constants above.

fields.name: ObjectiveName
fields.doc:
ObjectiveName is the name of the objective that the scoreboard displays. Filling out a random unique
value for this field works: It is not displayed in the scoreboard.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.doc: DisplayName is the name, or title, that is displayed at the top of the scoreboard.

fields.name: CriteriaName
fields.doc:
CriteriaName is the name of the criteria that need to be fulfilled in order for the score to be
increased. This can be any kind of string and does not show up client-side.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.doc:
SortOrder is the order in which entries on the scoreboard should be sorted. It is one of the constants
that may be found above.

types.name: packet.SetHealth
types.doc:
SetHealth is sent by the server. It sets the health of the player it is sent to. The SetHealth packet
should no longer be used. Instead, the health attribute should be used so that the health and maximum
health may be changed directly.

fields.name: Health
fields.doc: Health is the new health of the player.

types.name: packet.SetHud
