types.doc: SetHud is sent by the server to set the visibility of individual HUD elements on the client.

fields.name: Elements
fields.doc:
Elements is a list of HUD elements that are being modified. The values can be any of the HudElement
constants above.

fields.name: Visibility
fields.doc:
Visibility represents the new visibility of the specified Elements. It can be any of the HudVisibility
constants above.

types.name: packet.SetLastHurtBy
types.doc:
SetLastHurtBy is sent by the server to let the client know what entity type it was last hurt by. At this
moment, the packet is useless and should not be used. There is no behaviour that depends on if this
packet is sent or not.

fields.name: EntityType
fields.doc: EntityType is the numerical type of the entity that the player was last hurt by.

types.name: packet.SetLocalPlayerAsInitialised
types.doc:
SetLocalPlayerAsInitialised is sent by the client in response to a PlayStatus packet with the status set
to 3. The packet marks the moment at which the client is fully initialised and can receive any packet
without discarding it.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID the player was assigned earlier in the login sequence in the
StartGame packet.

types.name: packet.SetPlayerFurnaceOptions
types.doc:
SetPlayerFurnaceOptions is a bidirectional packet that can be used to update the options a player has
selected in a furnace-like container's UI.

fields.name: FurnaceType
fields.doc:
FurnaceType is the type of furnace that the options apply to. It is one of the FurnaceType constants
above.

fields.name: FurnaceOptions
fields.doc: FurnaceOptions holds the options that the player has selected for the furnace type above.

types.name: packet.SetPlayerGameType
types.doc:
SetPlayerGameType is sent by the server to update the game type, which is otherwise known as the game mode,
of a player.

fields.name: GameType
fields.doc:
GameType is the new game type of the player. It is one of the constants that can be found above. Some
of these game types require additional flags to be set in an AdventureSettings packet for the game mode
to obtain its full functionality.

types.name: packet.SetPlayerInventoryOptions
types.doc: SetPlayerInventoryOptions is a bidirectional packet that can be used to update the inventory options of a player.

fields.name: LeftInventoryTab
fields.doc:
LeftInventoryTab is the tab that is selected on the left side of the inventory. This is usually for the creative
inventory. It is one of the InventoryLeftTab constants above.

fields.name: RightInventoryTab
fields.doc:
RightInventoryTab is the tab that is selected on the right side of the inventory. This is usually for the player's
own inventory. It is one of the InventoryRightTab constants above.

fields.name: Filtering
fields.doc: Filtering is whether the player has enabled the filtering between recipes they have unlocked or not.

fields.name: InventoryLayout
fields.doc: InventoryLayout is the layout of the inventory. It is one of the InventoryLayout constants above.

fields.name: CraftingLayout
fields.doc: CraftingLayout is the layout of the crafting inventory. It is one of the InventoryLayout constants above.

types.name: packet.SetScore
types.doc:
SetScore is sent by the server to send the contents of a scoreboard to the player. It may be used to either
add, remove or edit entries on the scoreboard.

fields.name: Entries
fields.doc:
Entries is a list of all entries that the client should operate on. Each entry's IdentityType specifies
whether it is added, modified or removed.

types.name: packet.SetScoreboardIdentity
types.doc:
SetScoreboardIdentity is sent by the server to change the identity type of one of the entries on a
scoreboard. This is used to change, for example, an entry pointing to a player, to a fake player when it
leaves the server, and to change it back to a real player when it joins again.
In non-vanilla situations, the packet is quite useless.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the action to execute. The action is either ScoreboardIdentityActionRegister
to associate an identity with the entry, or ScoreboardIdentityActionClear to remove associations with
an entity.

fields.name: Entries
fields.doc:
Entries is a list of all entries in the packet. Each of these entries points to one of the entries on
a scoreboard. Depending on ActionType, their identity will either be registered or cleared.

types.name: packet.SetSpawnPosition
types.doc:
SetSpawnPosition is sent by the server to update the spawn position of a player, for example when sleeping
in a bed.

fields.name: SpawnType
fields.doc:
SpawnType is the type of spawn to set. It is either SpawnTypePlayer or SpawnTypeWorld, and specifies
the behaviour of the spawn set. If SpawnTypeWorld is set, the position to which compasses will point is
also changed.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the new position of the spawn that was set. If SpawnType is SpawnTypeWorld, compasses will
point to this position. As of 1.16, Position is always the position of the player.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc:
Dimension is the ID of the dimension that had its spawn updated. This is specifically relevant for
behaviour added in 1.16 such as the respawn anchor, which allows setting the spawn in a specific
dimension.

fields.name: SpawnPosition
fields.doc:
SpawnPosition is a new field added in 1.16. It holds the spawn position of the world. This spawn
position is {-2147483648, -2147483648, -2147483648} for a default spawn position.

types.name: packet.SetTime
types.doc:
SetTime is sent by the server to update the current time client-side. The client actually advances time
client-side by itself, so this packet does not need to be sent each tick. It is merely a means of
synchronising time between server and client.

fields.name: Time
fields.doc:
Time is the current time. The time is not limited to 24000 (time of day), but continues progressing
after that.

types.name: packet.SetTitle
types.doc:
SetTitle is sent by the server to make a title, subtitle or action bar shown to a player. It has several
fields that allow setting the duration of the titles.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the action that should be executed upon the title of a player. It is one of
the constants above and specifies the response of the client to the packet.

fields.name: Text
fields.doc:
Text is the text of the title, which has a different meaning depending on the ActionType that the
packet has. The text is the text of a title, subtitle or action bar, depending on the type set.

fields.name: FadeInDuration
fields.doc:
FadeInDuration is the duration that the title takes to fade in on the screen of the player. It is
measured in 20ths of a second (AKA in ticks).

fields.name: RemainDuration
fields.doc:
RemainDuration is the duration that the title remains on the screen of the player. It is measured in
20ths of a second (AKA in ticks).

fields.name: FadeOutDuration
fields.doc:
FadeOutDuration is the duration that the title takes to fade out of the screen of the player. It is
measured in 20ths of a second (AKA in ticks).

fields.name: XUID
fields.doc:
XUID is the XBOX Live user ID of the player, which will remain consistent as long as the player is
logged in with the XBOX Live account. It is empty if the user is not logged into its XBL account.

fields.name: PlatformOnlineID
fields.doc: PlatformOnlineID is either a uint64 or an empty string.

fields.name: FilteredMessage
fields.doc:
FilteredMessage is a filtered version of Message with all the profanity removed. The client will use
this over Message if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

types.name: packet.SettingsCommand
types.doc:
SettingsCommand is sent by the client when it changes a setting in the settings that results in the issuing
of a command to the server, such as when Show Coordinates is enabled.

fields.name: CommandLine
fields.doc:
CommandLine is the full command line that was sent to the server as a result of the setting that the
client changed.

fields.name: SuppressOutput
fields.doc:
SuppressOutput specifies if the client requests the suppressing of the output of the command that was
executed. Generally this is set to true, as the client won't need a message to confirm the output of
the change.

types.name: packet.ShowCredits
types.doc:
ShowCredits is sent by the server to show the Minecraft credits screen to the client. It is typically sent
when the player beats the ender dragon and leaves the End.

fields.name: PlayerRuntimeID
fields.doc:
PlayerRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID of the player to show the credits to. It's not clear why this
field is actually here in the first place.

fields.name: StatusType
fields.doc:
StatusType is the status type of the credits. It is one of the constants above, and either starts or
stops the credits.

types.name: packet.ShowProfile
types.doc: ShowProfile is sent by the server to show the XBOX Live profile of one player to another.

fields.name: XUID
fields.doc:
XUID is the XBOX Live User ID of the player whose profile should be shown to the player. If it is not
a valid XUID, the client ignores the packet.

types.name: packet.ShowStoreOffer
types.doc:
ShowStoreOffer is sent by the server to show a Marketplace store offer to a player. It opens a window
client-side that displays the item.
The ShowStoreOffer packet only works on the partnered servers: Servers that are not partnered will not have
a store buttons show up in the in-game pause menu and will, as a result, not be able to open store offers
on the client side. Sending the packet does therefore not work when using a proxy that is not connected to
with the domain of one of the partnered servers.

fields.name: OfferID
fields.doc: OfferID is a UUID that identifies the offer for which a window should be opened.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc:
Type is the type of the store offer that is being shown to the player. It is one of the constants that may be
found above.

types.name: packet.SimpleEvent
types.doc:
SimpleEvent is used for enabling or disabling commands and for unlocking world template settings
(both unlocking UI buttons on client and the actual setting on the server).
This is fired from the client to the server and a SetCommandsEnabled is sent back when enabling commands.

fields.name: EventType
fields.doc: EventType is the type of the event to be called. It is one of the constants that may be found above.

types.name: packet.SimulationType
types.doc: SimulationType is an in-progress packet. We currently do not know the use case.

fields.name: SimulationType
fields.doc: SimulationType is the simulation type selected.

types.name: packet.SpawnExperienceOrb
types.doc:
SpawnExperienceOrb is sent by the server to spawn an experience orb entity client-side. Much like the
AddPainting packet, it is one of the few packets that spawn an entity without using the AddActor packet.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position to spawn the experience orb on. If the entity is on a distance that the player
cannot see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

fields.name: ExperienceAmount
fields.doc:
ExperienceAmount is the amount of experience in experience points that the orb carries. The client-side
size of the orb depends on the amount of experience in the orb: There are 11 possible sizes for the
orb, for 1–2, 3–6, 7–16, 17–36, 37–72, 73–148, 149–306, 307–616, 617–1236, 1237–2476, and 2477 and up.

types.name: packet.SpawnParticleEffect
types.doc:
SpawnParticleEffect is sent by the server to spawn a particle effect client-side. Unlike other packets that
result in the appearing of particles, this packet can show particles that are not hardcoded in the client.
They can be added and changed through behaviour packs to implement custom particles.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc:
Dimension is the dimension that the particle is spawned in. Its exact usage is not clear, as the
dimension has no direct effect on the particle.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity that the spawned particle may be attached to. If this ID
is not -1, the Position below will be interpreted as relative to the position of the entity associated
with this unique ID.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position that the particle should be spawned at. If the position is too far away from
the player, it will not show up.
If EntityUniqueID is not -1, the position will be relative to the position of the entity.

fields.name: ParticleName
fields.doc:
ParticleName is the name of the particle that should be shown. This name may point to a particle effect
that is built-in, or to one implemented by behaviour packs.

fields.name: MoLangVariables
fields.doc:
MoLangVariables is an encoded JSON map of MoLang variables that may be applicable to the particle spawn. This can
just be left empty in most cases.

types.name: packet.StartGame
types.doc:
StartGame is sent by the server to send information about the world the player will be spawned in. It
contains information about the position the player spawns in, and information about the world in general
such as its game rules.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the player. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: PlayerGameMode
fields.doc:
PlayerGameMode is the game mode the player currently has. It is a value from 0-4, with 0 being
survival mode, 1 being creative mode, 2 being adventure mode, 3 being survival spectator and 4 being
creative spectator.
This field may be set to 5 to make the client fall back to the game mode set in the WorldGameMode
field.

fields.name: PlayerPosition
fields.doc:
PlayerPosition is the spawn position of the player in the world. In servers this is often the same as
the world's spawn position found below.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc:
Pitch is the vertical rotation of the player. Facing straight forward yields a pitch of 0. Pitch is
measured in degrees.

fields.name: Yaw
fields.doc: Yaw is the horizontal rotation of the player. Yaw is also measured in degrees.

fields.name: WorldSeed
fields.doc:
WorldSeed is the seed used to generate the world. Unlike in PC edition, the seed is a 32bit integer
here.

fields.name: SpawnBiomeType
fields.doc:
SpawnBiomeType specifies if the biome that the player spawns in is user defined (through behaviour
packs) or builtin. See the constants above.

fields.name: UserDefinedBiomeName
fields.doc:
UserDefinedBiomeName is a readable name of the biome that the player spawned in, such as 'plains'. This
might be a custom biome name if any custom biomes are present through behaviour packs.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc:
Dimension is the ID of the dimension that the player spawns in. It is a value from 0-2, with 0 being
the overworld, 1 being the nether and 2 being the end.

fields.name: Generator
fields.doc:
Generator is the generator used for the world. It is a value from 0-4, with 0 being old limited worlds,
1 being infinite worlds, 2 being flat worlds, 3 being nether worlds and 4 being end worlds. A value of
0 will actually make the client stop rendering chunks you send beyond the world limit.

fields.name: WorldGameMode
fields.doc:
WorldGameMode is the game mode that a player gets when it first spawns in the world. It is shown in the
settings and is used if the PlayerGameMode is set to 5.

fields.name: Hardcore
fields.doc: Hardcore is if the world is in hardcore mode. In hardcore mode, the player cannot respawn after dying.

fields.name: Difficulty
fields.doc:
Difficulty is the difficulty of the world. It is a value from 0-3, with 0 being peaceful, 1 being easy,
2 being normal and 3 being hard.

fields.name: WorldSpawn
fields.doc:
WorldSpawn is the block on which the world spawn of the world. This coordinate has no effect on the
place that the client spawns, but it does have an effect on the direction that a compass points.

fields.name: AchievementsDisabled
fields.doc:
AchievementsDisabled defines if achievements are disabled in the world. The client crashes if this
value is set to true while the player's or the world's game mode is creative, and it's recommended to
simply always set this to false as a server.

fields.name: EditorWorldType
fields.doc:
EditorWorldType is a value to dictate the type of editor mode, a special mode recently introduced adding
"powerful tools for editing worlds, intended for experienced creators." It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: CreatedInEditor
fields.doc:
CreatedInEditor is a value to dictate if the world was created as a project in the editor mode. The functionality
of this field is currently unknown.

fields.name: ExportedFromEditor
fields.doc:
ExportedFromEditor is a value to dictate if the world was exported from editor mode. The functionality of this
field is currently unknown.

fields.name: ServerEditorConnectionPolicy
fields.doc: ServerEditorConnectionPolicy controls the editor connection policy.

fields.name: AllowAnonymousBlockDropsInEditorWorlds
fields.doc:
AllowAnonymousBlockDropsInEditorWorlds specifies if anonymous block
drops are allowed in hybrid editor worlds.

fields.name: DayCycleLockTime
fields.doc:
DayCycleLockTime is the time at which the day cycle was locked if the day cycle is disabled using the
respective game rule. The client will maintain this time as long as the day cycle is disabled.

fields.name: EducationEditionOffer
fields.doc:
EducationEditionOffer is some Minecraft: Education Edition field that specifies what 'region' the world
was from, with 0 being None, 1 being RestOfWorld, and 2 being China.
The actual use of this field is unknown.

fields.name: EducationFeaturesEnabled
fields.doc:
EducationFeaturesEnabled specifies if the world has education edition features enabled, such as the
blocks or entities specific to education edition.

fields.name: EducationProductID
fields.doc:
EducationProductID is a UUID used to identify the education edition server instance. It is generally
unique for education edition servers.

fields.name: RainLevel
fields.doc:
RainLevel is the level specifying the intensity of the rain falling. When set to 0, no rain falls at
all.

fields.name: LightningLevel
fields.doc:
LightningLevel is the level specifying the intensity of the thunder. This may actually be set
independently from the RainLevel, meaning dark clouds can be produced without rain.

fields.name: ConfirmedPlatformLockedContent
fields.doc: ConfirmedPlatformLockedContent ...

fields.name: MultiPlayerGame
fields.doc:
MultiPlayerGame specifies if the world is a multi-player game. This should always be set to true for
servers.

fields.name: LANBroadcastEnabled
fields.doc: LANBroadcastEnabled specifies if LAN broadcast was intended to be enabled for the world.

fields.name: XBLBroadcastMode
fields.doc:
XBLBroadcastMode is the mode used to broadcast the joined game across Xbox Live.
When set to 0, the 'Invite' button in the pause screen is grayed out and players
cannot invite their friends to the Xbox Live multiplayer session they're currently in.
It only applies to worlds and has no effect on external servers.

fields.name: PlatformBroadcastMode
fields.doc: PlatformBroadcastMode is the mode used to broadcast the joined game across the platform.

fields.name: CommandsEnabled
fields.doc:
CommandsEnabled specifies if commands are enabled for the player. It is recommended to always set this
to true on the server, as setting it to false means the player cannot, under any circumstance, use a
command.

fields.name: TexturePackRequired
fields.doc:
TexturePackRequired specifies if the texture pack the world might hold is required, meaning the client
was forced to download it before joining.

fields.name: GameRules
fields.doc:
GameRules defines game rules currently active with their respective values. The value of these game
rules may be either 'bool', 'int32' or 'float32'. Some game rules are server side only, and don't
necessarily need to be sent to the client.

fields.name: Experiments
fields.doc:
Experiments holds a list of experiments that are either enabled or disabled in the world that the
player spawns in.

fields.name: ExperimentsPreviouslyToggled
fields.doc:
ExperimentsPreviouslyToggled specifies if any experiments were previously toggled in this world. It is
probably used for some kind of metrics.

fields.name: BonusChestEnabled
fields.doc:
BonusChestEnabled specifies if the world had the bonus map setting enabled when generating it. It does
not have any effect client-side.

fields.name: StartWithMapEnabled
fields.doc:
StartWithMapEnabled specifies if the world has the start with map setting enabled, meaning each joining
player obtains a map. This should always be set to false, because the client obtains a map all on its
own accord if this is set to true.

fields.name: PlayerPermissions
fields.doc:
PlayerPermissions is the permission level of the player. It is a value from 0-3, with 0 being visitor,
1 being member, 2 being operator and 3 being custom.

fields.name: ServerChunkTickRadius
fields.doc:
ServerChunkTickRadius is the radius around the player in which chunks are ticked. Most servers set this
value to a fixed number, as it does not necessarily affect anything client-side.

fields.name: HasLockedBehaviourPack
fields.doc:
HasLockedBehaviourPack specifies if the behaviour pack of the world is locked, meaning it cannot be
disabled from the world. This is typically set for worlds on the marketplace that have a dedicated
behaviour pack.

fields.name: HasLockedTexturePack
fields.doc:
HasLockedTexturePack specifies if the texture pack of the world is locked, meaning it cannot be
disabled from the world. This is typically set for worlds on the marketplace that have a dedicated
texture pack.

fields.name: FromLockedWorldTemplate
fields.doc:
FromLockedWorldTemplate specifies if the world from the server was from a locked world template. For
servers this should always be set to false.

fields.name: MSAGamerTagsOnly
fields.doc: MSAGamerTagsOnly ..

fields.name: FromWorldTemplate
fields.doc:
FromWorldTemplate specifies if the world from the server was from a world template. For servers this
should always be set to false.

fields.name: WorldTemplateSettingsLocked
fields.doc:
WorldTemplateSettingsLocked specifies if the world was a template that locks all settings that change
properties above in the settings GUI. It is recommended to set this to true for servers that do not
allow things such as setting game rules through the GUI.

fields.name: OnlySpawnV1Villagers
fields.doc:
OnlySpawnV1Villagers is a hack that Mojang put in place to preserve backwards compatibility with old
villagers. The bool is never actually read though, so it has no functionality.

fields.name: PersonaDisabled
fields.doc: PersonaDisabled is true if persona skins are disabled for the current game session.

fields.name: CustomSkinsDisabled
fields.doc: CustomSkinsDisabled is true if custom skins are disabled for the current game session.

fields.name: EmoteChatMuted
fields.doc: EmoteChatMuted specifies if players will be sent a chat message when using certain emotes.

fields.name: BaseGameVersion
fields.doc:
BaseGameVersion is the version of the game from which Vanilla features will be used. The exact function
of this field isn't clear.

fields.name: LimitedWorldWidth
fields.doc:
LimitedWorldWidth and LimitedWorldDepth are the dimensions of the world if the world is a limited
world. For unlimited worlds, these may simply be left as 0.

fields.name: LimitedWorldDepth
fields.doc:
LimitedWorldWidth and LimitedWorldDepth are the dimensions of the world if the world is a limited
world. For unlimited worlds, these may simply be left as 0.

fields.name: NewNether
fields.doc: NewNether specifies if the server runs with the new nether introduced in the 1.16 update.

fields.name: EducationSharedResourceURI
fields.doc: EducationSharedResourceURI is an education edition feature that transmits education resource settings to clients.

fields.name: ForceExperimentalGameplay
fields.doc:
ForceExperimentalGameplay specifies if experimental gameplay should be force enabled/disabled. For servers this
should always be empty.

fields.name: LevelID
fields.doc: LevelID is a base64 encoded world ID that is used to identify the world.

fields.name: WorldName
fields.doc:
WorldName is the name of the world that the player is joining. Note that this field shows up above the
player list for the rest of the game session, and cannot be changed. Setting the server name to this
field is recommended.

fields.name: TemplateContentIdentity
fields.doc:
TemplateContentIdentity is a UUID specific to the premium world template that might have been used to
generate the world. Servers should always fill out an empty string for this.

fields.name: Trial
fields.doc:
Trial specifies if the world was a trial world, meaning features are limited and there is a time limit
on the world.

fields.name: PlayerMovementSettings
fields.doc: PlayerMovementSettings ...

fields.name: Time
fields.doc: Time is the total time that has elapsed since the start of the world.

fields.name: EnchantmentSeed
fields.doc:
EnchantmentSeed is the seed used to seed the random used to produce enchantments in the enchantment
table. Note that the exact correct random implementation must be used to produce the correct results
both client- and server-side.

fields.name: Blocks
fields.doc: Blocks is a list of all custom blocks registered on the server.

fields.name: MultiPlayerCorrelationID
fields.doc:
MultiPlayerCorrelationID is a unique ID specifying the multi-player session of the player. A random
UUID should be filled out for this field.

fields.name: ServerAuthoritativeInventory
fields.doc:
ServerAuthoritativeInventory specifies if the server authoritative inventory system is enabled. This
is a new system introduced in 1.16. Backwards compatibility with the inventory transactions has to
some extent been preserved, but will eventually be removed.

fields.name: GameVersion
fields.doc: GameVersion is the version of the game the server is running. The exact function of this field isn't clear.

fields.name: PropertyData
fields.doc:
PropertyData contains properties that should be applied on the player. These properties are the same as the
ones that are sent in the SyncActorProperty packet.

fields.name: ServerBlockStateChecksum
fields.doc:
ServerBlockStateChecksum is a checksum to ensure block states between the server and client match.
This can simply be left empty, and the client will avoid trying to verify it.

fields.name: ClientSideGeneration
fields.doc:
ClientSideGeneration is true if the client should use the features registered in the FeatureRegistry packet to
generate terrain client-side to save on bandwidth.

fields.name: WorldTemplateID
fields.doc:
WorldTemplateID is a UUID that identifies the template that was used to generate the world. Servers that do not
use a world based off of a template can set this to an empty UUID.

fields.name: ChatRestrictionLevel
fields.doc: ChatRestrictionLevel specifies the level of restriction on in-game chat. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: DisablePlayerInteractions
fields.doc: DisablePlayerInteractions is true if the client should ignore other players when interacting with the world.

fields.name: UseBlockNetworkIDHashes
fields.doc:
UseBlockNetworkIDHashes is true if the client should use the hash of a block's name as its network ID rather than
its index in the expected block palette. This is useful for servers that wish to support multiple protocol versions
and custom blocks, but it will result in extra bytes being written for every block in a sub chunk palette.

fields.name: ServerAuthoritativeSound
fields.doc: ServerAuthoritativeSound is currently unknown as to what it does.

fields.name: ServerJoinInformation
fields.doc: ServerJoinInformation contains optional information about the server the player is joining.

fields.name: ServerID
fields.doc: ServerID is the server identifier for telemetry.

fields.name: ScenarioID
fields.doc: ScenarioID is the scenario identifier for telemetry.

fields.name: WorldID
fields.doc: WorldID is the world identifier for telemetry.

fields.name: OwnerID
fields.doc: OwnerID is the owner identifier for telemetry.

types.name: packet.StopSound
types.doc:
StopSound is sent by the server to stop a sound playing to the player, such as a playing music disk track
or other long-lasting sounds.

fields.name: SoundName
fields.doc:
SoundName is the name of the sound that should be stopped from playing. If no sound with this name is
currently active, the packet is ignored.

fields.name: StopAll
fields.doc:
StopAll specifies if all sounds currently playing to the player should be stopped. If set to true, the
SoundName field may be left empty.

fields.name: StopMusicLegacy
fields.doc: StopMusicLegacy is currently unknown.

types.name: packet.StructureBlockUpdate
types.doc:
StructureBlockUpdate is sent by the client when it updates a structure block using the in-game UI. The
data it contains depends on the type of structure block that it is. In Minecraft Bedrock Edition v1.11,
there is only the Export structure block type, but in v1.13 the ones present in Java Edition will,
according to the wiki, be added too.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position of the structure block that is updated.

fields.name: StructureName
fields.doc:
StructureName is the name of the structure that was set in the structure block's UI. This is the name
used to export the structure to a file.

fields.name: FilteredStructureName
fields.doc:
FilteredStructureName is a filtered version of StructureName with all the profanity removed. The client
will use this over StructureName if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity"
setting enabled.

fields.name: DataField
fields.doc:
DataField is the name of a function to run, usually used during natural generation. A description can
be found here: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Structure_Block#Data.

fields.name: IncludePlayers
fields.doc:
IncludePlayers specifies if the 'Include Players' toggle has been enabled, meaning players are also
exported by the structure block.

fields.name: ShowBoundingBox
fields.doc:
ShowBoundingBox specifies if the structure block should have its bounds outlined. A thin line will
encapsulate the bounds of the structure if set to true.

fields.name: StructureBlockType
fields.doc:
StructureBlockType is the type of the structure block updated. A list of structure block types that
will be used can be found in the constants above.

fields.name: Settings
fields.doc:
Settings is a struct of settings that should be used for exporting the structure. These settings are
identical to the last sent in the StructureBlockUpdate packet by the client.

fields.name: RedstoneSaveMode
fields.doc:
RedstoneSaveMode is the mode that should be used to save the structure when used with redstone. In
Java Edition, this is always stored in memory, but in Bedrock Edition it can be stored either to disk
or memory. See the constants above for the options.

fields.name: ShouldTrigger
fields.doc:
ShouldTrigger specifies if the structure block should be triggered immediately after this packet
reaches the server.

fields.name: Waterlogged
fields.doc: Waterlogged specifies if non-air blocks replace water or combine with water.

types.name: packet.StructureTemplateDataRequest
types.doc: StructureTemplateDataRequest is sent by the client to request data of a structure.

fields.name: StructureName
fields.doc:
StructureName is the name of the structure that was set in the structure block's UI. This is the name
used to export the structure to a file.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position of the structure block that has its template data requested.

fields.name: Settings
fields.doc:
Settings is a struct of settings that should be used for exporting the structure. These settings are
identical to the last sent in the StructureBlockUpdate packet by the client.

fields.name: RequestType
fields.doc:
RequestType specifies the type of template data request that the player sent. It is one of the
constants found above.

types.name: packet.StructureTemplateDataResponse
types.doc:
StructureTemplateDataResponse is sent by the server to send data of a structure to the client in response
to a StructureTemplateDataRequest packet.

fields.name: StructureName
fields.doc:
StructureName is the name of the structure that was requested. This is the name used to export the
structure to a file.

fields.name: Success
fields.doc:
Success specifies if a structure template was found by the StructureName that was sent in a
StructureTemplateDataRequest packet.

fields.name: ResponseType
fields.doc:
ResponseType specifies the response type of the packet. This depends on the RequestType field sent in
the StructureTemplateDataRequest packet and is one of the constants above.

fields.name: StructureTemplate
fields.doc: StructureTemplate holds the data of the structure template.

types.name: packet.SubChunk
types.doc: SubChunk sends data about multiple sub-chunks around a center point.

fields.name: CacheEnabled
fields.doc: CacheEnabled is whether the sub-chunk caching is enabled or not.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc: Dimension is the dimension the sub-chunks are in.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is an absolute sub-chunk center point that every SubChunkRequest uses as a reference.

fields.name: SubChunkEntries
fields.doc: SubChunkEntries contains sub-chunk entries relative to the center point.

types.name: packet.SubChunkRequest
types.doc: SubChunkRequest requests specific sub-chunks from the server using a center point.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc: Dimension is the dimension of the sub-chunk.

fields.name: Offsets
fields.doc: Offsets contains all requested offsets around the center point.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is an absolute sub-chunk center point used as a base point for all sub-chunks requested. The X and Z
coordinates represent the chunk coordinates, while the Y coordinate is the absolute sub-chunk index.

types.name: packet.SubClientLogin
types.doc:
SubClientLogin is sent when a sub-client joins the server while another client is already connected to it.
The packet is sent as a result of split-screen game play, and allows up to four players to play using the
same network connection. After an initial Login packet from the 'main' client, each sub-client that
connects sends a SubClientLogin to request their own login.

fields.name: ConnectionRequest
fields.doc:
ConnectionRequest is a string containing information about the player and JWTs that may be used to
verify if the player is connected to XBOX Live. The connection request also contains the necessary
client public key to initiate encryption.
The ConnectionRequest in this packet is identical to the one found in the Login packet.

types.name: packet.SyncActorProperty
types.doc: SyncActorProperty is an alternative to synced actor data.

fields.name: PropertyData
fields.doc: PropertyData ...

types.name: packet.SyncWorldClocks
types.doc: SyncWorldClocks is sent by the server to initialise and synchronise world clocks with the client.

fields.name: PayloadType
fields.doc: PayloadType is the type of clock payload. It is one of the protocol.ClockPayloadType constants.

fields.name: SyncStates
fields.doc: SyncStates is set if PayloadType is ClockPayloadTypeSyncState.

fields.name: Clocks
fields.doc: Clocks is set if PayloadType is ClockPayloadTypeInitializeRegistry.

fields.name: AddClockID
fields.doc: AddClockID is the clock ID for adding time markers, set if PayloadType is ClockPayloadTypeAddTimeMarker.

fields.name: AddTimeMarkers
fields.doc: AddTimeMarkers is the list of time markers to add, set if PayloadType is ClockPayloadTypeAddTimeMarker.

fields.name: RemoveClockID
fields.doc: RemoveClockID is the clock ID for removing time markers, set if PayloadType is ClockPayloadTypeRemoveTimeMarker.

fields.name: RemoveTimeMarkerIDs
fields.doc: RemoveTimeMarkerIDs is the list of time marker IDs to remove.

types.name: packet.TakeItemActor
types.doc:
TakeItemActor is sent by the server when a player picks up an item entity. It makes the item entity
disappear to viewers and shows the pick-up animation.

fields.name: ItemEntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
ItemEntityRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID of the item that is being taken by another entity. It will
disappear to viewers after showing the pick-up animation.

fields.name: TakerEntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
TakerEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity that took the item, which is usually a player, but
could be another entity like a zombie too.

types.name: packet.Text
types.doc:
Text is sent by the client to the server to send chat messages, and by the server to the client to forward
or send messages, which may be chat, popups, tips etc.

fields.name: TextType
fields.doc:
TextType is the type of the text sent. When a client sends this to the server, it should always be
TextTypeChat. If the server sends it, it may be one of the other text types above.

fields.name: NeedsTranslation
fields.doc:
NeedsTranslation specifies if any of the messages need to be translated. It seems that where % is found
in translatable text types, these are translated regardless of this bool. Translatable text types
include TextTypeTranslation, TextTypeTip, TextTypePopup and TextTypeJukeboxPopup.

fields.name: SourceName
fields.doc:
SourceName is the name of the source of the messages. This source is displayed in text types such as
the TextTypeChat and TextTypeWhisper, where typically the username is shown.

fields.name: Message
fields.doc:
Message is the message of the packet. This field is set for each TextType and is the main component of
the packet.

fields.name: Parameters
fields.doc:
Parameters is a list of parameters that should be filled into the message. These parameters are only
written if the type of the packet is TextTypeTranslation, TextTypeTip, TextTypePopup or TextTypeJukeboxPopup.

fields.name: XUID
fields.doc:
XUID is the XBOX Live user ID of the player that sent the message. It is only set for packets of
TextTypeChat. When sent to a player, the player will only be shown the chat message if a player with
this XUID is present in the player list and not muted, or if the XUID is empty.

fields.name: PlatformChatID
fields.doc:
PlatformChatID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when chatting (presumably only for
Nintendo Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to
chat with each other.

fields.name: FilteredMessage
fields.doc:
FilteredMessage is a filtered version of Message with all the profanity removed. The client will use
this over Message if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

types.name: packet.TickingAreasLoadStatus
types.doc: TickingAreasLoadStatus is sent by the server to the client to notify the client of a ticking area's loading status.

fields.name: Preload
fields.doc: Preload is true if the server is waiting for the area's preload.

types.name: packet.ToastRequest
types.doc:
ToastRequest is a packet sent from the server to the client to display a toast to the top of the screen. These toasts
are the same as the ones seen when, for example, loading a new resource pack or obtaining an achievement.

fields.name: Title
fields.doc: Title is the title of the toast.

fields.name: Message
fields.doc: Message is the message that the toast may contain alongside the title.

types.name: packet.Transfer
types.doc:
Transfer is sent by the server to transfer a player from the current server to another. Doing so will
fully disconnect the client, bring it back to the main menu and make it connect to the next server.

fields.name: Address
fields.doc: Address is the address of the new server, which might be either a hostname or an actual IP address.

fields.name: Port
fields.doc: Port is the UDP port of the new server.

fields.name: ReloadWorld
fields.doc: ReloadWorld currently has an unknown usage.

fields.name: GatheringJoinInfo
fields.doc: GatheringJoinInfo optionally identifies the gathering being joined on the target server.

types.name: packet.TrimData
types.doc:
TrimData is sent by the server to the client when they first join the server. It contains a list of all the patterns
and materials that can be applied via armour trims.

fields.name: Patterns
fields.doc:
Patterns is a list of patterns that can be applied to armour. Each pattern has its own style and texture that is
defined through resource packs.

fields.name: Materials
fields.doc:
Materials is a list of materials that can be applied to armour. These are mostly different ores that have different
colours for more customization.

types.name: packet.UnlockedRecipes
types.doc:
UnlockedRecipes gives the client a list of recipes that have been unlocked, restricting the recipes that appear in
the recipe book.

fields.name: UnlockType
fields.doc:
UnlockType is the type of unlock that the packet represents, and can either be adding or removing a list of recipes.
It is one of the constants listed above.

fields.name: Recipes
fields.doc: Recipes is a list of recipe names that have been unlocked.

types.name: packet.UpdateAbilities
types.doc:
UpdateAbilities is a packet sent from the server to the client to update the abilities of the player. It, along with
the UpdateAdventureSettings packet, are replacements of the AdventureSettings packet since v1.19.10.

fields.name: AbilityData
fields.doc: AbilityData represents various data about the abilities of a player, such as ability layers or permissions.

types.name: packet.UpdateAdventureSettings
types.doc:
UpdateAdventureSettings is a packet sent from the server to the client to update the adventure settings of the player.
It, along with the UpdateAbilities packet, are replacements of the AdventureSettings packet since v1.19.10.

fields.name: NoPvM
fields.doc: NoPvM is a boolean indicating whether the player is allowed to fight mobs or not.

fields.name: NoMvP
fields.doc:
NoMvP is a boolean indicating whether mobs are allowed to fight the player or not. It is unclear why this is sent
to the client.

fields.name: ImmutableWorld
fields.doc: ImmutableWorld is a boolean indicating whether the player is allowed to modify the world or not.

fields.name: ShowNameTags
fields.doc: ShowNameTags is a boolean indicating whether player name tags are shown or not.

fields.name: AutoJump
fields.doc: AutoJump is a boolean indicating whether the player is allowed to jump automatically or not.

types.name: packet.UpdateAttributes
types.doc:
UpdateAttributes is sent by the server to update an amount of attributes of any entity in the world. These
attributes include ones such as the health or the movement speed of the entity.

fields.name: EntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

fields.name: Attributes
fields.doc:
Attributes is a slice of new attributes that the entity gets. It includes attributes such as its
health, movement speed, etc. Note that only changed attributes have to be sent in this packet. It is
not required to send attributes that did not have their values changed.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

types.name: packet.UpdateBlock
types.doc:
UpdateBlock is sent by the server to update a block client-side, without resending the entire chunk that
the block is located in. It is particularly useful for small modifications like block breaking/placing.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the block position at which a block is updated.

fields.name: NewBlockRuntimeID
fields.doc:
NewBlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block that is placed at Position after sending the packet
to the client.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
Flags is a combination of flags that specify the way the block is updated client-side. It is a
combination of the flags above, but typically sending only the BlockUpdateNetwork flag is sufficient.

fields.name: Layer
fields.doc:
Layer is the world layer on which the block is updated. For most blocks, this is the first layer, as
that layer is the default layer to place blocks on, but for blocks inside of each other, this differs.

types.name: packet.UpdateBlockSynced
types.doc:
UpdateBlockSynced is sent by the server to synchronise the falling of a falling block entity with the
transitioning back and forth from and to a solid block. It is used to prevent the entity from flickering,
and is used in places such as the pushing of blocks with pistons.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the block position at which a block is updated.

fields.name: NewBlockRuntimeID
fields.doc:
NewBlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block that is placed at Position after sending the packet
to the client.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
Flags is a combination of flags that specify the way the block is updated client-side. It is a
combination of the flags above, but typically sending only the BlockUpdateNetwork flag is sufficient.

fields.name: Layer
fields.doc:
Layer is the world layer on which the block is updated. For most blocks, this is the first layer, as
that layer is the default layer to place blocks on, but for blocks inside of each other, this differs.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the falling block entity that the block transitions to or that the
entity transitions from.
Note that for both possible values for TransitionType, the EntityUniqueID should point to the falling
block entity involved.

fields.name: TransitionType
fields.doc:
TransitionType is the type of the transition that happened. It is either BlockToEntityTransition, when
a block placed becomes a falling entity, or EntityToBlockTransition, when a falling entity hits the
ground and becomes a solid block again.

types.name: packet.UpdateClientInputLocks
types.doc:
UpdateClientInputLocks is sent by the server to the client to lock specific player inputs such as camera
rotation, movement, jumping, sneaking, mounting or individual directional movement.

fields.name: Locks
fields.doc:
Locks is a set of flags that specify which client inputs are disabled, such as whether the player can
move, rotate the camera, jump, sneak or mount/dismount entities. It is a combination of the
ClientInputLock constants above.

types.name: packet.UpdateClientOptions
types.doc:
UpdateClientOptions is sent by the client when some of the client's options are updated, such as the
graphics mode.

fields.name: GraphicsMode
fields.doc: GraphicsMode is the graphics mode that the client is using. It is one of the constants above.

fields.name: FilterProfanity
fields.doc: FilterProfanity is if the client only uses filtered messages or not.

types.name: packet.UpdateEquip
types.doc:
UpdateEquip is sent by the server to the client upon opening a horse inventory. It is used to set the
content of the inventory and specify additional properties, such as the items that are allowed to be put
in slots of the inventory.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc:
WindowID is the identifier associated with the window that the UpdateEquip packet concerns. It is the
ID sent for the horse inventory that was opened before this packet was sent.

fields.name: WindowType
fields.doc:
WindowType is the type of the window that was opened. Generally, this is the type of a horse inventory,
as the packet is specifically made for that.

fields.name: Size
fields.doc:
Size is the size of the horse inventory that should be opened. A bigger size does, in fact, change the
amount of slots displayed.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity whose equipment was 'updated' to the player. It is
typically the horse entity that had its inventory opened.

fields.name: SerialisedInventoryData
fields.doc:
SerialisedInventoryData is a network NBT serialised compound holding the content of the inventory of
the entity (the equipment) and additional data such as the allowed items for a particular slot, used to
make sure only saddles can be put in the saddle slot etc.

types.name: packet.UpdatePlayerGameType
types.doc:
UpdatePlayerGameType is sent by the server to change the game mode of a player. It is functionally
identical to the SetPlayerGameType packet.

fields.name: GameType
fields.doc:
GameType is the new game type of the player. It is one of the constants that can be found in
set_player_game_type.go. Some of these game types require additional flags to be set in an
UpdateAbilities packet for the game mode to obtain its full functionality.

fields.name: PlayerUniqueID
fields.doc:
PlayerUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the player that should have its game mode updated. If this
packet is sent to other clients with the player unique ID of another player, nothing happens.

fields.name: Tick
fields.doc: Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

types.name: packet.UpdateSoftEnum
types.doc:
UpdateSoftEnum is sent by the server to update a soft enum, also known as a dynamic enum, previously sent
in the AvailableCommands packet. It is sent whenever the enum should get new options or when some of its
options should be removed.
The UpdateSoftEnum packet will apply for enums that have been set in the AvailableCommands packet with the
'Dynamic' field of the CommandEnum set to true.

fields.name: EnumType
fields.doc:
EnumType is the type of the enum. This type must be identical to the one set in the AvailableCommands
packet, because the client uses this to recognise which enum to update.

fields.name: Options
fields.doc:
Options is a list of options that should be updated. Depending on the ActionType field, either these
options will be added to the enum, the enum options will be set to these options or all of these
options will be removed from the enum.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the action to execute on the enum. The Options field has a different result,
depending on what ActionType is used.

types.name: packet.UpdateSubChunkBlocks
types.doc: UpdateSubChunkBlocks is essentially just UpdateBlock packet, however for a set of blocks in a sub-chunk.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the block position of the sub-chunk being referred to.

fields.name: Blocks
fields.doc: Blocks contains each updated block change entry.

fields.name: Extra
fields.doc: Extra contains each updated block change entry for the second layer, usually for waterlogged blocks.

types.name: packet.UpdateTrade
types.doc:
UpdateTrade is sent by the server to update the trades offered by a villager to a player. It is sent at the
moment that a player interacts with a villager.

fields.name: WindowID
fields.doc: WindowID is the ID that identifies the trading window that the client currently has opened.

fields.name: WindowType
fields.doc:
WindowType is an identifier specifying the type of the window opened. In vanilla, it appears this is
always filled out with 15.

fields.name: Size
fields.doc: Size is the amount of trading options that the villager has.

fields.name: TradeTier
fields.doc:
TradeTier is the tier of the villager that the player is trading with. The tier starts at 0 with a
first two offers being available, after which two additional offers are unlocked each time the tier
becomes one higher.

fields.name: VillagerUniqueID
fields.doc:
VillagerUniqueID is the unique ID of the villager entity that the player is trading with. The
TradeTier sent above applies to this villager.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity (usually a player) for which the trades are updated. The
updated trades may apply only to this entity.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.doc:
DisplayName is the name displayed at the top of the trading UI. It is usually used to represent the
profession of the villager in the UI.

fields.name: NewTradeUI
fields.doc:
NewTradeUI specifies if the villager should be using the new trade UI (The one added in 1.11.) rather
than the old one. This should usually be set to true.

fields.name: DemandBasedPrices
fields.doc:
DemandBasedPrices specifies if the prices of the villager's offers are modified by an increase in
demand for the item. (A mechanic added in 1.11.) Buying more of the same item will increase the price
of that particular item.

fields.name: SerialisedOffers
fields.doc: SerialisedOffers is a network NBT serialised compound of offers that the villager has.

types.name: packet.VoxelShapes
types.doc: VoxelShapes is sent by the server to send voxel shape data to the client.

fields.name: Shapes
fields.doc: Shapes is a list of voxel shapes.

fields.name: NameMap
fields.doc: NameMap is a map of shape names to IDs.

fields.name: CustomShapeCount
fields.doc: CustomShapeCount is the number of custom shapes.

types.name: protocol.AbilityData
types.doc: AbilityData represents various data about the abilities of a player, such as ability layers or permissions.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is a unique identifier of the player. It appears it is not required to fill this field
out with a correct value. Simply writing 0 seems to work.

fields.name: PlayerPermissions
fields.doc:
PlayerPermissions is the permission level of the player as it shows up in the player list built up using
the PlayerList packet.

fields.name: CommandPermissions
fields.doc: CommandPermissions is a set of permissions that specify what commands a player is allowed to execute.

fields.name: Layers
fields.doc:
Layers contains all ability layers and their potential values. This should at least have one entry, being the
base layer.

types.name: protocol.AbilityLayer
types.doc: AbilityLayer represents the abilities of a specific layer, such as the base layer or the spectator layer.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type represents the type of the layer. This is one of the AbilityLayerType constants defined above.

fields.name: Abilities
fields.doc:
Abilities is a set of abilities that are enabled for the layer. This is one of the Ability constants defined
above.

fields.name: Values
fields.doc:
Values is a set of values that are associated with the enabled abilities, representing the values of the
abilities.

fields.name: FlySpeed
fields.doc: FlySpeed is the default horizontal fly speed of the layer.

fields.name: VerticalFlySpeed
fields.doc: VerticalFlySpeed is the default vertical fly speed of the layer.

fields.name: WalkSpeed
fields.doc: WalkSpeed is the default walk speed of the layer.

types.name: protocol.AchievementAwardedEvent
types.doc: AchievementAwardedEvent is the event data sent for achievements.

fields.name: AchievementID
fields.doc: AchievementID is the ID for the achievement.

types.name: protocol.AgentCommandEvent
types.doc: AgentCommandEvent is an event used in Education Edition.

fields.name: AgentResult
fields.doc: AgentResult ...

fields.name: DataValue
fields.doc: DataValue ...

fields.name: Command
fields.doc: Command ...

fields.name: DataKey
fields.doc: DataKey ...

fields.name: Output
fields.doc: Output ...

types.name: protocol.AgentCreatedEvent
types.doc: AgentCreatedEvent is the event data sent when an agent is created.

types.name: protocol.ArrowShape
types.doc: ArrowShape represents an arrow debug shape.

fields.name: ArrowEndLocation
fields.doc: ArrowEndLocation is the arrow end location of the shape.

fields.name: ArrowHeadLength
fields.doc: ArrowHeadLength is the arrow head length of the shape.

fields.name: ArrowHeadRadius
fields.doc: ArrowHeadRadius is the arrow head radius of the shape.

fields.name: Segments
fields.doc: Segments is the segments that used for the debug arrow's head.

types.name: protocol.Attribute
types.doc:
Attribute is an entity attribute, that holds specific data such as the health of the entity. Each attribute
holds a default value, maximum and minimum value, name and its current value.

fields.name: DefaultMin
fields.doc:
DefaultMin is the default minimum value of the attribute. It's not clear why this field must be sent to
the client, but it is required regardless.

fields.name: DefaultMax
fields.doc:
DefaultMax is the default maximum value of the attribute. It's not clear why this field must be sent to
the client, but it is required regardless.

fields.name: Default
fields.doc:
Default is the default value of the attribute. It's not clear why this field must be sent to the
client, but it is required regardless.

fields.name: Modifiers
fields.doc: Modifiers is a slice of AttributeModifiers that are applied to the attribute.

types.name: protocol.AttributeData
types.doc: AttributeData represents a polymorphic attribute value.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the attribute data type. It is one of the AttributeDataType constants.

fields.name: BoolValue
fields.doc: BoolValue is the boolean value if Type is AttributeDataTypeBool.

fields.name: BoolOperation
fields.doc: BoolOperation is the optional operation for boolean attributes.

fields.name: FloatValue
fields.doc: FloatValue is the float value if Type is AttributeDataTypeFloat.

fields.name: FloatOperation
fields.doc: FloatOperation is the optional operation for float attributes.

fields.name: FloatConstraintMin
fields.doc: FloatConstraintMin is the optional minimum constraint for float attributes.

fields.name: FloatConstraintMax
fields.doc: FloatConstraintMax is the optional maximum constraint for float attributes.

fields.name: ColourValue
fields.doc: ColourValue is the colour value if Type is AttributeDataTypeColour.

fields.name: ColourOperation
fields.doc: ColourOperation is the optional operation for colour attributes.

types.name: protocol.AttributeLayerData
types.doc: AttributeLayerData represents a complete attribute layer.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the name of the attribute layer.

fields.name: NoiseName
fields.doc: NoiseName is the optional name of the noise used by the layer.

fields.name: DimensionID
fields.doc: DimensionID is the dimension the layer applies to.

fields.name: Settings
fields.doc: Settings is the layer's settings.

fields.name: EnvironmentAttributes
fields.doc: EnvironmentAttributes is the list of environment attributes in this layer.

types.name: protocol.AttributeLayerSettings
types.doc: AttributeLayerSettings represents settings for an attribute layer.

fields.name: Priority
fields.doc: Priority is the priority of the layer.

fields.name: FloatWeight
fields.doc: FloatWeight is the weight of the layer.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.doc: Enabled indicates if the layer is enabled.

fields.name: TransitionsPaused
fields.doc: TransitionsPaused indicates if transitions are paused for this layer.

types.name: protocol.AttributeModifier
types.doc:
AttributeModifier temporarily buffs/debuffs a given attribute until the modifier is used. In vanilla, these are
mainly used for effects.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the unique ID of the modifier. It is used to identify the modifier in the packet.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the name of the attribute that is modified.

fields.name: Amount
fields.doc: Amount is the amount of difference between the current value of the attribute and the new value.

fields.name: Operation
fields.doc:
Operation is the operation that is performed on the attribute. It can be addition, multiply base, multiply total
or cap.

fields.name: Operand
fields.doc:
Operand ...
TODO: Figure out what this field is used for.

fields.name: Serializable
fields.doc:
Serializable ...
TODO: Figure out what this field is used for.

types.name: protocol.AttributeValue
types.doc: AttributeValue holds the value of an attribute, including the min and max.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc:
Name is the name of the attribute, for example 'minecraft:health'. These names must be identical to
the ones defined client-side.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc:
Value is the current value of the attribute. This value will be applied to the entity when sent in a
packet.

fields.name: Max
fields.doc:
Max and Min specify the boundaries within the value of the attribute must be. The definition of these
fields differ per attribute. The maximum health of an entity may be changed, whereas the maximum
movement speed for example may not be.

fields.name: Min
fields.doc:
Max and Min specify the boundaries within the value of the attribute must be. The definition of these
fields differ per attribute. The maximum health of an entity may be changed, whereas the maximum
movement speed for example may not be.

types.name: protocol.AutoCraftRecipeStackRequestAction
types.doc:
AutoCraftRecipeStackRequestAction is sent by the client similarly to the CraftRecipeStackRequestAction. The
only difference is that the recipe is automatically created and crafted by shift clicking the recipe book.

fields.name: RecipeNetworkID
fields.doc:
RecipeNetworkID is the network ID of the recipe that is about to be crafted. This network ID matches
one of the recipes sent in the CraftingData packet, where each of the recipes have a RecipeNetworkID as
of 1.16.

fields.name: NumberOfCrafts
fields.doc: NumberOfCrafts is how many times the recipe was crafted.

fields.name: Ingredients
fields.doc:
Ingredients is a slice of ItemDescriptorCount that contains the ingredients that were used to craft the recipe.
It is not exactly clear what this is used for, but it is sent by the vanilla client.

types.name: protocol.BeaconPaymentStackRequestAction
types.doc:
BeaconPaymentStackRequestAction is sent by the client when it submits an item to enable effects from a
beacon. These items will have been moved into the beacon item slot in advance.

fields.name: PrimaryEffect
fields.doc: PrimaryEffect and SecondaryEffect are the effects that were selected from the beacon.

fields.name: SecondaryEffect
fields.doc: PrimaryEffect and SecondaryEffect are the effects that were selected from the beacon.

types.name: protocol.BellUsedEvent
types.doc: BellUsedEvent is the event data sent when a bell is used.

fields.name: ItemID
fields.doc: ItemID ...

types.name: protocol.BiomeCappedSurface
types.doc: BiomeCappedSurface specifies the materials to use for the capped surface of a biome, such as in the Nether.

fields.name: FloorBlocks
fields.doc: FloorBlocks is a list of runtime IDs to use for the floor blocks.

fields.name: CeilingBlocks
fields.doc: CeilingBlocks is a list of runtime IDs to use for the ceiling blocks.

fields.name: SeaBlock
fields.doc: SeaBlock is an optional runtime ID to use for the sea block.

fields.name: FoundationBlock
fields.doc: FoundationBlock is an optional runtime ID to use for the foundation block.

fields.name: BeachBlock
fields.doc: BeachBlock is an optional runtime ID to use for the beach block.

types.name: protocol.BiomeChunkGeneration
types.doc:
BiomeChunkGeneration represents the information required for the client to generate chunks itself
to create the illusion of a larger render distance.

fields.name: Climate
fields.doc: Climate is optional information to specify the biome's climate.

fields.name: ConsolidatedFeatures
fields.doc: ConsolidatedFeatures is a list of features that are consolidated into a single feature.

fields.name: MountainParameters
fields.doc: MountainParameters is optional information to specify the biome's mountain parameters.

fields.name: SurfaceMaterialAdjustments
fields.doc: SurfaceMaterialAdjustments is a list of surface material adjustments.

fields.name: SurfaceMaterials
fields.doc: SurfaceMaterials is a set of materials to use for the surface layers of the biome.

fields.name: HasDefaultOverworldSurface
fields.doc: HasDefaultOverworldSurface is true if the biome has a default overworld surface.

fields.name: HasSwampSurface
fields.doc: HasSwampSurface is true if the biome has a swamp surface.

fields.name: HasFrozenOceanSurface
fields.doc: HasFrozenOceanSurface is true if the biome has a frozen ocean surface.

fields.name: HasEndSurface
fields.doc: HasEndSurface is true if the biome has an end surface.

fields.name: MesaSurface
fields.doc: MesaSurface is optional information to specify the biome's mesa surface.

fields.name: CappedSurface
fields.doc: CappedSurface is optional information to specify the biome's capped surface, i.e. in the Nether.

fields.name: OverworldRules
fields.doc: OverworldRules is optional information to specify the biome's overworld rules, such as rivers and hills.

fields.name: MultiNoiseRules
fields.doc: MultiNoiseRules is optional information to specify the biome's multi-noise rules.

fields.name: LegacyRules
fields.doc:
LegacyRules is a list of legacy rules for the biomes using an older format, which is just a list of
weighted biomes.

fields.name: ReplacementsData
fields.doc: ReplacementsData is a list of biome replacement data.

fields.name: VillageType
fields.doc: VillageType is the optional village type for the biome's chunk generation.

fields.name: SurfaceBuilder
fields.doc: SurfaceBuilder is optional information for the biome's surface builder.

fields.name: SubsurfaceBuilder
fields.doc: SubsurfaceBuilder is optional information for the biome's subsurface builder.

types.name: protocol.BiomeClimate
types.doc: BiomeClimate represents the climate of a biome, mainly for ambience but also defines certain behaviours.

fields.name: Temperature
fields.doc: Temperature is the temperature of the biome, used for weather, biome behaviours and sky colour.

fields.name: Downfall
fields.doc: Downfall is the amount that precipitation affects colours and block changes.

fields.name: SnowAccumulationMin
fields.doc:
SnowAccumulationMin is the minimum amount of snow that can accumulate in the biome, every 0.125 is
another layer of snow.

fields.name: SnowAccumulationMax
fields.doc:
SnowAccumulationMax is the maximum amount of snow that can accumulate in the biome, every 0.125 is
another layer of snow.

types.name: protocol.BiomeConditionalTransformation
types.doc: BiomeConditionalTransformation is the legacy method of transforming biomes.

fields.name: WeightedBiomes
fields.doc: WeightedBiomes is a list of biomes and their weights.

fields.name: ConditionJSON
fields.doc: ConditionJSON is an index of the condition JSON data in the string list.

fields.name: MinPassingNeighbours
fields.doc:
MinPassingNeighbours is the minimum number of neighbours that must pass the condition for the
transformation to be applied.

types.name: protocol.BiomeConsolidatedFeature
types.doc: BiomeConsolidatedFeature represents a feature that is consolidated into a single feature for the biome.

fields.name: Scatter
fields.doc: Scatter defines how the feature is scattered in the biome.

fields.name: Feature
fields.doc: Feature is the index of the feature's name in the string list.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.doc: Identifier is the index of the feature's identifier in the string list.

fields.name: Pass
fields.doc: Pass is the index of the feature's pass in the string list.

fields.name: CanUseInternal
fields.doc: CanUseInternal is true if the feature can use internal features.

types.name: protocol.BiomeCoordinate
types.doc: BiomeCoordinate specifies coordinate rules for where features can be scattered in the biome.

fields.name: MinValueType
fields.doc:
MinValueType is the type of expression operation to use for the minimum value, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.

fields.name: MinValue
fields.doc: MinValue is the index of the minimum value expression in the string list.

fields.name: MaxValueType
fields.doc: MaxValueType is the type of expression operation to use for the maximum value, and is one of the

fields.name: MaxValue
fields.doc: MaxValue is the index of the maximum value expression in the string list.

fields.name: GridOffset
fields.doc: GridOffset is the offset of the grid, used for fixed grid and jittered grid distributions.

fields.name: GridStepSize
fields.doc: GridStepSize is the step size of the grid, used for fixed grid and jittered grid distributions.

fields.name: Distribution
fields.doc:
Distribution is the type of distribution to use for the coordinate, and is one of the
BiomeRandomDistributionType constants above.

types.name: protocol.BiomeDefinition
types.doc:
BiomeDefinition represents a biome definition in the game. This can be a vanilla biome or a completely
custom biome.

fields.name: NameIndex
fields.doc: NameIndex represents the index of the biome name in the string list.

fields.name: BiomeID
fields.doc: BiomeID is the biome ID.

fields.name: Temperature
fields.doc: Temperature is the temperature of the biome, used for weather, biome behaviours and sky colour.

fields.name: Downfall
fields.doc: Downfall is the amount that precipitation affects colours and block changes.

fields.name: FoliageSnow
fields.doc: FoliageSnow is the progression factor for foliage turning white due to snow.

fields.name: Depth
fields.doc: Depth is the depth of the biome.

fields.name: Scale
fields.doc: Scale is the scale of the biome.

fields.name: MapWaterColour
fields.doc: MapWaterColour is an ARGB value for the water colour on maps in the biome.

fields.name: Rain
fields.doc: Rain is true if the biome has rain, false if it is a dry biome.

fields.name: Tags
fields.doc:
Tags are a list of indices of tags in the string list. These are used to group biomes together for
biome generation and other purposes.

fields.name: ChunkGeneration
fields.doc:
ChunkGeneration is optional information to assist in client-side chunk generation. Almost all servers
can and should leave this empty to greatly reduce the size of this packet. Only BDS and servers which
*exactly* match the vanilla chunk generation can benefit from this.

types.name: protocol.BiomeElementData
types.doc: BiomeElementData are set rules to adjust the surface materials of the biome.

fields.name: NoiseFrequencyScale
fields.doc: NoiseFrequencyScale is the frequency scale of the noise used to adjust the surface materials.

fields.name: NoiseLowerBound
fields.doc: NoiseLowerBound is the minimum noise value required to be selected.

fields.name: NoiseUpperBound
fields.doc: NoiseUpperBound is the maximum noise value required to be selected.

fields.name: HeightMinType
fields.doc:
HeightMinType is the type of expression operation to use for the minimum height, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.

fields.name: HeightMin
fields.doc: HeightMin is the index of the minimum height expression in the string list.

fields.name: HeightMaxType
fields.doc:
HeightMaxType is the type of expression operation to use for the maximum height, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.

fields.name: HeightMax
fields.doc: HeightMax is the index of the maximum height expression in the string list.

fields.name: AdjustedMaterials
fields.doc: AdjustedMaterials is the materials to use for the surface layers of the biome if selected.

types.name: protocol.BiomeMesaSurface
types.doc: BiomeMesaSurface specifies the materials to use for the mesa biome.

fields.name: ClayMaterial
fields.doc: ClayMaterial is the runtime ID of the block to use for clay layers.

fields.name: HardClayMaterial
fields.doc: HardClayMaterial is the runtime ID of the block to use for hard clay layers.

fields.name: BrycePillars
fields.doc: BrycePillars is true if the biome has bryce pillars, which are tall spire-like structures.

fields.name: HasForest
fields.doc: HasForest is true if the biome has a forest.

types.name: protocol.BiomeMountainParameters
types.doc: BiomeMountainParameters specifies the parameters for a mountain biome.

fields.name: SteepBlock
fields.doc: SteepBlock is the runtime ID of the block to use for steep slopes.

fields.name: NorthSlopes
fields.doc: NorthSlopes is true if the biome has north slopes.

fields.name: SouthSlopes
fields.doc: SouthSlopes is true if the biome has south slopes.

fields.name: WestSlopes
fields.doc: WestSlopes is true if the biome has west slopes.

fields.name: EastSlopes
fields.doc: EastSlopes is true if the biome has east slopes.

fields.name: TopSlideEnabled
fields.doc: TopSlideEnabled is true if the biome has top slide enabled.

types.name: protocol.BiomeMultiNoiseRules
types.doc:
BiomeMultiNoiseRules specifies the rules for multi-noise biomes, which are biomes that are defined by
multiple noise parameters instead of just temperature and humidity.

fields.name: Temperature
fields.doc: Temperature is the temperature level of the biome.

fields.name: Humidity
fields.doc: Humidity is the humidity level of the biome.

fields.name: Altitude
fields.doc: Altitude is the altitude level of the biome.

fields.name: Weirdness
fields.doc: Weirdness is the weirdness level of the biome.

fields.name: Weight
fields.doc: Weight is the weight of the biome, with a higher weight being more likely to be selected.

types.name: protocol.BiomeNoiseGradientSurface
types.doc: BiomeNoiseGradientSurface specifies noise-gradient surface block data for a biome.

fields.name: NonReplaceableBlocks
fields.doc: NonReplaceableBlocks is a list of block runtime IDs that may not be replaced.

fields.name: GradientBlocks
fields.doc: GradientBlocks is a list of noise block specifiers used by the gradient.

fields.name: Noise
fields.doc: Noise is the noise descriptor used by the gradient.

types.name: protocol.BiomeOverworldRules
types.doc: BiomeOverworldRules specifies a list of transformation rules to apply to different parts of the overworld.

fields.name: HillsTransformations
fields.doc: HillsTransformations is a list of weighted biome transformations to apply to hills.

fields.name: MutateTransformations
fields.doc: MutateTransformations is a list of weighted biome transformations to apply to mutated biomes.

fields.name: RiverTransformations
fields.doc: RiverTransformations is a list of weighted biome transformations to apply to rivers.

fields.name: ShoreTransformations
fields.doc: ShoreTransformations is a list of weighted biome transformations to apply to shores.

fields.name: PreHillsEdgeTransformations
fields.doc: PreHillsEdgeTransformations is a list of conditional transformations to apply to the edges of hills.

fields.name: PostShoreEdgeTransformations
fields.doc: PostShoreEdgeTransformations is a list of conditional transformations to apply to the edges of shores.

fields.name: ClimateTransformations
fields.doc: ClimateTransformations is a list of weighted temperature transformations to apply to the biome's climate.

types.name: protocol.BiomeReplacementData
types.doc: BiomeReplacementData represents data for biome replacements.

fields.name: Biome
fields.doc: Biome is the biome ID to replace.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.doc: Dimension is the dimension ID where the replacement applies.

fields.name: TargetBiomes
fields.doc: TargetBiomes is a list of target biome IDs for the replacement.

fields.name: Amount
fields.doc: Amount is the amount of replacement to apply.

fields.name: NoiseFrequencyScale
fields.doc: NoiseFrequencyScale ...

fields.name: ReplacementIndex
fields.doc: ReplacementIndex is the index of the replacement.

fields.name: Coordinates
fields.doc: Coordinates is a list of coordinate rules to scatter the feature within.

fields.name: EvaluationOrder
fields.doc:
EvaluationOrder is the order in which the coordinates are evaluated, and is one of the
CoordinateEvaluationOrder constants above.

fields.name: ChancePercentType
fields.doc:
ChancePercentType is the type of expression operation to use for the chance percent, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.

fields.name: ChancePercent
fields.doc: ChangePercent is the index of the chance expression in the string list.

fields.name: ChanceNumerator
fields.doc: ChanceNumerator is the numerator of the chance expression.

fields.name: ChanceDenominator
fields.doc: ChanceDenominator is the denominator of the chance expression.

fields.name: IterationsType
fields.doc:
IterationsType is the type of expression operation to use for the iterations, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.

fields.name: Iterations
fields.doc: Iterations is the index of the iterations expression in the string list.

types.name: protocol.BiomeSurfaceBuilder
types.doc: BiomeSurfaceBuilder specifies the materials and special surface rules to use for a biome surface.

fields.name: SurfaceMaterials
fields.doc: SurfaceMaterials is a set of materials to use for the surface layers of the biome.

fields.name: HasDefaultOverworldSurface
fields.doc: HasDefaultOverworldSurface is true if the biome has a default overworld surface.

fields.name: HasSwampSurface
fields.doc: HasSwampSurface is true if the biome has a swamp surface.

fields.name: HasFrozenOceanSurface
fields.doc: HasFrozenOceanSurface is true if the biome has a frozen ocean surface.

fields.name: HasEndSurface
fields.doc: HasEndSurface is true if the biome has an end surface.

fields.name: MesaSurface
fields.doc: MesaSurface is optional information to specify the biome's mesa surface.

fields.name: CappedSurface
fields.doc: CappedSurface is optional information to specify the biome's capped surface, i.e. in the Nether.

fields.name: NoiseGradientSurface
fields.doc: NoiseGradientSurface is optional information to specify noise-gradient surface data.

types.name: protocol.BiomeSurfaceMaterial
types.doc: BiomeSurfaceMaterial specifies the materials to use for the surface layers of the biome.

fields.name: TopBlock
fields.doc: TopBlock is the runtime ID of the block to use for the top layer.

fields.name: MidBlock
fields.doc: MidBlock is the runtime ID to use for the middle layers.

fields.name: SeaFloorBlock
fields.doc: SeaFloorBlock is the runtime ID to use for the sea floor.

fields.name: FoundationBlock
fields.doc: FoundationBlock is the runtime ID to use for the foundation layers.

fields.name: SeaBlock
fields.doc: SeaBlock is the runtime ID to use for the sea layers.

fields.name: SeaFloorDepth
fields.doc: SeaFloorDepth is the depth of the sea floor, in blocks.

types.name: protocol.BiomeTemperatureWeight
types.doc: BiomeTemperatureWeight defines the weight for a temperature, used for weighted randomness.

fields.name: Temperature
fields.doc: Temperature is the temperature that can be selected.

fields.name: Weight
fields.doc: Weight is the weight of the temperature, with a higher weight being more likely to be selected.

types.name: protocol.BiomeWeight
types.doc: BiomeWeight defines the weight for a biome, used for weighted randomness.

fields.name: Biome
fields.doc: Biome is the index of the biome name in the string list.

fields.name: Weight
fields.doc: Weight is the weight of the biome, with a higher weight being more likely to be selected.

types.name: protocol.Bitset
types.doc:
Bitset is a representation of std::bitset<size> being sent over the network, allowing for more than 64 bits
to be stored in a single integer. A Bitset has a fixed size, which is set at creation time.

types.name: protocol.BlockChangeEntry
types.doc: BlockChangeEntry is used by the UpdateSubChunkBlocks packet.

fields.name: BlockRuntimeID
fields.doc: BlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc: Flags is a combination of flags that specify the way the block is updated client-side.
