types.name: protocol.RecipeUnlockRequirement
types.doc:
RecipeUnlockRequirement represents a requirement that must be met in order to unlock a recipe. This is used
for both shaped and shapeless recipes.

fields.name: Context
fields.doc: Context is the context in which the recipe is unlocked. This is one of the constants above.

fields.name: Ingredients
fields.doc: Ingredients are the ingredients required to unlock the recipe and only used if Context is set to none.

types.name: protocol.ReleaseItemTransactionData
types.doc:
ReleaseItemTransactionData represents an inventory transaction data object sent when the client releases
the item it was using, for example when stopping while eating or stopping the charging of a bow.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the ReleaseItem inventory transaction. It is one of the action types found
in the constants above, and specifies the way the item was released.
As of 1.13, the ActionType is always 0. This field can be ignored, because releasing food (by consuming
it) or releasing a bow (to shoot an arrow) is essentially the same.

fields.name: HotBarSlot
fields.doc:
HotBarSlot is the hot bar slot that the player was holding while releasing the item. It should be used
to ensure that the hot bar slot and held item are correctly synchronised with the server.

fields.name: HeldItem
fields.doc:
HeldItem is the item that was released. The server should check if this item is actually present in the
HotBarSlot.

fields.name: HeadPosition
fields.doc:
HeadPosition is the position of the player's head at the time of releasing the item. This is used
mainly for purposes such as spawning eating particles at that position.

types.name: protocol.ScoreboardEntry
types.doc:
ScoreboardEntry represents a single entry that may be found on a scoreboard. These entries represent a
line on the scoreboard each.

fields.name: EntryID
fields.doc:
EntryID is a unique identifier of this entry. Each entry that represents a different value should get
its own entry ID. When modifying a scoreboard, entries that represent the same line should have the
same entry ID.

fields.name: ObjectiveName
fields.doc:
ObjectiveName is the name of the objective that this scoreboard entry is for. It must be identical to
the one set in the SetDisplayObjective packet previously sent.

fields.name: Score
fields.doc:
Score is the score that the entry represents. Scoreboard entries are ordered using this score, so in
order to get the scoreboard to be ordered as expected when trying to write non-score related text on
a scoreboard, this score should be incremented for each entry.

fields.name: IdentityType
fields.doc:
IdentityType is the identity type of the scoreboard entry. The entry may represent an entity, player or
a fake player, as the constants above indicate.
In order to write plain text to the scoreboard, ScoreboardIdentityFakePlayer should always be used, in
combination with the DisplayName field. A different identity type will use the name of the entity.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc:
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of either the player or the entity represented by the scoreboard entry.
This field is only used if IdentityType is either ScoreboardIdentityEntity or ScoreboardIdentityPlayer.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.doc:
DisplayName is the custom name of the scoreboard entry. This field is only used if IdentityType is
ScoreboardIdentityFakePlayer. If this identity type is not used, the name of the entity/player will be
shown instead.

types.name: protocol.ScoreboardIdentityEntry
types.doc:
ScoreboardIdentityEntry holds an entry to either associate an identity with one of the entries in a
scoreboard, or to remove associations.

fields.name: EntryID
fields.doc:
EntryID is the unique identifier of the entry that the identity should be associated with, or that
associations should be cleared from.

fields.name: EntityUniqueID
fields.doc: EntityUniqueID is the optional unique ID that the entry should be associated with.

types.name: protocol.ServerJoinInformation
types.doc: ServerJoinInformation contains optional information about the server the player is joining.

fields.name: GatheringJoinInfo
fields.doc: GatheringJoinInfo is optional information about the gathering being joined.

fields.name: StoreEntryPointInfo
fields.doc: StoreEntryPointInfo is optional information about the store entry point.

fields.name: PresenceInfo
fields.doc: PresenceInfo is optional presence information.

types.name: protocol.ShapeData
types.doc:
ShapeData represents an object that holds data specific to a debug shape.
The data it holds depends on the type.

types.name: protocol.ShapedChemistryRecipe
types.doc:
ShapedChemistryRecipe is a recipe specifically made for chemistry related features, which exist only in the
Education Edition. It functions the same as a normal ShapedRecipe.

types.name: protocol.ShapedRecipe
types.doc:
ShapedRecipe is a recipe that has a specific shape that must be used to craft the output of the recipe.
Trying to craft the item in any other shape will not work. The ShapedRecipe is of the same structure as the
ShapedChemistryRecipe.

fields.name: RecipeID
fields.doc:
RecipeID is a unique ID of the recipe. This ID must be unique amongst all other types of recipes too,
but its functionality is not exactly known.

fields.name: Width
fields.doc: Width is the width of the recipe's shape.

fields.name: Height
fields.doc: Height is the height of the recipe's shape.

fields.name: Input
fields.doc:
Input is a list of items that serve as the input of the shapeless recipe. These items are the items
required to craft the output. The amount of input items must be exactly equal to Width * Height.

fields.name: Output
fields.doc: Output is a list of items that are created as a result of crafting the recipe.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc: UUID is a UUID identifying the recipe. Since the CraftingEvent packet no longer exists, this can always be empty.

fields.name: Block
fields.doc:
Block is the block name that is required to craft the output of the recipe. The block is not prefixed
with 'minecraft:', so it will look like 'crafting_table' as an example.

fields.name: Priority
fields.doc: Priority ...

fields.name: AssumeSymmetry
fields.doc:
AssumeSymmetry specifies if the recipe is symmetrical. If this is set to true, the recipe will be
mirrored along the diagonal axis. This means that the recipe will be the same if rotated 180 degrees.

fields.name: RecipeNetworkID
fields.doc:
RecipeNetworkID is a unique ID used to identify the recipe over network. Each recipe must have a unique
network ID. Recommended is to just increment a variable for each unique recipe registered.
This field must never be 0.

types.name: protocol.ShapelessChemistryRecipe
types.doc:
ShapelessChemistryRecipe is a recipe specifically made for chemistry related features, which exist only in
the Education Edition. They function the same as shapeless recipes do.

types.name: protocol.ShapelessRecipe
types.doc:
ShapelessRecipe is a recipe that has no particular shape. Its functionality is shared with the
UserDataShapelessRecipe and ShapelessChemistryRecipe types.

fields.name: RecipeID
fields.doc:
RecipeID is a unique ID of the recipe. This ID must be unique amongst all other types of recipes too,
but its functionality is not exactly known.

fields.name: Input
fields.doc:
Input is a list of items that serve as the input of the shapeless recipe. These items are the items
required to craft the output.

fields.name: Output
fields.doc: Output is a list of items that are created as a result of crafting the recipe.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc: UUID is a UUID identifying the recipe. Since the CraftingEvent packet no longer exists, this can always be empty.

fields.name: Block
fields.doc:
Block is the block name that is required to craft the output of the recipe. The block is not prefixed
with 'minecraft:', so it will look like 'crafting_table' as an example.
The available blocks are:
- crafting_table
- cartography_table
- stonecutter
- furnace
- blast_furnace
- smoker
- campfire

fields.name: Priority
fields.doc: Priority ...

fields.name: RecipeNetworkID
fields.doc:
RecipeNetworkID is a unique ID used to identify the recipe over network. Each recipe must have a unique
network ID. Recommended is to just increment a variable for each unique recipe registered.
This field must never be 0.

types.name: protocol.Skin
types.doc:
Skin represents the skin of a player as sent over network. The skin holds a texture and a model, and
optional animations which may be present when the skin is created using persona or bought from the
marketplace.

fields.name: SkinID
fields.doc:
SkinID is a unique ID produced for the skin, for example 'c18e65aa-7b21-4637-9b63-8ad63622ef01_Alex'
for the default Alex skin.

fields.name: PlayFabID
fields.doc:
PlayFabID is the PlayFab ID produced for the skin. PlayFab is the company that hosts the Marketplace,
skins and other related features from the game. This ID is the ID of the skin used to store the skin
inside of PlayFab.

fields.name: SkinResourcePatch
fields.doc:
SkinResourcePatch is a JSON encoded object holding some fields that point to the geometry that the
skin has.
The JSON object that this holds specifies the way that the geometry of animations and the default skin
of the player are combined.

fields.name: SkinImageWidth
fields.doc:
SkinImageWidth and SkinImageHeight hold the dimensions of the skin image. Note that these are not the
dimensions in bytes, but in pixels.

fields.name: SkinImageHeight
fields.doc:
SkinImageWidth and SkinImageHeight hold the dimensions of the skin image. Note that these are not the
dimensions in bytes, but in pixels.

fields.name: SkinData
fields.doc:
SkinData is a byte slice of SkinImageWidth * SkinImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte
representation of the skin pixels.

fields.name: Animations
fields.doc: Animations is a list of all animations that the skin has.

fields.name: CapeImageWidth
fields.doc:
CapeImageWidth and CapeImageHeight hold the dimensions of the cape image. Note that these are not the
dimensions in bytes, but in pixels.

fields.name: CapeImageHeight
fields.doc:
CapeImageWidth and CapeImageHeight hold the dimensions of the cape image. Note that these are not the
dimensions in bytes, but in pixels.

fields.name: CapeData
fields.doc:
CapeData is a byte slice of 64*32*4 bytes. It is a RGBA ordered byte representation of the cape
colours, much like the SkinData.

fields.name: SkinGeometry
fields.doc:
SkinGeometry is a JSON encoded structure of the geometry data of a skin, containing properties
such as bones, uv, pivot etc.

fields.name: AnimationData
fields.doc: TODO: Find out what value AnimationData holds and when it does hold something.

fields.name: GeometryDataEngineVersion
fields.doc: GeometryDataEngineVersion ...

fields.name: PremiumSkin
fields.doc: PremiumSkin specifies if this is a skin that was purchased from the marketplace.

fields.name: PersonaSkin
fields.doc: PersonaSkin specifies if this is a skin that was created using the in-game skin creator.

fields.name: PersonaCapeOnClassicSkin
fields.doc:
PersonaCapeOnClassicSkin specifies if the skin had a Persona cape (in-game skin creator cape) equipped
on a classic skin.

fields.name: PrimaryUser
fields.doc: PrimaryUser ...

fields.name: CapeID
fields.doc: CapeID is a unique identifier that identifies the cape. It usually holds a UUID in it.

fields.name: FullID
fields.doc:
FullID is an ID that represents the skin in full. The actual functionality is unknown: The client
does not seem to send a value for this.

fields.name: ArmSize
fields.doc: ArmSize is the size of the arms of the player's model. This is one of the ArmSize constants above.

fields.name: PersonaPieces
fields.doc: PersonaPieces is a list of all persona pieces that the skin is composed of.

fields.name: PieceTintColours
fields.doc:
PieceTintColours is a list of specific tint colours for (some of) the persona pieces found in the list
above.

fields.name: Trusted
fields.doc:
Trusted specifies if the skin is 'trusted'. No code should rely on this field, as any proxy or client
can easily change it.

fields.name: OverrideAppearance
fields.doc:
OverrideAppearance specifies if the skin should override the player's skin that is equipped client-side.
When false, the client will reject the skin and continue to use the skin that the player has equipped.

types.name: protocol.SkinAnimation
types.doc:
SkinAnimation represents an animation that may be added to a skin. The client plays the animation itself,
without the server having to do so.
The rate at which these animations play appears to be decided by the client.

fields.name: ImageWidth
fields.doc:
ImageWidth and ImageHeight hold the dimensions of the animation image. Note that these are not the
dimensions in bytes, but in pixels.

fields.name: ImageHeight
fields.doc:
ImageWidth and ImageHeight hold the dimensions of the animation image. Note that these are not the
dimensions in bytes, but in pixels.

fields.name: ImageData
fields.doc:
ImageData is a byte slice of ImageWidth * ImageHeight bytes. It is an RGBA ordered byte representation
of the animation image pixels. The ImageData contains FrameCount images in it, which each represent one
stage of the animation. The actual part of the skin that this field holds depends on the AnimationType,
where SkinAnimationHead holds only the head and its hat, whereas the other animations hold the entire
body of the skin.

fields.name: AnimationType
fields.doc:
AnimationType is the type of the animation, which is one of the types found above. The data that
ImageData contains depends on this type.

fields.name: FrameCount
fields.doc:
FrameCount is the amount of frames that the skin animation holds. The number of frames here is the
amount of images that may be found in the ImageData field.

fields.name: ExpressionType
fields.doc: ExpressionType is the type of expression made by the skin, which is one the types found above.

fields.name: MessageCount

types.name: protocol.SmithingTransformRecipe
types.doc:
SmithingTransformRecipe is a recipe specifically used for smithing tables. It has three input items and adds them
together, resulting in a new item.

fields.name: RecipeNetworkID
fields.doc:
RecipeNetworkID is a unique ID used to identify the recipe over network. Each recipe must have a unique
network ID. Recommended is to just increment a variable for each unique recipe registered.
This field must never be 0.

fields.name: RecipeID
fields.doc:
RecipeID is a unique ID of the recipe. This ID must be unique amongst all other types of recipes too,
but its functionality is not exactly known.

fields.name: Template
fields.doc: Template is the item that is used to shape the Base item based on the Addition being applied.

fields.name: Base
fields.doc: Base is the item that the Addition is being applied to in the smithing table.

fields.name: Addition
fields.doc: Addition is the item that is being added to the Base item to result in a modified item.

fields.name: Result
fields.doc: Result is the resulting item from the two items being added together.

fields.name: Block
fields.doc:
Block is the block name that is required to create the output of the recipe. The block is not prefixed with
'minecraft:', so it will look like 'smithing_table' as an example.

types.name: protocol.SmithingTrimRecipe
types.doc: SmithingTrimRecipe is a recipe specifically used for applying armour trims to an armour piece inside a smithing table.

fields.name: RecipeNetworkID
fields.doc:
RecipeNetworkID is a unique ID used to identify the recipe over network. Each recipe must have a unique
network ID. Recommended is to just increment a variable for each unique recipe registered.
This field must never be 0.

fields.name: RecipeID
fields.doc:
RecipeID is a unique ID of the recipe. This ID must be unique amongst all other types of recipes too,
but its functionality is not exactly known.

fields.name: Template
fields.doc: Template is the item that is used to shape the Base item based on the Addition being applied.

fields.name: Base
fields.doc: Base is the item that the Addition is being applied to in the smithing table.

fields.name: Addition
fields.doc: Addition is the item that is being added to the Base item to result in a modified item.

fields.name: Block
fields.doc:
Block is the block name that is required to create the output of the recipe. The block is not prefixed with
'minecraft:', so it will look like 'smithing_table' as an example.

types.name: protocol.SneakCloseToSculkSensorEvent
types.doc: SneakCloseToSculkSensorEvent is an event sent by the server when a player sneaks close to a sculk sensor.

types.name: protocol.SoundDataUpdate
types.doc: SoundDataUpdate is a single change to a sound that is currently playing.

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is the type of the update. It is one of the SoundDataUpdate constants above.

fields.name: Volume
fields.doc: Volume is used if Type is SoundDataUpdateSetVolume.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc: Pitch is used if Type is SoundDataUpdateSetPitch.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Duration is the fade duration in seconds. It is used if Type is SoundDataUpdateFade.

fields.name: TargetVolume
fields.doc: TargetVolume is the fade target volume. It is used if Type is SoundDataUpdateFade.

fields.name: Seconds
fields.doc: Seconds is the position to seek to. It is used if Type is SoundDataUpdateSeekTo.

types.name: protocol.SphereShape
types.doc: SphereShape represents a circle or sphere debug shape.

fields.name: Segments
fields.doc: Segments is the segments that used for the debug circle or sphere.

types.name: protocol.StackRequestAction
types.doc:
StackRequestAction represents a single action related to the inventory present in an ItemStackRequest.
The action is one of the concrete types below, each of which are indicative of a different action by the
client, such as moving an item around the inventory or placing a block. It is an alias of Marshaler.

types.name: protocol.StackRequestItem
types.doc:
StackRequestItem is the descriptor-backed item format used by deprecated craft-result stack request actions.
Unlike ordinary item stacks, it identifies the item by name instead of a numeric network ID.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.doc: Identifier is the namespaced item identifier, such as minecraft:stone.

fields.name: MetadataValue
fields.doc: MetadataValue is the metadata value or damage value of the item.

fields.name: BlockRuntimeID
fields.doc: BlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block represented by the item, if any.

fields.name: Count
fields.doc: Count is the number of items in the stack.

fields.name: NBTData
fields.doc: NBTData is the item's compound tag.

fields.name: CanBePlacedOn
fields.doc: CanBePlacedOn contains the block identifiers this item may be placed on.

fields.name: CanBreak
fields.doc: CanBreak contains the block identifiers this item may break.

fields.name: BlockingTick
fields.doc: BlockingTick is the tick at which a shield started blocking.

types.name: protocol.StackRequestSlotInfo
types.doc: StackRequestSlotInfo holds information on a specific slot client-side.

fields.name: Container
fields.doc: Container is the FullContainerName that describes the container that the slot is in.

fields.name: Slot
fields.doc: Slot is the index of the slot within the container with the ContainerID above.

fields.name: StackNetworkID
fields.doc:
StackNetworkID is the unique stack ID that the client assumes to be present in this slot. The server
must check if these IDs match. If they do not match, servers should reject the stack request that the
action holding this info was in.

types.name: protocol.StackResourcePack
types.doc:
StackResourcePack represents a resource pack sent on the stack of the client. When sent, the client will
apply them in the order of the stack sent.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc:
UUID is the UUID of the resource pack. Each resource pack downloaded must have a different UUID in
order for the client to be able to handle them properly.

fields.name: Version
fields.doc:
Version is the version of the resource pack. The client will cache resource packs sent by the server as
long as they carry the same version. Sending a resource pack with a different version than previously
will force the client to re-download it.

fields.name: SubPackName
fields.doc: SubPackName ...

types.name: protocol.StackResponseContainerInfo
types.doc: StackResponseContainerInfo holds information on what slots in a container have what item stack in them.

fields.name: Container
fields.doc:
Container is the FullContainerName that describes the container that the slots that follow are in. For
the main inventory, the ContainerID seems to be 0x1b. Fur the cursor, this value seems to be 0x3a. For
the crafting grid, this value seems to be 0x0d.

fields.name: SlotInfo
fields.doc: SlotInfo holds information on what item stack should be present in specific slots in the container.

types.name: protocol.StackResponseSlotInfo
types.doc: StackResponseSlotInfo holds information on what item stack should be present in a specific slot.

fields.name: Slot
fields.doc:
Slot and HotbarSlot seem to be the same value every time: The slot that was actually changed. I'm not
sure if these slots ever differ.

fields.name: HotbarSlot
fields.doc:
Slot and HotbarSlot seem to be the same value every time: The slot that was actually changed. I'm not
sure if these slots ever differ.

fields.name: Count
fields.doc:
Count is the total count of the item stack. This count will be shown client-side after the response is
sent to the client.

fields.name: StackNetworkID
fields.doc: StackNetworkID is the network ID of the new stack at a specific slot.

fields.name: CustomName
fields.doc: CustomName is the custom name of the item stack. It is used in relation to text filtering.

fields.name: FilteredCustomName
fields.doc:
FilteredCustomName is a filtered version of CustomName with all the profanity removed. The client will
use this over CustomName if present and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

fields.name: DurabilityCorrection
fields.doc:
DurabilityCorrection is the current durability of the item stack. This durability will be shown
client-side after the response is sent to the client.

types.name: protocol.StoreEntryPointInfo
types.doc: StoreEntryPointInfo contains information about the store entry point.

fields.name: StoreID
fields.doc: StoreID is the store identifier.

fields.name: StoreName
fields.doc: StoreName is the store name.

types.name: protocol.StriderRiddenInLavaInOverworldEvent
types.doc: StriderRiddenInLavaInOverworldEvent is an event sent by the server when a strider is ridden in lava in the overworld.

types.name: protocol.StructureSettings
types.doc:
StructureSettings is a struct holding settings of a structure block. Its fields may be changed using the
in-game UI on the client-side.

fields.name: PaletteName
fields.doc:
PaletteName is the name of the palette used in the structure. Currently, it seems that this field is
always 'default'.

fields.name: IgnoreEntities
fields.doc:
IgnoreEntities specifies if the structure should ignore entities or include them. If set to false,
entities will also show up in the exported structure.

fields.name: IgnoreBlocks
fields.doc:
IgnoreBlocks specifies if the structure should ignore blocks or include them. If set to false, blocks
will show up in the exported structure.

fields.name: AllowNonTickingChunks
fields.doc:
AllowNonTickingChunks specifies if the structure should allow non-ticking chunks. If set to false, the structure
will export non-ticking chunks.

fields.name: Size
fields.doc:
Size is the size of the area that is about to be exported. The area exported will start at the
Position + Offset, and will extend as far as Size specifies.

fields.name: Offset
fields.doc:
Offset is the offset position that was set in the structure block. The area exported is offset by this
position.

fields.name: LastEditingPlayerUniqueID
fields.doc:
LastEditingPlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the player that last edited the structure block that
these settings concern.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.doc:
Rotation is the rotation that the structure block should obtain. See the constants above for available
options.

fields.name: Mirror
fields.doc:
Mirror specifies the way the structure should be mirrored. It is either no mirror at all, mirror on the
x/z axis or both.

fields.name: AnimationMode
fields.doc: AnimationMode ...

fields.name: AnimationDuration
fields.doc: AnimationDuration ...

fields.name: Integrity
fields.doc:
Integrity is usually 1, but may be set to a number between 0 and 1 to omit blocks randomly, using
the Seed that follows.

fields.name: Seed
fields.doc:
Seed is the seed used to omit blocks if Integrity is not equal to one. If the Seed is 0, a random
seed is selected to omit blocks.

fields.name: Pivot
fields.doc: Pivot is the pivot around which the structure may be rotated.

types.name: protocol.SubChunkEntry
types.doc:
SubChunkEntry contains the data of a sub-chunk entry relative to a center sub chunk position, used for the sub-chunk
requesting system introduced in v1.18.10.

fields.name: Offset
fields.doc: Offset contains the offset between the sub-chunk position and the center position.

fields.name: Result
fields.doc: Result is always one of the constants defined in the SubChunkResult constants.

fields.name: RawPayload
fields.doc: RawPayload contains the serialized sub-chunk data, if present.

fields.name: HeightMapType
fields.doc: HeightMapType is always one of the constants defined in the HeightMapData constants.

fields.name: HeightMapData
fields.doc: HeightMapData is the data for the height map, if present.

fields.name: RenderHeightMapType
fields.doc: RenderHeightMapType is always one of the constants defined in the HeightMapData constants.

fields.name: RenderHeightMapData
fields.doc: RenderHeightMapData is the data for the render height map, if present.

fields.name: BlobHash
fields.doc: BlobHash is the hash of the blob, if present.

types.name: protocol.SubChunkOffset
types.doc: SubChunkOffset represents an offset from the base position of another sub chunk.

types.name: protocol.SubChunkPos
types.doc:
SubChunkPos is the position of a sub-chunk. The X and Z coordinates are the coordinates of the chunk, and the Y
coordinate is the absolute sub-chunk index.

types.name: protocol.SwapStackRequestAction
types.doc:
SwapStackRequestAction is sent by the client to swap the item in its cursor with an item present in another
container. The two item stacks swap places.

fields.name: Source
fields.doc:
Source and Destination point to the source slot from which Count of the item stack were taken and the
destination slot to which this item was moved.

fields.name: Destination
fields.doc:
Source and Destination point to the source slot from which Count of the item stack were taken and the
destination slot to which this item was moved.

types.name: protocol.SyncWorldClockStateData
types.doc: SyncWorldClockStateData represents the state data for synchronising a world clock.

fields.name: ClockID
fields.doc: ClockID is the unique identifier for the clock.

fields.name: Time
fields.doc: Time is the current time of the clock.

fields.name: Paused
fields.doc: Paused indicates if the clock is paused.

types.name: protocol.SystemCategory
types.doc: SystemCategory maps a diagnostics category name to a system index.

types.name: protocol.SystemDiagnosticTimingInfo
types.doc: SystemDiagnosticTimingInfo represents diagnostics for a specific system index.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.doc: DisplayName is the name to display for this timing entry.

fields.name: SystemIndex
fields.doc: SystemIndex is the index of the system that is being timed.

fields.name: DurationNanos
fields.doc: DurationNanos is whole long the timing entry has lasted, in nanoseconds.

fields.name: PercentOfTotal
fields.doc: PercentOfTotal is the percentage of time that this timing entry has used compared to others.

types.name: protocol.TakeStackRequestAction
types.doc:
TakeStackRequestAction is sent by the client to the server to take x amount of items from one slot in a
container to the cursor.

types.name: protocol.TargetBlockHitEvent
types.doc: TargetBlockHitEvent is an event used when a target block is hit by a arrow.

fields.name: RedstoneLevel
fields.doc: RedstoneLevel ...

types.name: protocol.TeleportData
types.doc: TeleportData holds the additional information accompanying a MovePlayer teleport.

fields.name: TeleportCause
fields.doc: TeleportCause specifies why the teleport occurred. See the TeleportCause constants in the packet package.

fields.name: TeleportSourceEntityType
fields.doc: TeleportSourceEntityType is the entity type that caused the teleportation, for example an ender pearl.

types.name: protocol.TextShape
types.doc: TextShape represents a text debug shape.

fields.name: Text
fields.doc: Text is the text of the debug text shape.

fields.name: UseRotation
fields.doc:
UseRotation is if the text should use the provided rotation, meaning it will be static and does not follow the
camera. Use false for default behaviour.

fields.name: BackgroundColour
fields.doc: BackgroundColour is the RGBA colour to use for the text background. This is a translucent black colour by default.

fields.name: LineGapHeight
fields.doc:
LineGapHeight is the gap to leave between each line of multiline text. If not set, the client uses its
default gap.

fields.name: DepthTest
fields.doc: DepthTest is whether the text should show through walls. Use true for default behaviour.

fields.name: ShowBackface
fields.doc:
ShowBackface is if the background should render on the back side of the shape. This only has a visible effect when
UseRotation is true since you cannot see the back side of the text otherwise. Use true for default behaviour.

fields.name: ShowBackfaceText
fields.doc:
ShowBackfaceText is if the text should render on the back side of the shape. This only has a visible effect when
UseRotation is true since you cannot see the back side of the text otherwise. Use true for default behaviour.

types.name: protocol.TexturePackInfo
types.doc:
TexturePackInfo represents a texture pack's info sent over network. It holds information about the
texture pack such as its name, description and version.

fields.name: UUID
fields.doc:
UUID is the UUID of the texture pack. Each texture pack downloaded must have a different UUID in
order for the client to be able to handle them properly.

fields.name: Version
fields.doc:
Version is the version of the texture pack. The client will cache texture packs sent by the server as
long as they carry the same version. Sending a texture pack with a different version than previously
will force the client to re-download it.

fields.name: Size
fields.doc:
Size is the total size in bytes that the texture pack occupies. This is the size of the compressed
archive (zip) of the texture pack.

fields.name: ContentKey
fields.doc:
ContentKey is the key used to decrypt the behaviour pack if it is encrypted. This is generally the case
for marketplace texture packs.

fields.name: SubPackName
fields.doc: SubPackName ...

fields.name: ContentIdentity
fields.doc:
ContentIdentity is another UUID for the resource pack, and is generally set for marketplace texture
packs. It is also required for client-side validations when the resource pack is encrypted.

fields.name: HasScripts
fields.doc:
HasScripts specifies if the texture packs has any scripts in it. A client will only download the
behaviour pack if it supports scripts, which, up to 1.11, only includes Windows 10.

fields.name: AddonPack
fields.doc: AddonPack specifies if the texture pack is from an addon.

fields.name: RTXEnabled
fields.doc: RTXEnabled specifies if the texture pack uses the raytracing technology introduced in 1.16.200.

fields.name: DownloadURL
fields.doc:
DownloadURL is a URL that the client can use to download the pack instead of the server sending it in
chunks, which it will continue to do if this field is left empty.

types.name: protocol.TimeMarkerData
types.doc: TimeMarkerData represents a time marker within a world clock.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the unique identifier for the time marker.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the name of the time marker.

fields.name: Time
fields.doc: Time is the time at which the marker is set.

fields.name: Period
fields.doc: Period is the optional period for the time marker.

types.name: protocol.TrimMaterial
types.doc: TrimMaterial represents a material that can be used when applying an armour trim.

fields.name: MaterialID
fields.doc: MaterialID is the identifier of the material, for example 'netherite'.

fields.name: Colour
fields.doc: Colour is the colour code used for text formatting, for example '§j'.

fields.name: ItemName
fields.doc: ItemName is the identifier of the item that represents the material, for example, 'minecraft:netherite_ingot'.

types.name: protocol.TrimPattern
types.doc: TrimPattern represents a pattern that can be applied to an armour piece in combination with a TrimMaterial.

fields.name: ItemName
fields.doc:
ItemName is the identifier of the item that represents the pattern, for example
'minecraft:wayfinder_armor_trim_smithing_template'.

fields.name: PatternID
fields.doc: PatternID is the identifier of the pattern, for example, 'wayfinder'.

types.name: protocol.UseItemOnEntityTransactionData
types.doc:
UseItemOnEntityTransactionData represents an inventory transaction data object sent when the client uses
an item on an entity.

fields.name: TargetEntityRuntimeID
fields.doc:
TargetEntityRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID of the target that was clicked. It is the runtime ID
that was assigned to it in the AddEntity packet.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the UseItemOnEntity inventory transaction. It is one of the action types
found in the constants above, and specifies the way the player interacted with the entity.

fields.name: HotBarSlot
fields.doc:
HotBarSlot is the hot bar slot that the player was holding while clicking the entity. It should be used
to ensure that the hot bar slot and held item are correctly synchronised with the server.

fields.name: HeldItem
fields.doc:
HeldItem is the item that was held to interact with the entity. The server should check if this item
is actually present in the HotBarSlot.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the position of the player at the time of clicking the entity.

fields.name: ClickedPosition
fields.doc:
ClickedPosition is the position that was clicked relative to the entity's base coordinate. It can be
used to find out exactly where a player clicked the entity.

types.name: protocol.UseItemTransactionData
types.doc:
UseItemTransactionData represents an inventory transaction data object sent when the client uses an item on
a block.

fields.name: LegacyRequestID
fields.doc:
LegacyRequestID is an ID that is only non-zero at times when sent by the client. The server should
always send 0 for this. When this field is not 0, the LegacySetItemSlots slice below will have values
in it.
LegacyRequestID ties in with the ItemStackResponse packet. If this field is non-0, the server should
respond with an ItemStackResponse packet. Some inventory actions such as dropping an item out of the
hotbar are still one using this packet, and the ItemStackResponse packet needs to tie in with it.

fields.name: LegacySetItemSlots
fields.doc:
LegacySetItemSlots are only present if the LegacyRequestID is non-zero. These item slots inform the
server of the slots that were changed during the inventory transaction, and the server should send
back an ItemStackResponse packet with these slots present in it. (Or false with no slots, if rejected.)

fields.name: Actions
fields.doc:
Actions is a list of actions that took place, that form the inventory transaction together. Each of
these actions hold one slot in which one item was changed to another. In general, the combination of
all of these actions results in a balanced inventory transaction. This should be checked to ensure that
no items are cheated into the inventory.

fields.name: ActionType
fields.doc:
ActionType is the type of the UseItem inventory transaction. It is one of the action types found above,
and specifies the way the player interacted with the block.

fields.name: TriggerType
fields.doc:
TriggerType is the type of the trigger that caused the inventory transaction. It is one of the trigger
types found in the constants above. If TriggerType is TriggerTypePlayerInput, the transaction is from
the initial input of the player. If it is TriggerTypeSimulationTick, the transaction is from a simulation
tick when the player is holding down the input.

fields.name: BlockPosition
fields.doc:
BlockPosition is the position of the block that was interacted with. This is only really a correct
block position if ActionType is not UseItemActionClickAir.

fields.name: BlockFace
fields.doc:
BlockFace is the face of the block that was interacted with. When clicking the block, it is the face
clicked. When breaking the block, it is the face that was last being hit until the block broke.

fields.name: HotBarSlot
fields.doc:
HotBarSlot is the hot bar slot that the player was holding while clicking the block. It should be used
to ensure that the hot bar slot and held item are correctly synchronised with the server.

fields.name: Hand
fields.doc:
Hand is the hand that the player used to interact with the block. It is one of the HandSlot constants
above.

fields.name: HeldItem
fields.doc:
HeldItem is the item that was held to interact with the block. The server should check if this item
is actually present in the HotBarSlot.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc:
Position is the position of the player at the time of interaction. For clicking a block, this is the
position at that time, whereas for breaking the block it is the position at the time of breaking.

fields.name: ClickedPosition
fields.doc:
ClickedPosition is the position that was clicked relative to the block's base coordinate. It can be
used to find out exactly where a player clicked the block.

fields.name: BlockRuntimeID
fields.doc:
BlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block that was clicked. It may be used by the server to verify
that the player's world client-side is synchronised with the server's.

fields.name: ClientPrediction
fields.doc:
ClientPrediction is the client's prediction on the output of the transaction. It is one of the client
prediction found in the constants above.

fields.name: ClientCooldownState
fields.doc:
ClientCooldownState is the client's cooldown state for the item used. It is one of the
ClientCooldownState constants above.

types.name: protocol.UserDataShapelessRecipe
types.doc:
UserDataShapelessRecipe is a shapeless recipe for crafting items that must retain their user data, such
as their contents or colour, when crafted. Vanilla uses these recipes for dyeing shulker boxes, bundles
and harnesses.

types.name: protocol.VoxelCells
types.doc: VoxelCells represents a 3D grid of voxel cell data.

fields.name: XSize
fields.doc: XSize is the size of the grid along the X axis.

fields.name: YSize
fields.doc: YSize is the size of the grid along the Y axis.

fields.name: ZSize
fields.doc: ZSize is the size of the grid along the Z axis.

fields.name: Storage
fields.doc: Storage is the raw cell data stored in the grid.

types.name: protocol.VoxelShape
types.doc: VoxelShape represents a voxel shape with cells and coordinate axes.

fields.name: Cells
fields.doc: Cells is the grid of cells representing solid and empty regions.

fields.name: XCoordinates
fields.doc: XCoordinates is a list of X axis coordinates for the shape.

fields.name: YCoordinates
fields.doc: YCoordinates is a list of Y axis coordinates for the shape.

fields.name: ZCoordinates
fields.doc: ZCoordinates is a list of Z axis coordinates for the shape.

types.name: protocol.VoxelShapeNameEntry
types.doc: VoxelShapeNameEntry represents a name-to-ID mapping entry for voxel shapes.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the name of the voxel shape.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the numeric ID of the voxel shape.

types.name: protocol.WaxedOrUnwaxedCopperEvent
types.doc: WaxedOrUnwaxedCopperEvent is an event sent by the server when a copper block is waxed or unwaxed.

types.name: protocol.Waypoint
types.doc: Waypoint holds optional data for a locator bar waypoint.

fields.name: UpdateFlag
fields.doc: UpdateFlag is a bitmask indicating which optional fields are set.

fields.name: Visible
fields.doc: Visible determines whether the waypoint is shown.

fields.name: WorldPosition
fields.doc: WorldPosition is the position and dimension of the waypoint.

fields.name: TexturePath
fields.doc: TexturePath is the resource path for the waypoint icon texture.

fields.name: IconSize
fields.doc: IconSize is the size of the waypoint icon.

fields.name: Colour
fields.doc: Colour is the RGB colour used to tint the waypoint icon.

fields.name: ClientPositionAuthority
fields.doc: ClientPositionAuthority determines whether the client has authority over the waypoint position.

fields.name: ActorUniqueID
fields.doc: ActorUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity the waypoint tracks.

types.name: protocol.WaypointWorldPosition
types.doc: WaypointWorldPosition holds a position and dimension for a waypoint.

fields.name: Position
fields.doc: Position is the world position of the waypoint.

fields.name: DimensionID
fields.doc: DimensionID is the dimension the waypoint is in.

types.name: protocol.WhiskerScopeDataSummary
types.doc: WhiskerScopeDataSummary represents a whisker profiler scope diagnostic summary.

fields.name: Label
fields.doc: Label is the label of the whisker scope.

fields.name: Indentation
fields.doc: Indentation is the indentation string of the whisker scope within the profiler hierarchy.

fields.name: TotalHighCostNS
fields.doc: TotalHighCostNS is the total time, in nanoseconds, spent in the high-cost portion of the scope.

fields.name: TotalMidCostNS
fields.doc: TotalMidCostNS is the total time, in nanoseconds, spent in the mid-cost portion of the scope.

fields.name: TotalLowCostNS
fields.doc: TotalLowCostNS is the total time, in nanoseconds, spent in the low-cost portion of the scope.

types.name: protocol.WorldClockData
types.doc: WorldClockData represents a complete world clock with its time markers.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the unique identifier for the clock.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the name of the clock.

fields.name: Time
fields.doc: Time is the current time of the clock.

fields.name: Paused
fields.doc: Paused indicates if the clock is paused.

fields.name: TimeMarkers
fields.doc: TimeMarkers is a list of time markers for this clock.

types.name: protocol.transferStackRequestAction
types.doc:
transferStackRequestAction is the structure shared by StackRequestActions that transfer items from one
slot into another.

fields.name: Count
fields.doc: Count is the count of the item in the source slot that was taken towards the destination slot.

fields.name: Source
fields.doc:
Source and Destination point to the source slot from which Count of the item stack were taken and the
destination slot to which this item was moved.

fields.name: Destination
fields.doc:
Source and Destination point to the source slot from which Count of the item stack were taken and the
destination slot to which this item was moved.

functions.name: protocol.CommandOriginData
functions.doc: CommandOriginData reads/writes a CommandOrigin x using IO r.

functions.name: protocol.InputFlagList
functions.doc:
InputFlagList reads/writes an InputFlags holding flags in the range [0, size) as a list of the IDs of the
flags that are set. Flag IDs must be unique and within range.

functions.name: protocol.PlayerMoveSettings
functions.doc: PlayerMoveSettings reads/writes PlayerMovementSettings x to/from IO r.

functions.name: protocol.Skin.validate
functions.doc:
validate checks the skin and makes sure every one of its values are correct. It checks the image dimensions
and makes sure they match the image size of the skin, cape and the skin's animations.

args.value: expected size of skin is %vx%v (%v bytes total), but got %v bytes
expected size of cape is %vx%v (%v bytes total), but got %v bytes
expected size of animation %v is %vx%v (%v bytes total), but got %v bytes

functions.name: protocol.StackReqSlotInfo
functions.doc: StackReqSlotInfo reads/writes a StackRequestSlotInfo x using IO r.

functions.name: protocol.StackRequestItemDescriptorCount
functions.doc: StackRequestItemDescriptorCount reads/writes the Cereal item descriptor format used by auto-craft actions.

reason.value: must equal width multiplied by height

functions.name: protocol.personaPieceTintLoginType
functions.doc: personaPieceTintLoginType converts v2168 wire names back to the persona_* names used in login data.

functions.name: protocol.personaPieceTintWireType
functions.doc:
personaPieceTintWireType converts the persona_* names used in login data to the shorter names used by the

functions.name: protocol.stackRequestActionVariant
functions.doc:
stackRequestActionVariant maps an action type to its index in the variant list the action is sent under.
The list leaves out the two container actions that are never sent, so the two run out of step above them.

consts.name: protocol.ParamOptionCollapseEnum
consts.doc:
ParamOptionCollapseEnum specifies if the enum (only if the Type is actually an enum type. If not,
setting this to true has no effect) should be collapsed. This means that the options of the enum are
never shown in the actual usage of the command, but only as auto-completion, like it automatically does
with enums that have a big amount of options. To illustrate, it can make
<false|true|yes|no> <$Name: bool>.
